- **Who is affected:** on a shared cell under pressure, a project whose queue (or stream) traffic is more than 1/k of the cell's: its queue requests are now refused too; its neighbours are unaffected by this change (their spared sends are #191/#192).
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/queue_overload.rs::over_the_shed_line_the_queue_project_over_its_share_is_refused_before_its_neighbour (k = 8, line 1,000, RSS 1,001; project 0 sent 120 messages under the line: its five sends, a claim, the queue's stats and the listing get 429 `project_memory_pressure`, `retry-after: 2`, 8 blamed refusals counted; project 1's five sends are 201; under the line both are served; `queuedMessages` 121 and 6 exactly) and ::at_the_inflight_cap_the_queue_project_over_its_share_is_refused_before_its_neighbour (cap 8 held: 429 `rate_limited`, `retry-after: 1`, 8 counted as in-flight blame, none as RSS; counts 121 and 5). Red before: `assertion failed: round 0 left: (201, None, None) right: (429, Some("project_memory_pressure"), Some("2"))` and `... right: (429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("1"))`.
- **Risk reason:** medium: a queue-heavy project's queue requests gain refusals they never had under pressure; the answers and the blame rule are #184/#185's. Reversal: drop `overload::judge` and the blamed refusal from `product::queues`.
- **Status:** ratified as drafted by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #191 (this record's commit) — Over the RSS shed line a queue send or settle is refused 429 `rate_limited` before its body is read, as an append is, and a spared project's pass until the instance is an eighth over the line

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 1, overload parity (DESIGN-6A §4.1; research-queues §3.1 row "RSS write shed", rules 2-3 of §3.2): under memory pressure the cell shed stream writes and never queue writes.
- **Surface:** product.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /v1/queues/{name}/messages`, `messages:batch` and `groups/default:settle`. Owners: `product::queues::overload` (`rss_shed`, `writes_like_append`), `application::append::memory_gate` and `AdmissionController::admit_write_memory` (the append's gate and its fair-shed exception, #183/#184), `product::append_error::render_product_append_error` (the append's wire answer). Not affected: claims, the other queue verbs (`:pause`, `:resume`, `:redrive`, `:discard`, `:cancel`, `:republish`), creates, PATCH, deletes and reads.
- **Condition:** sampled RSS plus the absorber's reserved bytes over `ADMIT_RSS_SHED_MB` (500 MiB on the 1 GiB profiles). On a cell shared k > 1 ways a request #189 spares passes until the pressure is over the line x 9/8.
- **Before:** queue sends and settles were served over the line, whatever the pressure.
- **After:** they are refused 429 `rate_limited` (`"instance memory pressure; retry"`), `Retry-After: 2`, after the gate's 25 ms tarpit, before the body is buffered (the body read and dropped, so an uploading client reads the 429 on its connection), counted `admit_shed_rss`; a spared project's pass up to the line x 9/8, as its appends do. Under the line nothing changes.
- **Retry semantics:** retryable after 2 s; nothing was written. A refused settle leaves its leases as they were: they expire and redeliver as a settle that never arrived would. Option for the owner (research-queues §3.2 rule 3): spare settles that only end leases up to the hard line, since refusing acks causes redelivery; this record follows the task's "like appends".
- **Who is affected:** queue producers and consumers on an instance over its memory line; their neighbours' appends, which no longer carry the whole shed alone.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/queue_overload.rs::over_the_shed_line_queue_sends_and_settles_are_shed_before_their_bodies (k = 1, line 500, RSS 501: a send, a batch and a settle each 429 `rate_limited`, `retry-after: 2`; a head declaring 4 MiB with no body sent reads the 429; a claim 200 and the stats served; under the line a send 201; `queuedMessages` 2 exactly) and ::over_the_shed_line_the_queue_project_over_its_share_is_refused_before_its_neighbour (k = 8: the spared neighbour's send 201 inside line x 9/8, 429 `rate_limited` `retry-after: 2` past it). Red before: `assertion failed: /v1/queues/jobs/messages left: (201, None, None) right: (429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("2"))` and `assertion failed: past it left: (201, None, None) right: (429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("2"))`.
- **Risk reason:** medium: queue writes gain a refusal under memory pressure, and a refused settle can mean a redelivery; the answer and its line are the append's. Reversal: drop `rss_shed` from `overload::body`.
- **Status:** ratified with option (b) by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1); amended below.
- **Amendment (#191 option (b), the lead's ruling of 2026-10-27 under the owner's delegation; its own commit):** a settle that only ends leases (every op an ack, release, retry, fail or discard: no message bytes) is not refused by the RSS shed before its body; it is refused only past the hard line (the line x 9/8; 562 MiB at 500), 429 `rate_limited`, `Retry-After: 2`, after the 25 ms tarpit, counted `admit_shed_rss` (`AdmissionController::admit_lease_ending_write`). A settle with any `extend` op is judged once its body is read under the append's rule (refused over the line unless its project is spared, `overload::extend_shed`). The in-flight write gate (#192) still binds every settle. Before: every settle was refused over the line unless spared. Reason: a refused settle turns each of its leases into a redelivery and more claims, which feeds the overload; settles drain it. Pins: src/dst/tests/queue_overload.rs::over_the_shed_line_a_settle_that_ends_leases_passes_until_the_hard_line (line 500, RSS 501: an ack and a release served `ok`, an extend 429 `rate_limited` `retry-after: 2`; at 563 an ack refused the same; under the line served; acked 2, queued 1), red before: `assertion failed: an ack left: ((429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("2")), None) right: ((200, None, None), Some("ok"))`; src/admission/line_tests.rs::a_lease_ending_write_passes_the_rss_gate_until_the_hard_line (1,125 passes, 1,126 refused and counted, no line passes); the send leg is ::over_the_shed_line_queue_sends_are_shed_before_their_bodies.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #192 (this record's commit) — At the in-flight write cap a queue send or settle is refused 429 `rate_limited` once its body is buffered, as an append is, and a spared project's pass until the active requests are a quarter over the cap

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 1, overload parity (DESIGN-6A §4.1; research-queues §3.1 row "in-flight write gate", rule 2 of §3.2).
- **Surface:** product.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /v1/queues/{name}/messages`, `messages:batch` and `groups/default:settle`. Owners: `product::queues::overload::inflight_refused`, `AdmissionController::admit_write_inflight` (with #185's spared exception), the append's rendering. Not affected: claims (a parked claim leaves the active count, #194), the other verbs, reads.
- **Condition:** `ADMIT_MAX_INFLIGHT` = cap > 0 (512 on the beta profiles) and the active requests (in flight minus parked) over it; on a cell shared k > 1 ways a spared request passes until they are over cap x 5/4.
- **Before:** queue sends and settles were served at the cap.
- **After:** refused 429 `rate_limited` (`"instance at admission capacity; retry"`), `Retry-After: 1`, after a 25 ms tarpit, counted `admit_shed_inflight`, once the body is buffered (where an append meets the gate); a spared project's pass up to cap x 5/4. Below the cap nothing changes.
- **Retry semantics:** retryable after 1 s; nothing was written (a refused settle leaves its leases to expire, as #191 says).
- **Who is affected:** queue producers and consumers of an instance at its cap; the appends that shared the slots.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/queue_overload.rs::at_the_inflight_cap_queue_sends_and_settles_are_refused_as_appends_are (k = 1, cap 8 held: a send, a batch and a settle 429 `rate_limited` `retry-after: 1`, 3 counted as the gate's; a claim 200; under the cap a send 201; `queuedMessages` 2) and ::at_the_inflight_cap_the_queue_project_over_its_share_is_refused_before_its_neighbour (k = 8: the spared neighbour's send 201 at 10 active, 429 `rate_limited` at 11). Red before: `assertion failed: /v1/queues/jobs/messages left: (201, None, None) right: (429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("1"))` and `assertion failed: past it left: (201, None, None) right: (429, Some("rate_limited"), Some("1"))`.
- **Risk reason:** medium: queue writes gain a refusal at the cap; the answer is the append's. Reversal: drop `inflight_refused`.
- **Status:** ratified as drafted by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #196 (this record's commit) — On a shared cell a project's ceilings are its weights' share of each bound: the policy feed's `request_weight` and `byte_weight` scale bound / k on the request axes and the byte rates

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 1, weighted per-project shares (DESIGN-6A §4.2, F15; the model of `~/.streams-k2/analysis/layout6a/pkg1/FABLE-WEIGHTS.md`, Fable 5.1, 2026-10-26): at k = 8 every project's ceiling was bound / 8, which refused ~79% of profile M's and ~86% of profile L's writes (`docs/STREAMS-COST-LEVERS-2026-10.md`), so medium and large tenants could not share a cell.
- **Surface:** product (the effective quotas every route enforces) and the policy-feed contract.
- **Endpoint:** the policy feed (`contracts/streams-platform/v1/project-policies.schema.json`: two new optional quota fields, `request_weight` and `byte_weight`, integers >= 0); every route a project's quotas bound. Owner: `auth::ceiling::CellCeiling::effective` (and `weight`, `clamps`). Not affected: dedicated cells (k = 1), which ignore weights; a policy without weights (weight 1, today's quotas to the unit).
- **Condition:** `PROJECT_SHARE_K` = k > 1 and a policy setting a weight w > 1.
- **Before:** the feed refused an unknown quota field (`deny_unknown_fields`), so no weight existed; every project's ceiling on a bounded axis was max(1, bound / k).
- **After:** the ceiling is max(1, ⌊bound x w / k⌋): w = `request_weight` on `requests_per_sec`, `max_inflight_requests`, `max_live_subscriptions`, `max_streams`; w = `byte_weight` on `append_bytes_per_sec`, `read_bytes_per_sec`; `queued_append_bytes` stays bound / k whatever the weights (a committer burst buffer: 64 MiB is 50 s of M's rate, and five eighths of 512 MiB would pass the shard's 256 MiB unabsorbed line). A value the feed sets below the ceiling stands, a 0 takes it, as before. Each weight is held to 1..k-1 (0 is 1; above k - 1 is held to k - 1 and warned in the log), so the unit-weight projects always keep at least 1/k of every bound; the published quotas carry the held weights. At k = 8 over the shared-cell profile's bounds, M = (2, 5) gets 352 req/s, 128 in flight, 300 live places, 16,384 streams, 1,287,500 B/s appended, 18,750,000 B/s read; L = (1, 7) gets 1,802,500 B/s appended.
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged (the same 429 `project_rate_limit` and quota refusals, at the weighted ceilings).
- **Who is affected:** projects the feed gives weights (more capacity); their neighbours, whose own ceilings are unchanged but who share the cell's envelope with a heavier tenant; the admission tool (cell-admin) and the interim issuer, which publish weight 1 explicitly until cell-admin's packing (#199).
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/weighted_shares.rs::a_weighted_project_appends_at_its_weighted_ceiling_beside_a_unit_project (k = 8, append envelope 2,060,000 B/s: M (2, 5)'s ten 120,000-byte appends all 200, the unit project's third 429 `project_rate_limit`, stored 10 and 2). Red before: `assertion failed: M's 1.2 MB second left: [(200, None), (200, None), (429, Some("project_rate_limit")), ... x8] right: [(200, None); 10]`. src/auth/ceiling.rs::tests::weights_scale_a_projects_share_of_each_bound (every axis at (2, 5); below the share stands; 0 and 1 are the unit; (9, max) held to 7, `clamps` true only above k - 1; k = 1 ignores weights). deploy/cell-admin/cell-admin.test.ts (the bundle carries both weights at 1 and is schema-valid; `--quota byte_weight=5` refused), deploy/issuer/projects.test.ts (the issuer's projects at weight 1).
- **Risk reason:** medium: a weighted project can take up to (k - 1)/k of a bound; the packing rule that keeps several heavy projects off one cell is the admission tool's (#199). Reversal: drop the two fields from the contract and `effective`.
- **Status:** ratified as drafted by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #197 (this record's commit) — Fair shedding judges a project against its request weight's share of the cell, w/k, so a weighted project is blamed only past its weighted share and spared within it

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 1, weighted per-project shares (DESIGN-6A §4.2; FABLE-WEIGHTS.md decision 4): with #196's weights a heavy tenant entitled to w/k of the cell's requests would still have been blamed as soon as it passed 1/k (#184/#185), refusing the very tenant the weights admit.
- **Surface:** product (and the queue routes, #189).
- **Endpoint:** every route #184/#185/#189 refuse for a blamed project and every append (and queue send or settle) they spare. Owners: `admission::fair_shed` (`Weighted`, `over_share`, `judge`, `InstanceLoad::count`/`judge` now take the request weight; the cell's heaviest load is kept per unit of weight), `QuotaRegistry::admit_counted` (counts at the admitted quotas' weight), `ParkShare::judge` (judges at it).
- **Condition:** `PROJECT_SHARE_K` = k > 1, over the RSS shed line or at the in-flight cap, and a project whose policy sets a `request_weight` w > 1 (published held to 1..k-1, #196).
- **Before:** blamed when its recent requests x k exceeded the cell's, whatever its weight; spared when the heaviest raw count was over 1/k.
- **After:** blamed when its recent requests x k exceed the cell's x w; spared when it is not and the heaviest project per unit of its own weight is over its share; even otherwise. Weight 1 (every project without a weight) judges exactly as before. Byte loads are not judged (bytes are unknown where the request is counted, at admission; a byte-heavy tenant is bounded by its weighted byte ceilings, its memory line and the RSS gate).
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged.
- **Who is affected:** weighted projects on a shared cell under pressure (now spared within their weighted share), and unit projects beside them (blamed against the cell's total as before; a weighted project's load no longer counts as "the heaviest" until it passes its own share).
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/weighted_shares.rs::over_the_shed_line_blame_follows_the_weighted_share (k = 8; project 0 at request weight 4 sent 100 of 250 appends, project 1 at weight 1 sent 150; over the line project 0's five appends are 200 and project 1's 429 `project_memory_pressure`, 5 blamed refusals; stored 105 and 150). Red before: `assertion failed: weighted, round 0 left: (429, Some("project_memory_pressure")) right: (200, None)`. src/admission/fair_shed/tests.rs (`over_share` at w/k, weight 0 as 1, no overflow at u64::MAX; `judge` with a weighted own and heaviest; `the_heaviest_load_is_the_heaviest_per_unit_of_weight`); the unweighted #184/#185 DSTs unchanged and green.
- **Risk reason:** medium: who is refused under pressure changes for weighted projects. Reversal: judge every project at weight 1.
- **Status:** ratified as drafted by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #198 (this record's commit) — A project's memory line is the cell's line times its byte weight, held so two unit projects' lines still fit beside it in the instance's read memory, for its write latch, its buffered bodies and its read reservations

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 1, weighted shares (DESIGN-6A §4.2, F15; FABLE-WEIGHTS.md decision 5): profile M's pulls held the 32 MiB project line (`bench/k2cost/README.md` SCR-M: 429 `project_memory_pressure`), so a byte-heavy tenant admitted by #196's weights would still be refused by memory; an uncapped weighted line (5 x 32 = 160 MiB) would let one project fill the 125 MiB instance read memory alone.
- **Surface:** product (and the queue routes).
- **Endpoint:** every write the project latch refuses (`product::project_memory_gate`), every body charged under the line (`admission::body::buffer_within` via `product::read_memory::body` and `product::queues::overload::body`), every read reservation (`product::read_memory::reserve`, `park::try_reserve_read`, `park::reserve_read`) and every woken wait's re-reservation (`ReadHold::resume_with`, at its hold's weight, read when it wakes). The multiplexed wait (`POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait`, #200) takes the same line for its buffered body (`admit_live_wait`), its answer's reservation (`reserve_live_answer`) and its group walks' (`park::reserve_read_until`). Owner: `AdmissionController::project_memory_line`. The catalog's page reservation takes the weight of the share its admission bound (`park::byte_weight`), since it shares the project's one read ledger.
- **Condition:** `PROJECT_MEMORY_PRESSURE_BYTES` = line > 0 and a project whose published `byte_weight` w > 1 (#196; held to 1..k-1).
- **Before:** every project's line was `PROJECT_MEMORY_PRESSURE_BYTES`.
- **After:** the project's line is min(line x w, max(line, read memory - 2 x line - 1 B)), the read memory being a quarter of `ADMIT_RSS_SHED_MB` (125 MiB at 500 MiB: M = (2, 5) gets 61 MiB less a byte against the unit 32 MiB), so with one weighted project the read memory still takes at least four projects at their lines to fill, the owner's acceptance (README "Shared cells Q1" (A)) (FABLE-WEIGHTS.md proposed read memory / 2; one 62.5 MiB line and two unit lines would fill 125 MiB with three projects); a second weighted line would break it, which the admission tool's packing refuses (#199); unbounded by the read memory when it has no budget; exactly the cell's line at weight 1. The release point stays `PROJECT_MEMORY_RELEASE_PCT` of the project's line.
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged.
- **Who is affected:** byte-weighted projects (more headroom before 429 `project_memory_pressure`); their neighbours, who now share the instance read memory with one project that may hold almost half of it, two unit lines always fitting beside it.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/weighted_shares.rs::a_weighted_projects_memory_line_scales_leaving_two_unit_lines_beside_it (line 32 MiB, read memory 125 MiB; 40 MiB of each project's read bytes held: project 0 at byte weight 5 (line 61 MiB less a byte) appends 200 and its 8 MiB page read is reserved, the unit project 1 gets 429 `project_memory_pressure` on both; 70 MiB held: project 0 refused too, the cap; stored 2 and 1). Red before (and with the weighting disabled as a control): `assertion failed: weighted at 40 MiB left: (429, Some("project_memory_pressure")) right: (200, None)`. src/admission.rs::tests::a_projects_memory_line_scales_with_its_byte_weight_leaving_two_lines_beside_it (weights 0/1/2/5 at 125 MiB: 32, 32, 61 MiB - 1 B; under the cap; never below the line; no read budget; off). The read-memory and woken-wait DSTs (`dst_tests::read_memory::`), which move the line while waits are parked, unchanged and green.
- **Risk reason:** medium: one weighted project may hold almost half the instance read memory. Reversal: return the cell's line from `project_memory_line`.
- **Status:** ratified as drafted by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-27 (README "Owner decisions", layout 6A package 1).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

## Low risk (120)

None of these changes alters a status or code on a path that worked before, and only #92 and #95 add a header to one (`Cache-Control: no-store` on successes that WIRE-MATRIX already listed with it: one for #92, four for #95), except shared cells phase A's #101 and #104, which refuse requests that crossed a trust boundary (a reserved identity's tokens, a watch carrier with only a stream key), as their risk reasons say, and phase B's #141, which extends #104's rule to off and shadow modes (a key beside a capability that does not verify) and answers a spent anonymous lookup budget with a retryable `429` instead of a `403`; #102's amendment and #178 add `Retry-After: 1` to existing retryable `503`s; #114, #116 and #133 change answers on paths that worked (a pull may now wait for memory and be refused retryably or answered empty; a deleted stream's watchers, and since #133 an expired stream's and those returning after ten idle minutes, are answered `stale`), as their records say; #132 lets a boot pass that was refused; #135 changes only a refusal's message text (whitespace); #136 moves one retryable refusal from `429` to `503` with `Retry-After: 1` (an append whose engine closed under it), the answer its neighbours in time already give, retryable before and after; and #137 serves a request that a sweep's close of its engine refused before, leaving the retryable `503` `shard_closing` refusal that any request meets during a retirement, as each route already renders it, only where the engine was retired before the request resumed; #140 changes no answer of the server and spares a shared cell's client the platform edge's retryable wake `404` after an idle spell; and #147 changes no answer of the server either: the SDK's plain appends reject an answer that leaves their outcome unknown (a transport failure, a `408`, a `5xx` other than `503`) with its own error class, code `outcome_unknown` and `retryable: false`, and the SDK never sends one again after that answer, as before; and #148 changes no answer of the server: the SDK sends a request again after a transport failure where the server answers a replay without a second effect, within the attempts the `429`/`503` replay already used, and its consumer and watch loops reconnect where they ended. Most are internal, operator-facing or timing-only; the rest correct data inside successful responses, or turn a failure (or a hang) into a success.

### #178 415a71b2 — A read's `503 temporarily_unavailable`, on both surfaces, and a product append's `503 temporarily_unavailable` that stated no delay carry `Retry-After: 1`, so the SDK's restart ride-through (#177) covers reads

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, field round 3 (FIELD-REPORT.md "Round 3", "Why D4 still fails"; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-19 07:00, decision (1), the lead under the owner's delegation): the lifecycle restart leg on e94a8fd3 failed call 10's bar of 0 SDK errors with 2 of 1,889 calls failed; one was a read refused `503 temporarily_unavailable` on each of its 4 attempts in 3.8 s with no `Retry-After` on any of them, so #177's ride-through, which needs `Retry-After`, never started for it.
- **Surface:** both. Product: `render_product_read_failure` (`src/product.rs`; records GET and long-poll, `:scan`, the consumer pull's read) and `render_product_append_error` (`src/product/append_error.rs`; single append, `records:batch`, a `:seal`'s final record), through `product::answers::retry_unavailable`, which `DescriptorReadAnswer` (#64) now also uses. Raw: `read_failure_response` (`src/http/read.rs`).
- **Endpoint:** `GET /v1/streams/{name}/records` and its long-poll, `POST /v1/streams/{name}:scan`, consumer `:pull`, `POST /v1/streams/{name}/records` and `records:batch`, `:seal`; raw `GET /v1/stream/{name}`.
- **Condition:** product read: the read failed resolving its shard here (`ResolveError::Opening`, a shard still opening or held off after a fence, which is what a restart or deploy shows; `ResolveError::OpenFailed`) or reading a span from its peer (`ReadFailure::Remote`). Product append: a `FailureClass::Unavailable` failure without a delay of its own (a `:seal` whose stream handle its engine could not load, `src/application/append/close.rs`). Raw read: a failed peer read.
- **Before:** `503`, code `temporarily_unavailable`, `retryable: true` (product), with no `Retry-After`. The SDK replayed such a read four times about 1 s apart (its default wait) and then rejected it with `StreamsError`.
- **After:** the same status, code, body and message, plus `Retry-After: 1`. A failure that states its own delay keeps it (a product append's `retry-after` from the raw answer still overwrites the default; the raw read's shard-opening `503` keeps its own code and delay). Nothing else changes: the raw surface's `503 creating` and the product's `503 creating` and `project_tracker_capacity` are unchanged, and the fleet-internal receivers' `503 temporarily_unavailable` (`internal_desc`, the internal segment routes) are unchanged, since no client sees them (a peer read that fails is answered to the client by the rows above).
- **Retry semantics:** clients already told to retry (`retryable: true`) are now told when: one second. The SDK (#177) now keeps replaying such a read for up to 15 s since its first attempt instead of rejecting it after four attempts; a raw client that honours `Retry-After` waits 1 s.
- **Who is affected:** every client reading while a shard opens or a peer read fails: a restart, a deploy, a fence, a shard opened after an idle release. SDK reads that failed after about 3-4 s now ride through a window of up to about 15 s.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - `src/product/answers.rs` `product::answers::tests::a_read_temporarily_unavailable_asks_for_a_retry_after_one_second` (new: `Resolve(Opening)`, `Resolve(OpenFailed)` and `Remote(Transport)` render `503`, `Retry-After: 1`, `temporarily_unavailable`). Red on the unfixed tree: `left: (503, None, "temporarily_unavailable") right: (503, Some("1"), "temporarily_unavailable")`.
  - `product::answers::tests::an_append_temporarily_unavailable_asks_for_a_retry` (new: an `Unavailable` failure with no delay renders `Retry-After: 1`, one with `.retry(5)` keeps `5`). Red: `left: (503, None, "temporarily_unavailable") right: (503, Some("1"), "temporarily_unavailable")`.
  - `src/http/read.rs` `http::read_adapter::tests::a_failed_peer_read_asks_for_a_retry_after_one_second` (new). Red: `left: None right: Some([49])`.
  - unchanged and green: `product::tests::every_append_failure_renders_its_product_row`, the `product::`, `http::` and read DST filters `impact.py` selects (180 tests in the dev profile).
- **Risk reason:** low: a header is added to answers that were already retryable `503`s; no status, code or body changes. The only behavioural effect is that clients which honour `Retry-After`, the SDK among them, wait 1 s and (the SDK) keep waiting up to 15 s. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (the d4 lane's commit, before landing); #178 was the next free number at slate e94a8fd3.

### #180 6ee74d37 — At a stop each HTTP connection finishes the request it is serving, for up to 10 s, instead of being reset at once

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17 (d4-report.md "SIGTERM today, on a fleet-off cell", FENCE-YIELD-DESIGN.md "SIGTERM drain", approved by the lead under the owner's delegation): `serve_connections` dropped the listener and aborted every connection at the stop, so a request in flight at a SIGTERM got a connection reset; an append among them had an unknown outcome.
- **Surface:** both (every HTTP/1.1 connection, `/health` and the operator surfaces included).
- **Endpoint:** every route.
- **Condition:** a stop begins (SIGTERM/SIGINT, after a fleet instance's planned drain; or a critical loop's exit) while a connection is open.
- **Before:** the listener closed and every connection was aborted at once: a request in flight got a reset (no response), whatever it had done.
- **After:** the listener closes and every connection gets hyper's graceful shutdown (`serve_one`, `src/http/serve.rs`): a request in flight is answered and then the connection closes; an idle keep-alive closes at once. `drain` joins them for at most `HttpConfig::stop_drain`, 10 s (a code constant, `http.stop_drain_ms` in the effective-configuration summary; the DST rigs use 0), then resets those still serving (an SSE session, a long-poll, a slow reader) as before. Only then do the supervised loops join and the shards close, so an append in flight at the stop is answered from its engine. All of it stays inside the 30 s stop bound (item 38).
- **Retry semantics:** none new: a request answered during the drain is final; one reset at 10 s is as before (an append's outcome unknown, a read retried). A keep-alive client's next request on the closing connection meets a closed connection, as with any server close.
- **Who is affected:** every client with a request in flight when a server stops (a deploy, a restart): it now gets its answer instead of a reset. Live subscriptions and long-polls end up to 10 s later than before.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - `src/http/serve.rs` `http::serve::tests::a_request_in_flight_at_the_stop_is_answered_before_its_connection_closes` (new: a 2.5 s request in flight at the stop is answered `200` and its connection then closes; the stop waited for it). Red with the drain's bound zero (every connection aborted at the stop, as on the unfixed tree): `assertion left != right failed: closed before the response head completed left: 0 right: 0`; the second test fails there too (the running request reset before the drain).
  - `http::serve::tests::the_stop_closes_idle_connections_at_once_and_resets_the_rest_at_the_drain` (new: at the stop an idle keep-alive closes within 1.5 s, and a request that never answers is reset at the 3 s drain, with nothing aborted by the supervisor).
  - unchanged and green: `a_panicking_handler_is_counted_once_and_an_aborted_connection_is_not` (now reset at the rig's 3 s drain) and the rest of `http::serve::`.
- **Risk reason:** low: no status, code or body changes; a request that was reset is answered instead, and a stop can take up to 10 s longer, inside its 30 s bound. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (the d4 lane's commit, before landing); #180 was the next free number after #179.

### #181 bb1872f6 — `GET /operator/data.json` carries a `boot` section naming the serving boot, the boot it replaced and whether that boot learned of it, so the cell watch's crash-loop rule (RUNBOOK row 4) does not count a deploy or a restart as a crash

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, field round 4, finding 2 (FIELD-REPORT.md): on Compute every deploy or restart runs the outgoing boot beside the new one, so a deploy followed by a restart within 30 min was 3 boot ids in the watch's window and paged as a crash loop (the PAGE opened 08:30:10 at the first restart 6 min after a normal deploy). The first cut (a watch that read the old process's `superseded` 503) could not work in the field: the main domain never routes a poll to the outgoing process (`/health` 200 in 749 of 749 samples across a deploy). The lead asked for the link to come from the server: the new boot names the boot it replaced.
- **Surface:** operator-debug. Fleet-off cells fill it; a cell with a fleet store reports no predecessor.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /operator/data.json` (deployment bearer; 401 otherwise, unchanged). Not on `/health`, `/readyz` or any customer surface.
- **Condition:** every request. The section is `boot: {id, predecessor, predecessorSuperseded}`. `id` is the serving boot's id (the one `x-streams-boot-id` carries). `predecessor` is the boot id `_cell/boot` named when this boot registered (read before its own write), else `null`. `predecessorSuperseded`: `true` once `_cell/superseded` names the predecessor; `false` when it does not 60 s after the registration; `null` before then, or without a predecessor. A boot writes `_cell/superseded` (`{"bootId","atMs"}`, one record, last writer wins, one bounded write) when it learns a newer boot is registered: at its yield (`Supersession::yield_to_newer`), or at its stop if it never lost an engine. A predecessor that went while the record still named it (a crash, an OOM kill, a loop that exits) writes none. The answer is read from the store until decided (one bounded `GET` per request) and kept.
- **Before:** the document had `ts_ms`, `local`, `ops`, `feeds`, `fleet`. A boot wrote only `_cell/boot`, and did not read it first.
- **After:** the same plus `boot`; one more small object, `_cell/superseded`, in the data store (no listing reads it). The cell watch (`deploy/cell-watch/rules.ts`) leaves a boot id out of row 4's 30 min count when its successor reports `predecessorSuperseded: true`, so a deploy and a restart within 30 min notify twice and do not page; a boot change without the link still counts, and 3 of them in 30 min still page. A server without the section (older, or fleet-on) counts every boot id as before.
- **Retry semantics:** none; no client request changes.
- **Who is affected:** the on-call (fewer false crash-loop pages after a deploy plus a restart) and any reader of `/operator/data.json`, which gains one key. No customer-visible change.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - `src/dst/tests/fence_yield.rs` `a_boot_names_the_boot_it_replaced_and_learns_it_was_superseded` (new; A serves, B registers: B's `boot` names A with `predecessorSuperseded: null`, A's has none; after B fences A and A yields, B's `boot` reads `true`; no `/health` header carries it). Red on the tree without the change: `left: Null right: Object {"id": ..., "predecessor": Null, "predecessorSuperseded": Null}`.
  - `an_idle_replaced_boot_marks_itself_at_its_stop` (A holds no shard, B registers, A stops: B reads `true`). Red: `left: Null right: Object {..., "predecessorSuperseded": Bool(true)}`.
  - `a_predecessor_that_went_before_the_next_boot_leaves_no_mark` (A stops while the record names it, B registers: B names A and never reads `true`). Red: `left: Null right: Object {..., "predecessor": String(...), "predecessorSuperseded": Null}`.
  - `src/sharddir/supersede/tests.rs` (new): `the_mark_decides_yes_at_once_and_no_only_after_the_wait`, `a_registering_boot_learns_the_boot_the_record_named`, `a_replaced_boot_marks_itself_and_the_next_boot_keeps_the_answer`, `an_unread_record_leaves_no_mark`.
  - `deploy/cell-watch/rules-cell.test.ts` row 4 (the field sequence: a deploy, then a restart 6 min later, notify twice and never page; five replacements stay below the page; crashes with no mark, an undecided mark, no predecessor, no `boot` section or no operator payload still page at `boot_ids_30m = 3`; a replacement then two crashes pages) and `runbook.test.ts` (row 4 names the fields and the mark).
- **Risk reason:** low: one added key on a bearer-gated operator document and one small object written at a yield or a stop; no customer-facing status, header or body changes. A failed read or write only leaves a replacement unmarked, which the watch counts as it did before. The first-boot read adds one bounded `GET` (2 s at most) in the supersession task, which does not delay the boot. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (the row4 lane's commit, before landing); #181 was the next free number after #180 in this tree.

### #160 3cdc7d1e — The rollup's reads of its own ledgers are internal reads that meter nothing, so under enforce they no longer count `unowned_meter_events_total`

- **Program item:** Public beta, the owner's round-4 decisions of 2026-10-14 (README, "Owner decisions", row "Public-beta calls, round 4 (decided 2026-10-14)"), item 2 (alerting #1, found by the alerting lane's Fable review in round 3: on every enforce-mode cell the counter grew from the cell's own activity, so the lane's alert row 17, `r17_unowned_usage`, opened within the first minute on an idle cell and never resolved). The owner decided (a): fix the server, with a red DST first (idle rollup steps on an enforce rig leave `UNOWNED_METER_EVENTS` and the deployment account's read rows unchanged), then `billing::system_read` reads with `internal = true`, line-neutral in `src/billing.rs`, and an edge record for the change, ratified with that answer ("Agreed on the two questions. Thanks."). Numbered #160 at landing-4 (2026-10-17), in landing order from #160, the next free number at slate 5b639a55.
- **Surface:** operator-debug: the counter `unowned_meter_events_total` of the ops snapshot (`ops::collect_snapshot`), in the record the drain loop appends to `_ops_metrics` and in the snapshot the alert evaluator reads. No status, code, header or body of any request changes, and no usage answer changes.
- **Endpoint:** no route. `billing::system_read` (`src/billing.rs`), the in-process reader of the reserved system streams: the usage rollup's `rollup_step` (`_usage`) and `ops_rollup_step` (`_ops_metrics`), which the rollup loop runs as a pair about every 2 s while both are idle. Its relay hop to the owner (`/v1/internal/segment-read`, `internal_segment_read`) already read with `internal` set and is unchanged.
- **Condition:** an instance with a usage rollup and the system ledger key under `AUTH_MODE=enforce`, on each page `system_read` reads locally (on the instance that owns the ledger's segment). Off and shadow modes never counted an unowned event, so nothing changes there.
- **Before:** each local page went through `render_raw_read`'s metering (`meter_read_outcome`, since `params.internal` was false): `billing::identity_of` looked the system project up in the policy snapshot, which never names it, fell back to the deployment's `ACCOUNT_ID` and, under enforce, counted one `UNOWNED_METER_EVENTS`. An idle enforce instance's counter therefore rose by two every rollup poll, about one a second (about nine per 8 s telemetry tick, as the alerting lane measured it), and RUNBOOK's "unowned usage" signal ("not flat") and row 17 fired on every idle cell. The read row itself was then dropped by the read accumulator (`ReadUsageAccumulator::meter` skips `_`-reserved streams, OBSERVABILITY-BILLING §8.4), so no read row, `_usage` envelope or usage answer counted these reads, in any mode.
- **After:** `system_read`'s local read sets `ReadParams::internal`, as its relay hop already did, so `render_raw_read` meters nothing for it: no `identity_of` call and no unowned event. `unowned_meter_events_total` now rises only for metering events whose project has no owner in the policy snapshot (feed lag or a removal, or a request on the deployment project's raw streams under enforce). The flag's two other effects in the raw read path need request headers `system_read` never sends (`streams-internal-continuation`, `streams-internal-read-page`), so the page, its body and its `stream-next-offset` are as before.
- **Retry semantics:** Not applicable: nothing a client receives changes.
- **Who is affected:** Operators and alert rules that read `unowned_meter_events_total` (RUNBOOK, "What to alert on", row "unowned usage"; `deploy/cell-admin/README.md`, "Watch": "must stay flat"; the alerting lane's row 17): on an idle enforce cell it now stays flat, as those rules assume. No customer: the question as put to the owner said these reads were also added to the deployment `ACCOUNT_ID`'s read usage in every auth mode; at this tree they were not (the accumulator's reserved-stream skip above; the DST below shows the deployment account's read rows unchanged on the tree before the change too), so no usage report changes. The ratified decision covers this change, which is narrower than the one the question described.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting changes.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/billing_operation_counts.rs::idle_rollup_steps_count_no_unowned_meter_event (new: an enforce rig whose rollup has consumed one append's usage from `_usage` and one snapshot from `_ops_metrics`; each idle pair of `rollup_step` and `ops_rollup_step` applies nothing and leaves the deployment account's active read rows and the read window's `unflushed()` exactly as they were, and some pair, taken 10 ms apart up to 50 times because the counter is process-wide, counts exactly no unowned meter event. Red on the tree before the change: `every idle rollup pair counted unowned meter events: [2, 2, …, 2]` (50 pairs), `left: Some(2) right: Some(0)`, with the read-row assertion green. Control: the change reverted and the accumulator's reserved-stream skip removed fails the read-row assertion, the deployment account `acct_test`'s rows for `system`/`_usage` and `system`/`_ops_metrics` going from `read_operations: 2` to `3`, so that assertion is live)
  - unchanged and green (dev profile): the `billing`, `runtime_journals` and `security_audit` filters (135 tests, the new one included) and the `security_workload` and `shared_cell_hostile` filters, which read the system streams through `system_read`
- **Risk reason:** low: no client-visible change; an operator counter stops counting the server's own reads, which no usage row ever counted. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the release profile, the suite, the `billing` mutation leg (CI runs it; the change adds no mutant), Miri and any field run; no formal receipt is staled. Ratified 2026-10-14 by the owner's round-4 decision, item 2 (README, "Owner decisions", row "Public-beta calls, round 4 (decided 2026-10-14)").
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #161 e11f45c9 — A long-poll its stream's split wakes and refreshes onto the published child waits there only what its first wait left, so no long-poll waits more than 25 s in all

- **Program item:** Public beta, the owner's round-3 answers of 2026-10-13 ("accept all recommended.", `OWNER-DECISIONS-3-2026-10-13.md`), call 11 (research key deploy-q5-3, the 60 s first-byte deadline of the platform edge): option (c) with the skeptic's four amendments. The certification design's probe of that deadline (§3.5 item 5) is dropped, and its premise, that no long-poll holds its first byte anywhere near 60 s, is made true by construction: a long-poll refreshed across a split keeps its first wait's budget, on the SDK's subscribe and on the raw surface, built in `wait_tail` with no path, call or line added inside `execute_read`'s frozen exception scopes. The edgeprobe `deadline` mode and its FACT lines stay (the platform's real deadline is still unmeasured; the design's §6 (5) question to Compute stays open). Numbered #161 at landing-4 (2026-10-17), in landing order from #160, the next free number at slate 5b639a55.
- **Surface:** both: the product long-poll (`GET /v1/streams/{name}/records:long-poll`, `waitMs`; the SDK's `subscribe` sends `waitMs=25000`) and the raw long-poll (`GET /v1/stream/{name}?live=long-poll`, `timeout`, at most `MAX_LONG_POLL`, 25 s).
- **Endpoint:**
  - Those two routes, through `ReadService::execute_read` (`src/application/read_request.rs`): its one long-poll wait at the live tail (`wait_tail`, through `wait_tail_measuring`) and the one refresh after it (`refreshed_read`), which both surfaces request (`refresh: true`).
  - Code: `wait_tail` takes the read's wait as `&mut Duration` and `wait_tail_measuring` writes back what its deadline (`min(wait, 25 s)` from when it parked) had left when it ended; `execute_read`'s one call site reads `&mut command.mode`, so the refreshed read carries the remainder in its mode.
  - Not changed: the two refreshes before any wait (a cursor the descriptor cannot place; a live last span found closed), which have not waited and keep the whole wait; fork long-polls, which never refresh (`wait_fork_tail` keeps its own budget); consumer pulls, watch waits and SSE.
- **Condition:** a long-poll parked at the live tail of a span that its stream's split seals while it waits, when the split publishes its child before the woken read's refresh reads the registry. This is a race: the seal wakes the poll, and the refresh usually lands in the seal gap (no child yet), so it answers `204` at once with a resume cursor (`reads_raw::seal_gap_long_poll_wakes_without_closure`); only when the publication wins does the refreshed read step past the drained parent and wait on the child.
- **Before:** the refreshed read waited a fresh `min(wait, 25 s)` on the child. In the worst case a long-poll waited 25 + 25 s, plus the refresh's registry read and shard resolves (up to `open_wait_ms`, 10 s, for each cold one), before its `204`: past the 25 s cap that WIRE-MATRIX §1 (`timeout`) and 2.9/2.10 ("server cap 25 s") document, and up to about 60 s with cold resolves.
- **After:** the refreshed read waits on the child only what the first wait's deadline had left when the seal woke it: the two waits take at most `min(wait, 25 s)` together, so no long-poll waits more than 25 s in all. Its first byte comes after at most 25 s of waiting plus the refresh's own registry read and resolves, which the budget does not count. With nothing appended to the child by then, the answer is the `204` it was before, earlier: `Stream-Next-Offset` (raw) or `Prisma-Next-Cursor` (product) at the child's first position, without `Up-To-Date` on a segmented stream. A record appended to the child while it waits is served as before.
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged. A `204` is answered as before, and the client long-polls again from its cursor (the SDK re-polls a `204` at once).
- **Who is affected:** long-poll clients of a stream that the scaler or an operator splits, only in the race above: their answer comes by their first wait's deadline instead of up to a second whole wait later. A client that sized its timeout to the 25 s cap no longer meets a 50 s answer, and a long-poll no longer approaches an edge's 60 s first-byte deadline through a refresh (if the edge answered `504` at its deadline, the SDK would not retry it and `subscribe()` would throw). A parked slot is held at most 25 s across a split, not up to 50 s.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting changes.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/read_application.rs::a_raw_long_poll_refreshed_across_a_split_waits_one_budget and ::a_product_long_poll_refreshed_across_a_split_waits_one_budget (new, one per surface: a 2 s long-poll at the tail of an HTTP rig's stream, whose read service's topology holds each read that asks it to help a transition until the test lets it go, so the split publishes its child before the woken poll's refresh reads the registry; the split starts 1 s into the wait. The poll answers `204` with no record, its waits on the parent and on the child take at least 2 s and less than 2.75 s together, and a record appended next is served from its cursor. Red on the tree without the change: "it waited 1.008457208s on the parent and 2.002439792s on the child" (raw) and "1.007124208s ... 2.00291175s" (product); measured green: 2.002-2.004 s in all. A control that leaves nothing of the wait (`*wait = Duration::ZERO`) fails both legs at the lower bound, the child's wait 1-2 ms.)
  - src/dst/tests/read_application.rs::a_product_long_poll_over_the_cap_refreshed_across_a_split_waits_25_s (new, added on review: the product route does not clamp `waitMs`, so the 2 s legs, whose wait is below the cap, cannot tell the capped deadline's remainder from what the request's own wait left; this leg is the same scenario on the product surface with `waitMs=60000`, the split 12.5 s in, and asserts the two waits take at least 25 s and less than 25.75 s. A control that writes back what the request's uncapped wait had left (`*wait = (*wait).saturating_sub(started.elapsed())`, `started` taken where the deadline is set) passes the 2 s legs and fails this one: "it waited 12.504467417s on the parent and 25.005871875s on the child". Green with the `read_application` filter, 13 tests, in 29 s.)
  - unchanged and green (dev profile): the `read_application`, `reads_applied`, `reads_applied_history`, `read_memory`, `read_memory_wakes`, `reads_raw`, `reads_product`, `parked_waits`, `read_page_limits` and `reads_history` filters (74 tests, the two new ones included), and `livefeed_swap`, `topology_lifecycle`, `fork_lifecycle`, `seal_coordination`, `consumer_product`, `request_topology_debt`, `application::` and `http::read_adapter` (123).
- **Risk reason:** low: timing only, on a race: the same `204` and cursor, by the first wait's deadline instead of a second whole wait later; no status, code, header or body changes, and nothing is written. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the release profile, the suite, the `read_request` and `http_read` mutation legs (CI runs them; the driver's list command gives 210 for `read_request` before and after, and the 24 mutants `--in-diff` selects in the changed functions are existing ones), Miri and any field run. The TLA-018 receipt, which digests `src/application/read_request.rs`, is staled and is re-recorded at landing. Ratified 2026-10-13 by the owner's round-3 answer, call 11.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #155 0d1d51eb — The pre-auth survival refusal says `"retryable": true`, so a plain SDK append replays it, as it replays every other refusal that wrote nothing

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), built as the SDK triage's item B4 (SDK-E2; Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12, `sdk.md` and its triage, with the review's correction C10, under which a plain append reads a `503` whose JSON names no `retryable` as an unknown outcome, #154). The triage's D4 had it ride with the next commit that edits `src/http.rs`, to spare the `http` mutation owner's 256 mutants; the lead decided on 2026-10-13 to build it alone, because a push runs only the mutants in its diff (`scripts/quality/mutation_driver.py`, `--in-diff`): one for this edit (`track_inflight` replaced by `Default::default()`), as measured with the pinned cargo-mutants 27.1.0. X2 (sdk O2) was decided by the owner on 2026-10-12 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-2-2026-10-12.md`): the public-beta records are ratified at landing and numbered from #141 in landing order. Ratified at landing under X2; numbered #155 at landing.
- **Surface:** both, raw and product (the middleware answers before any route), and the SDK's plain appends, which read the field.
- **Endpoint:**
  - Every path that starts with `/v1/stream` (the raw `/v1/stream/...` and the product `/v1/streams...`; WIRE-MATRIX §0), whatever the method, before authentication.
  - Code: the body literal of `track_inflight` (`src/http.rs`), on the same line.
  - Not changed: the status, the code `overloaded`, the message `retry`, `retry-after: 1`, `content-type: application/json`, the origin marker and `nosniff`; the post-authentication admission refusals; every other route.
- **Condition:** more active requests than four times `admit_max_inflight` (default 512, so above 2,048; #79, #106) on a path that starts with `/v1/stream`.
- **Before:** `503`, `retry-after: 1`, body `{"error":{"code":"overloaded","message":"retry"}}` (#79). The SDK replayed it for every request (a `503` without the field defaulted retryable), except, since #154 (the previous commit), a plain append (`append`, `appendBytes`, `appendMany`), which read it as an unknown outcome and rejected at once with `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`the append's last attempt ended in HTTP 503 overloaded, ...`), sent once.
- **After:** the same status and headers, body `{"error":{"code":"overloaded","message":"retry","retryable":true}}`. A plain SDK append replays it on its `Retry-After` within its four attempts, the same request, as every other SDK request already did.
- **Retry semantics:** the refusal was retryable and still is; the body now says so. It is answered before any route, so nothing was written and a replay stores the record once. At the landing push an SDK plain append treats this answer as it did before #154 (replayed); only the commit between rejected it, as an unknown outcome (safe, not precise).
- **Who is affected:** raw HTTP clients that parse `retryable` (now `true` where the field was absent), and SDK plain-append callers on an instance above four times its admission cap (replayed instead of `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`, which only #154 had introduced). Clients that read only the status or the code see no change.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/security_routes.rs::the_survival_refusal_is_marked_as_this_servers_answer and ::the_survival_refusal_covers_reads_and_the_product_surface_at_the_default_caps (edited; #79's pin of the six paths): the exact new body with `503`, `retry-after: 1`, `application/json`, the origin marker and `nosniff`, for the raw `POST` and `GET /v1/stream/any`, a raw long-poll, `GET /v1/streams`, and the product `GET` and `POST /v1/streams/any/records`. Red on the unfixed tree: `left: (503, "{\"error\":{\"code\":\"overloaded\",\"message\":\"retry\"}}")`, `right: (503, "{\"error\":{\"code\":\"overloaded\",\"message\":\"retry\",\"retryable\":true}}")`, and the second test at `POST /v1/stream/any` with the same two bodies.
  - sdk/scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs (mocked `fetch`), new for each of `append`, `appendBytes` and `appendMany` (3): the refusal's new body is replayed, the same URL and body, and the replay succeeds. Green before and after (the SDK does not change). Control (hand-applied, reverted, `cmp`-checked): the same three rows with the old body fail at `Error [AppendOutcomeUnknownError]: the append's last attempt ended in HTTP 503 overloaded, ...`. The row "a 503 whose JSON body names no retryable" keeps the old body, as a JSON body without the field.
- **Risk reason:** low: one additive body field on a refusal that was already retryable and wrote nothing; no status, code, message or header changes. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the release profile, the suite, the `http` owner's in-diff mutant that CI selects, CI's `sdk-package` smokes through a real server and the platform e2e. No formal receipt is staled (`formal_batch.py cost src/http.rs`: 0 of 25).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the triage's B4 spec, with one departure: D4's riding dependency is dropped by the lead's decision of 2026-10-13 (its cost premise assumed a push runs all 256 of the `http` owner's mutants). The spec's WIRE-MATRIX `:272` is §4's plain-append bullet, which B6 had made name the old body's shape; §0 (`:12`) quotes the body. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #156 19c525fc — The policy feed carries a project's `max_stored_bytes`, a 0 or absent value takes the cell's `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT` at any k, and `cell-admin` and the issuer publish the shared-cell profile's 10 GiB explicitly; nothing is refused on it yet

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, and the lead's consequence that a per-project stored-bytes cap is needed before strangers write), built as the stored-cap triage's item B2 (Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12, `stored-cap.md` with its review and skeptic passes, and `stored-cap.TRIAGE.md`, disputes D4, D7, D8 and D9), under the owner's answers of 2026-10-12 to the public-beta calls: S1 (stored-cap Q1 (a), a 10 GiB default), X3 (MULTITENANCY r9 carries the field; the schema stays v1, additive; the binary first, then bundles) and X2 (stored-cap's records, "the setting" among them, ratified at landing). Ratified at landing under X2; numbered #156 at landing. The refusal on the quota (429 `stored_bytes_limit`), project usage's `ownedStoredBytesNow` and the operator report's `rollup.stored` are the same lane's items B3 and B4, under records of their own.
- **Surface:** process (the setting `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT`) and the platform contract (the policy feed's `quotas.max_stored_bytes`, MULTITENANCY r9). The interim issuer's management API (#151) shows the new member in a project's `quotas`. No answer of the server's HTTP surface changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - The policy feed (`STREAMS_AUTH_POLICY_FILE`, materialized from the bundle `cell-admin` and the issuer publish): `quotas.max_stored_bytes`, an integer of at least 0, the ninth and last member, optional (`contracts/streams-platform/v1/project-policies.schema.json`). The golden vectors: `project-policies.valid.json` now sets it (1 GiB); `project-policies.hostile-negative-stored.json` (-1) is refused by the schema and by the cell. Parsed into `ProjectQuotas.max_stored_bytes` (`src/project_policy.rs`).
  - `CellCeiling::effective` (`src/auth/ceiling.rs`), which `CellCeiling::apply` runs on every policy when `AuthService` publishes a snapshot, so every reader of a published policy holds the resolved value. Boot installs the default through `CellCeiling::of_config` (`with_stored_default`); `bootstrap::run` is byte-identical.
  - The setting `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT` (`src/config/cli.rs`, u64, default 0). `deploy/profiles/shared-cell.env` sets `10737418240`.
  - `deploy/cell-admin`: `QUOTA_FIELDS` gains `max_stored_bytes` (last; not a bounded field); `cellSizing` reads `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT` into `CellSizing.stored_default`; `checkSizing` answers the sizing; `admittedQuotas(state, given, storedDefault)` writes it. Its callers: `admit`, `init`'s canary (`placeCanary`) and the issuer's project create (`deploy/issuer/projects.ts`, from its compiled profile). `quota` sets any positive value. The issuer's `GET /v1/workspaces/{w}/streams/projects`, `GET …/projects/{p}` and a create's 201 show the project's `quotas` with the member.
- **Condition:** Every policy snapshot a cell publishes. The default applies on a cell whose `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT` is above 0 (the shared-cell profile) to every policy whose `max_stored_bytes` is 0 or absent.
- **Before:** The feed had no such field. `ProjectQuotas` refuses unknown keys (shared-cells R3), so a snapshot carrying `max_stored_bytes` was refused whole: the cell kept its previous snapshot, which aged toward `503 policy_stale`. Nothing bounded the bytes a project stores. `cell-admin` and the issuer published eight quota fields.
- **After:**
  - A snapshot carrying `max_stored_bytes` parses. A negative or non-integer value refuses the whole snapshot, as any malformed quota does. Absent is 0.
  - The effective value is the feed's when it is above 0, else `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT`, at any k. The field has no shared bound: it is never divided by k, and a feed value above the default stands. The setting's default, 0, leaves a dedicated cell, and any cell that does not set it, exactly as before (0, no limit): "0 or absent takes `PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT`, whose default 0 is unlimited" (triage D4).
  - The shared-cell profile sets 10 GiB (10,737,418,240 bytes). `cell-admin init` and `admit`, and the issuer's create (which answers 409 `beta_at_capacity`), refuse a profile without a positive value ("profile does not set PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT", "profile PROJECT_STORED_BYTES_DEFAULT=0 is not a positive integer").
  - They publish every project's value explicitly: the profile's default, unless `--quota max_stored_bytes=N` (any positive N; this field has no ceiling) sets one. `--quota max_stored_bytes=0` is refused: "--quota max_stored_bytes=0: omit the field to take the cell default". The canary carries the default too.
  - Nothing reads the resolved value yet: no request is refused on it, and no answer of the server changes. Its check is the lane's item B4: 429 `stored_bytes_limit` at append admission, against the stored figure the usage rollup publishes (item B3).
- **Retry semantics:** None changes.
- **Who is affected:**
  - Feed producers. A cell binary before this change refuses a whole feed carrying the field, so the binary goes first, then bundles that carry it; `cell-admin` and the issuer ship with or after it. There are no live cells.
  - Issuer clients see one more member in a project's `quotas`.
  - Shared-cell projects are given 10 GiB, which nothing enforces until item B4.
- **Given up:** Nothing. The default is a new value, not a change to an old one.
- **Deployment comparison:**
  - One new setting, default 0 (no change).
  - The shared-cell profile sets it, which changes the layered profile's digest: a cell initialised from the previous profile would refuse `admit` until it is initialised again. No such cell exists, and the owner chose no migrations.
  - The effective-configuration tool declares `cli.project_stored_bytes_default` as added under this record (137 -> 138 leaves).
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/auth_feed.rs::tests::a_policy_feed_carries_max_stored_bytes and ::golden_policy_vectors_parse_as_the_schema_judges_them. Red on the unfixed tree: "unknown field `max_stored_bytes`, expected one of `requests_per_sec`, …".
  - src/auth/ceiling.rs::tests::a_cell_gives_an_absent_stored_quota_its_default (k = 8 and k = 1: a 10 GiB default gives 0 → 10 GiB, and leaves 1 GiB and 20 GiB as fed; no default leaves 0) and ::boot_installs_the_ceiling_of_the_configured_cell (the setting is read at boot; a server without it keeps 0).
  - src/config/tests.rs::cli_surface_is_pinned; src/config/validation_tests.rs::the_shared_cell_profile_validates_under_the_release_posture (the profile's 10 GiB).
  - deploy/cell-admin/profile.test.ts: the profile's sizing carries the default; a profile without it, or with 0, is refused; "every name it sets is one the server reads"; the quota fields in the contract's order.
  - deploy/cell-admin/cell-admin.test.ts: init's canary and `admit` publish the default; `=0` is refused and publishes nothing; a value above the default is published, and the snapshot is valid against the schema. owner.test.ts: `quota` raises it past the default. deploy/issuer/projects.test.ts: a create's `quotas`.
  - deploy/cell-admin/e2e.test.ts (CI, against the release binary; run here against the dev binary, 2 pass): the real server boots on the shared-cell profile from a bundle whose every policy carries the field, and serves its tokens.
  - Controls (hand-applied, reverted): the default applied only at k > 1 (the design's E9) fails `a_cell_gives_an_absent_stored_quota_its_default`; boot ignoring the setting fails `boot_installs_the_ceiling_of_the_configured_cell`; `admittedQuotas` not writing the default fails 9 cell-admin and issuer tests.
- **Risk reason:** low: no request is refused on the new value and no server answer changes. A feed that was refused whole now parses, and dedicated cells keep 0. The default it installs becomes a refusal only with item B4, whose record carries that risk.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the stored-cap triage's B2 spec. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #157 b454d923, amended by 49e3a78d — The rollup report's `stored` member states the stored figures admission holds: how many projects, their bytes stored now and written as the drain saw them, when the rollup last published them, and the ten projects that wrote the most

- **Program item:** Public beta, built as the stored-cap triage's item B3 (Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12, `stored-cap.md` §4 with its review and skeptic passes, and `stored-cap.TRIAGE.md` B3, disputes D3 and D5, section 2 points 1, 2 and 4), under the owner's answer X2 of 2026-10-12 (stored-cap's records, `rollup.stored` named among them, ratified at landing). Ratified at landing under X2; numbered #157 at landing. The refusal that reads the figures (429 `stored_bytes_limit`) and project usage's `ownedStoredBytesNow` are the lane's item B4, under a record of its own; until it lands nothing is refused on them.
- **Surface:** operator-debug
- **Endpoint:** `GET /operator/billing.json` (bearer-gated; the 401 path is unchanged): the `rollup` member on an instance whose rollup is installed (`ROLLUP=1`). No product, raw or fleet-internal route changes, and no other member of the report.
- **Condition:** Every answer while the rollup is installed.
- **Before:** `rollup` had eight members (#93). The rollup kept no per-project figure of stored bytes: a project's stored bytes were readable only stream by stream (`ownedStoredBytesNow` on `GET /v1/streams/{name}/usage`), and the account-keyed `segment/` rows hold a segment twice after a workspace change re-stamps its account.
- **After:**
  - `rollup` gains `stored`. It is `null` until the rollup has published into admission's stored table, then `{"projects","totalBytes","writtenBytes","asOfMs","largest":[{"project","storedBytes","writtenBytes"}]}`: how many projects the table holds, the sum of their stored bytes now and of their written bytes, when the rollup last published (wall-clock ms), and the ten projects that wrote the most, largest first, ties by project id. `open_rollup` publishes as it installs the rollup, so a production rollup instance never shows `null`; an instance installed some other way shows it until its first page. The eight members keep their names and values; serde_json sorts members, so `stored` comes last.
  - The figures are the rollup's stored index (`src/rollup/stored_index.rs`), new rows in the rollup database (`telemetry/usage-rollup/v2/p0`, additive): `stored-seg/{project}/{stream_id}/{segment}` (the snapshot the index counts) and `stored/{project}` (`bytes`, `written`), written in each ledger page's one `WriteBatch` beside the segment rows. A project's `bytes` is the sum of its live segments' latest gauges (the unit of `ownedStoredBytesNow`: stored page bytes after compression, headers included), each segment counted once by (project, stream, segment) whatever account stamped it, by its latest snapshot (a greater usage version, or the same version accounted through a later instant, the segment state's own rule). `written` adds each increase of a segment's gauge among the snapshots the rollup applies, in that same order from the snapshot the index held, however the ledger's pages cut them (a rollup behind its ledger reads several drain rounds of a segment in one page), and a close never lowers it. A drain round emits a segment as it then stands, so bytes stored and freed between two rounds of its shard (8 s apart by default) never reach it: after deletes it bounds the bytes the project left in the bucket that a drain round saw, not every byte it wrote, until physical reclamation exists.
  - Publication: `billing::rollup_step` publishes the figures a page moved into the table once the page is durable (a failed page publishes nothing; its replay recomputes the same rows); a page that moved nothing still dates the table. `RollupSlot::install_published` publishes every `stored/` row before the slot reads as installed; required mode opens the rollup before the server serves, so the table holds the last life's figures from the first request. In non-required mode the rollup opens inside its task after serving begins.
  - New log lines: at install, a database with `segment/` rows and no `stored-seg/` row (the index's own rows; an index that has seen only gauge-0 snapshots holds `stored-seg/` rows and no `stored/` row, and is not reported) logs the error `segment rows and no stored index: this database predates the index` and publishes nothing; it is never backfilled (no such database exists: the beta's cell is new on layout 6; the fix would be a new rollup namespace, as `ROLLUP_PATH`'s v2 was). A segment snapshot whose project is no project id is logged (`a segment snapshot whose project is no project id is not in the stored index`) and not indexed, and the rest of its page applies; every descriptor carries a validated project id, so only a hand-made ledger reaches it.
  - One new way for a page to fail, as a corrupt row of any rollup family does: a `stored/` row holding less than a closing segment gives back (only a corrupt row reaches it). The rollup then retries that page and does not advance.
- **Retry semantics:** None.
- **Who is affected:** Operators and dashboards that read the report. A reader that reads members by name is unaffected; a reader that rejects unknown members fails. In the repository nothing reads the `rollup` member by name except the RUNBOOK table (`git grep` of `bench/`, `scripts/`, `deploy/` and `sdk/`). Admission holds the table and reads nothing from it until item B4.
- **Given up:** Nothing. The cost: one more read per segment a page advances and one per project it moves (beside the four `apply_snapshot` already makes), about 120 B per live segment in the rollup database, and one table entry per project in memory.
- **Deployment comparison:** No setting changes. A binary before this change never reads or writes the new keys: rolling back and forward again leaves the index short of the pages the earlier binary applied, which nothing reconciles. No cell has run this rollup database, and the owner chose no migrations.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/rollup/stored_index/tests.rs (new, T3): `the_figure_is_the_latest_gauge_of_each_live_segment` (replays, an older version and a newer one that moves no gauge publish nothing; a rollover's month-final and live snapshot of one version in either order), `a_workspace_change_counts_a_segment_once` (400, not 700; in one page out of order; another account's snapshot of the held version and clock moves nothing), `a_close_gives_its_bytes_back_and_written_keeps_them` (on the live path and as a late close of a closed month), `written_adds_each_increase_one_page_holds` (a growth and its close in one page written 100; the close first across a workspace change; a fall between two growths), `written_does_not_depend_on_where_pages_cut_the_ledger` (16 seeded random ledgers of eight segments with replays, cut into random pages, against each segment's sum of gauge increases), `a_failed_page_stages_nothing_and_publishes_nothing` (an injected read fault on either index row), `a_project_row_below_a_closing_segment_fails_the_page`, `a_snapshot_of_no_project_id_is_reported_and_not_indexed`, `the_index_equals_the_segment_rows_derivation` (16 seeded random sequences of 12 pages across two accounts against a derivation from the `segment/` rows), `a_reopened_rollup_publishes_its_durable_figures`, `a_database_that_predates_the_index_is_reported_never_backfilled`, `an_index_of_closes_alone_is_not_reported_as_predating_it` (a stream's close as its segment's first snapshot, reopened: no error, nothing published).
  - src/quota/stored/tests.rs (new): the table's publication, in place and for a new project, its date, and an empty publication.
  - src/rollup/readiness.rs::tests: `the_report_member_reads_the_rollup_and_ages_the_last_apply` (nine members, `stored` null before a publication) and `the_stored_member_totals_the_figures_and_lists_the_ten_that_wrote_most` (new: totals, the date, the top ten with a tie, a later publication).
  - src/dst/tests/billing_readiness.rs: `the_rollup_report_splits_pending_artifacts_by_publishability` (over the wire: the member list gains `stored`, which an installed rollup with no index rows answers with zero projects and its install's date); `the_rollup_report_states_the_stored_figures_admission_holds` (new: twelve projects of one shared cell append different volumes; after the drain and the rollup step the table admission reads holds each project's figure, equal to what its stream's usage says it stores, and the member lists the ten largest); `an_opened_rollup_publishes_the_stored_index_it_holds` (new: `open_rollup` publishes a database's `stored/` rows into the table as it installs it).
  - Red on the unfixed tree: the tests do not compile (`error[E0432]: unresolved imports super::StoredRow, super::k_stored, super::k_stored_seg`; `unresolved import crate::quota::stored`; `no method named stored_table found for struct QuotaRegistry`; `no method named publish_stored_into found for struct UsageRollup`; `this method takes 2 arguments but 3 arguments were supplied` for `readiness`).
  - Controls (hand-applied, reverted): keying the index's segment rows by account fails `a_workspace_change_counts_a_segment_once` (700 for 400) and the random derivation; a non-strict fence (`>=`) fails it (999 published for nothing); `rollup_step` not publishing fails `the_rollup_report_states_the_stored_figures_admission_holds` (0 projects for 12); `open_rollup` installing without publishing fails `an_opened_rollup_publishes_the_stored_index_it_holds`.
- **Risk reason:** low: one operator route gains one member and every existing member keeps its value; the rollup's page gains rows in its batch, one read per advanced segment and moved project, and one failure that only a corrupt `stored/` row reaches. Nothing refuses a request on the figures until item B4, whose record carries that risk.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the stored-cap triage's B3 spec. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #159 cb5e79fa — `GET /operator/data.json` serves the last telemetry tick's ops snapshot, cached and not re-collected, beside the auth feeds' ages, the shed breakdown, the maintenance latch, the reserved absorb bytes, the live subscriptions and the usage overflow admits

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12), built as the alerting triage's item B1 (S2; Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12): it makes `/operator/data.json` the single alert surface the cell watch polls (the triage's items B2 and B3). Ratified at landing by the owner's answer X2 of 2026-10-12 ("ratify all at landing; hold none"; X2 names "alerting's S2 operator record (no client-visible bytes)"); numbered #159 at landing, the next free number at slate cfc211e2.
- **Surface:** operator-debug: the operator surface behind the deployment bearer (SR-5). No customer route, status or header changes.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /operator/data.json` → `operator::data` (`src/operator.rs`). The snapshot is cached by `OpsService::remember` and read by `OpsService::last_snapshot` (`src/ops.rs`, an `ArcSwapOption`); the drain loop's emission (`MetricsEmission::round`, `src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs`, #164) remembers each telemetry tick's snapshot (every `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS`, 15 s by default) before it evaluates the alerts and before the `_ops_metrics` append, so the cache holds while the cell's own telemetry appends are shed; the rigs' one-shot `emit_metrics_once` remembers its snapshot the same way (before landing-4 joined this record to #164, `emit_metrics_once` was the loop's emission).
- **Condition:** A bearer-authenticated `GET /operator/data.json`.
- **Before:** `{ts_ms, local{instance, open_shards, ring_active, inflight, inflight_peak, parked, read_memory_bytes, read_memory_capacity_bytes, admit_shed, stream_shed, wedge_shed, admit_max_inflight, admit_max_inflight_per_stream, rss_mb, rss_shed_mb, store}, fleet{heartbeats, desired}}`. The ops snapshot (`history_flush_wait_ms_max`, `unowned_meter_events_total`, the history L0 gauges) was only in the `_ops_metrics` system stream; the shed breakdown, the maintenance latch and the reserved absorb bytes only on `/v1/debug/load` (whose read swaps the inflight peak); the feeds' ages and `reservedDropped` only on `/v1/debug/auth` and `/health`; the overflow admits only on the per-stream `/v1/debug/usage`.
- **After:** The same keys, unchanged, plus:
  - `ops`: the last telemetry tick's `_ops_metrics` snapshot as stored (`{v, ts_ms, cell, region, instance, role, counters, gauges}`), the same value on every read until the next tick: a read re-collects nothing, so it drains none of the snapshot's peak-since-scrape gauges (`history_flush_wait_ms_max`, `rss_peak_since_scrape_mb`). `null` before the first tick, and always on a server without a usage stream key (`emit_metrics_once` collects nothing there).
  - `feeds`: `AuthService::feed_json` at the request's second (`stalenessMaxSecs`, `jwks{keys, ageSecs}`, `policies{projects, feedVersion, reservedDropped, ageSecs, stale}`, `grants{credentials, feedVersion, ageSecs, stale}`), as `/health` and `/v1/debug/auth` compute it.
  - `local.admit_shed_rss`, `local.admit_shed_inflight`, `local.admit_shed_survival` (the parts of `admit_shed`); `local.maintenance_backpressure` (the instance latch's `engaged, cause, instance_engaged, instance_cause, engage_count, appends_shed, unabsorbed_bytes, absorb_lag_secs`, as `/v1/debug/load` prints it); `local.absorb_reserved_bytes_now` (the history absorb budget's reserved bytes); `local.sse_connections` and `local.sse_max_connections` (the effective cap); `local.usage_overflow_admits` (admissions charged to the shared overflow usage entry because the per-stream usage map was full, since boot).
  - The module's doc no longer calls the surface UNSECURED (it has been bearer-gated since SR-5), and RUNBOOK §8 says the same; RUNBOOK's shared-cell "What to alert on" table names these keys.
- **Retry semantics:** None: the watch polls the route.
- **Who is affected:** The operator and the cell watch. No customer: the payload stays operational metadata (the snapshot carries no stream names, routing keys or per-customer dimensions; `feeds` carries counts, versions and ages; the page `/operator` ignores the new keys).
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/runtime_journals.rs::r10_operator_data_serves_the_cached_ops_snapshot_without_recollecting (an enforce rig with an operator bearer; one `emit_metrics_once`; two bearer GETs, both 200; `ops` an object and the same `serde_json::Value` on both reads, its `ts_ms` included; `ops.gauges.history_flush_wait_ms_max`, `feeds.policies.reservedDropped`, `local.admit_shed_rss`, `local.maintenance_backpressure.appends_shed`, `local.sse_max_connections` and `local.usage_overflow_admits` all unsigned integers). Red on the unfixed tree: "operator ops: null". The mutants `last_snapshot -> None` and `remember -> ()` make `ops` null and fail the same assertion.
- **Risk reason:** low: added keys only, on a bearer-gated operator route; no existing key, status or header changes; the cache costs one pointer store per telemetry tick and one load per request, and holds one snapshot (two small maps of counters and gauges). `ops` is up to one telemetry interval old, which the watch's rules account for. WIRE-MATRIX: the `/operator/data.json` row. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the release profile and any field run; CI runs the `ops` mutation owner's mutants on the push; no formal receipt digests `src/ops.rs` or `src/operator.rs`.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the alerting triage's B1 spec. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #165 5f04256d, amended by 4020ac83 — A producer append answered `2xx` whose answer the SDK cannot read is sent again as a lost answer, inside the transport replay, and resolves with the server's answer; it rejects with `StreamsError` `unreadable_response`, retryable, only when its last attempt's answer cannot be read either

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), from the round-3 stack review's SDK correctness finding on 7ff142a7 (#147's review fix, which guarded only the plain appends' `2xx` read; Fable 5.1, `round3/stack-fable-review.json`), verdict real and low.
