Built in build round 4 (lane sdk, item sdk-findings, 5f04256d) with the verifier's fix: one request, then `StreamsError` `unreadable_response` (`retryable: false`), the producer keeping its sequence and the message telling the caller to send the same value again. Amended in build round 5 (lane sdk, item call3-resend-unreadable-2xx) to the owner's call 3 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`, "accept all recommended"; research `round3/owner-calls-5-recs.json` `sdk-1`, option (c) with the skeptic's guardrails): the SDK sends the append again itself, as a lost answer. Why the round-4 behaviour was replaced: the appends `_chain` had already queued on that routing key went out at the kept sequence before the caller could resend, each refused `409` `producer_sequence_reused` when the record was written (a caller who took `retryable: false` as final lost them), and its message said "so it was written", which is false when the `2xx` came from something in front of the server. The reviewer's fix (save `nextSeq + 1` on the unreadable `2xx`) stays refused: after a made-up `2xx` it loses the value and every later value on the key is refused `producer_gap`. Ratified under OWNER-DECISIONS-6 call 3; numbered #165 at landing-4 (2026-10-17).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - `Producer.append` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}/records` with the producer triple, WIRE-MATRIX §2.7) and `Producer.appendMany` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}/records:batch`, §2.8), through `Stream._producerAppend`.
  - Code: `req()` gains `read`, which reads a `2xx` inside the attempts or returns the `StreamsError` saying it could not; such an attempt's answer is lost and takes the transport failure's path (`lose`: sent again after 1, 2 or 4 s within the four attempts, setting `answerLost`; not with `retry: { transport: false }`), and is the request's failure when it ends the attempts. `Stream._producerAppend` passes `producerAnswer` (new), which returns the `unreadable_response` error for a body it cannot read. `producerAppendFailure` passes `unreadable_response` through, as it passes a transport failure through. The new message and `refusedReplayRecovery`'s last branch share `RESEND_SAME_VALUE`. `appendedResult` is again the plain appends' read alone (5f04256d had given it the producer's text); `Stream.appendRaw` stays without its unused `producerHeaders` parameter (5f04256d).
  - Not changed: `Producer.sendNow` (it saves the next sequence only after an answer it read, and claims an epoch only on a `ProducerFencedError`), a producer-backed final `seal` (which reads no body), plain appends (#147: still sent once, `unreadable_response`, `retryable: false`, "do not send it again") and every other request.
- **Condition:** An attempt of a producer append ends in a `2xx` whose body the SDK cannot read: not JSON (an edge's or a proxy's page), or a connection lost after the status line, mid-body.
- **Before:** The published SDK rejected with the runtime's raw `SyntaxError` (not JSON) or `TypeError` (`terminated`) from `res.json()`, not a `StreamsError`, after one request; 5f04256d (round 4, not published) rejected after one request with `StreamsError` `unreadable_response` (`retryable: false`), whose message said the record was written and told the caller to send the same value again. Either way the producer kept its epoch and sequence, so appends already queued on that routing key went out at that sequence: refused `409` `producer_sequence_reused` when the record was written, written ahead of it when the `2xx` was made up.
- **After:**
  - The attempt's answer is lost: the SDK sends the same `producer-id`, `producer-epoch`, `producer-seq` and body again after 1 s (then 2 and 4 s), within the four attempts it shares with the `429`/`503` replay and the transport replay, while the routing key's queue holds later operations. The append resolves with the server's answer to the resend: `duplicate: true`, `count: 0` and the original record's cursor if the lost attempt was written (`decide_producer`, `src/shard/commit_plan.rs`), or the record written once if the `2xx` was made up. The producer then saves the next sequence, and the queued appends go out at the next sequences.
  - A resend the server refuses before its duplicate check (another writer's fence, a seal, a quota still refusing after the attempts, a `421`, any other refusal) rejects as #148's producer variant of `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`outcome_unknown`, `retryable: false`, the refusal as `cause`, the recovery for it), and `autoClaim` claims no epoch: the unreadable answer counts as a lost one (`answerLost`), so a fence never reaches `sendNow` as a `ProducerFencedError`.
  - Only when the last attempt's `2xx` cannot be read either (all four; with `retry: { transport: false }`, the one) does the append reject with a `StreamsError` (not `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`): `status` the `2xx` status, `code` `unreadable_response`, `retryable: true`, `cause` the last read failure, and the message `the producer append's last attempt was answered HTTP <status>, but its answer could not be read, so the SDK cannot tell whether it was written; this producer keeps its sequence, so send the same value on the same routing key through this producer before any other value on that key: the server answers duplicate: true if it was written and writes it once if not; a different value sent first is refused 409 producer_sequence_reused if it was written` (the recovery is #148's for any other refusal). The producer keeps its epoch and sequence. A last attempt that fails in transport rejects as before (`StreamsTransportError`, `retryable: true`).
- **Retry semantics:** The SDK now sends a producer append whose `2xx` it cannot read again (it sent it once): up to three more times, after 1, 2 and 4 s, within the four attempts, as it replays a transport failure (#148), and not with `retry: { transport: false }`. A resend is the same producer triple and body, which the server deduplicates, so it never stores the record twice, and a refused resend claims no epoch. The final `unreadable_response` is `retryable: true`, as `StreamsTransportError` after its replays is: its recovery, the same value through the same producer, is deduplicated.
- **Who is affected:** Producer callers whose append meets an unreadable `2xx` (a proxy's page, a body cut off): they usually get a normal `AppendResult` up to about 7 s later (`duplicate: true` and `count: 0` when the first attempt was written, as after the transport replay), or a typed error they can retry, where they got an error after one request; the appends queued behind it on the routing key are no longer refused `producer_sequence_reused`. A resend costs one more rate-limit token and one more metered `append_request` (metered, not charged: `render_product_append`, `src/product.rs`, meters an accepted duplicate). Callers that branched on the raw `SyntaxError` or `TypeError`. Not the server, the raw surface, plain appends, seals, reads, consumers or watches.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting. `retry: { transport: false }` per client sends the append once and rejects `unreadable_response` at once.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs (mocked `fetch` over a model of `decide_producer` for one producer id that stores what it lets through; every backoff run at once with its requested delay recorded, as in producer-ordering.test.mjs), for `Producer.append` and `Producer.appendMany`, each with a `200` whose body is HTML and a `200` whose body breaks off mid-stream:
    - the round-4 rows ("sent once") rewritten, each in two worlds, the server took the first attempt or the `2xx` was made up (8 rows): two requests with the same URL, producer id, epoch 0, sequence 0 and body, the wait 1000 ms, the append resolving `{cursor: "c1", count: 0, duplicate: true}` (written) or `{cursor: "c1", count: 1, duplicate: false}` (made up), the record stored once, the state store `{epoch 0, nextSeq 1}`; the next value goes out at sequence 1, `{0, 2}`.
    - every attempt unreadable (4 rows): four requests at `0/0` with waits 1000, 2000 and 4000, then that `StreamsError` (`status` 200, `unreadable_response`, `retryable: true`, the exact message, the `SyntaxError` or `TypeError` as `cause`), state `{0, 0}`; the same value sent again resolves `duplicate: true` at `c1`, stored once, `{0, 1}`.
    - `retry: { transport: false }` (4 rows): one request, no wait, the same rejection and recovery.
    - a resend that another writer's fence refuses, `autoClaim` on (1 row): two requests at `0/0`; the record stored once, beside the other writer's; `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`403`, `outcome_unknown`, `retryable: false`, the fence's recovery text) with a `ProducerFencedError` (`currentEpoch` 1) as `cause`; state `{0, 0}`; wait 1000.
    - appends queued behind the unreadable one, written and made up (2 rows): `v1`, `v1` again, `v2` at sequence 1, `v3` at 2; results at `c1` (duplicate as written), `c2`, `c3`; each stored once, in order; `{0, 3}`; wait 1000.
  - Red on the round-4 SDK (`npm run build`, then `node --test scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs`): these 19 rows fail and the file's 73 others pass. The eight lost-answer rows at the rejection `Error [StreamsError]: the server accepted the append (HTTP 200), so it was written, but its answer could not be read; this producer keeps its sequence, ...`; the four every-attempt rows at the waits (`actual: []`, `expected: [ 1000, 2000, 4000 ]`); the four transport-off rows at `[ 200, 'unreadable_response', false ]` for `true`; the fence row at `stored once` (`[ '{"n":1}' ]`: no resend reached the fence); the queued rows at the wire (`0/0 v1, 0/0 v2, 0/0 v3` written, `0/0 v1, 0/0 v2, 0/1 v3` made up).
  - Controls (hand-applied to `src`, rebuilt, reverted, `cmp`-checked): the read path not setting `answerLost` fails the fence row at `stored once` with the record stored a second time (`['{"n":1}', '{"n":"successor"}', '{"n":1}']`: `autoClaim` claimed epoch 2 and resent); not resending an unreadable `2xx` fails 15 rows; `unreadable_response` with `retryable: false` fails the 8 rejection rows; a resend that ignores `retry: { transport: false }` fails the 4 transport-off rows at `the request resolved`; `producerAppendFailure` taking `unreadable_response` for a refused replay fails the 4 every-attempt rows (an `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`); a resend without its backoff fails 15 rows.
  - Unchanged and green: the six plain-append unreadable rows (#147: one request, "do not send it again"), sdk/scripts/producer-ordering.test.mjs (mechanism `sdk-producer-order`), restart-resilience.test.mjs and the rest of `npm test`.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes; a resend is the same producer triple and body, which the server deduplicates, inside the replay budget, queue order and off switch the ratified transport replay (#148) already has, and a refused resend falls back on #148's ratified error without claiming an epoch. The cost is one more rate-limit token and one more metered, uncharged `append_request` per resend, and a routing-key stall of up to about 7 s, in a rare case. The likelier real trigger, an intermediary's made-up `200`, may meet the same answer at every attempt, so there the gain is a true, retryable error about 7 s later instead of a false "it was written"; the exactness gain is in the cut-off-body case. The README's "Errors and retries" and "Producer state ownership", the CHANGELOG (Breaking) and WIRE-MATRIX §4 say so. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the suite, CI's `sdk-package` smokes and the platform e2e. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled.
- **Owner decision:** call 3 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`): option (c), the resend as a lost answer inside the transport replay. It replaces the round-4 question (ratify the one-request rejection, or save the next sequence).
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the owner's call and its research (`sdk-1`: the analyst's `on_accept` and the skeptic's `better`, guardrails included). Not checked by an independent pass.

### #166 da04d9a5 — The SDK refuses a stream key that, the whitespace around it trimmed, holds anything but printable ASCII without spaces, or that is not a string, with `StreamsError` `invalid_encryption_key_format` before any request and without showing the key

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), from the round-3 stack review's SDK correctness finding on dc8b29f4 (#148's transport replay; Fable 5.1, `round3/stack-fable-review.json`), verdict real and low: the stream-key twin of the credential finding that `presentedCredential` fixed (#148's amendments). Built in build round 4 (lane sdk, item sdk-findings), whose spec reads "trim `[ \t\r\n]`; refuse any other control character". Built wider than that sentence, and why: a character above U+00FF (a curly quote, a zero-width space from a copied document) makes `fetch` throw a `TypeError` too, which `req()` replayed as a transport failure exactly as the finding describes for a line break, so a rule of control characters alone leaves that half of the finding; the rule built is the credential's, printable ASCII without spaces, which refuses every character `fetch` cannot send and no key the server accepts (`StreamKey::from_b64` decodes base64 text; `product_key` reads only visible ASCII). Ratified as built under OWNER-DECISIONS-6 call 4 (2026-10-15, `OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`, "accept all recommended"; research `round3/owner-calls-5-recs.json` `sdk-2`, option (a), with the skeptic's text fix to Who is affected); numbered #166 at landing-4 (2026-10-17).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - `StreamsClient.stream(name, { encryptionKey })` (throws), `StreamsClient.createStream(name, { encryptionKey, ... })` (rejects; `PUT /v1/streams/{name}`, WIRE-MATRIX §2.2), and the exported `Stream` constructor both of them call; through the handle, every request that sends `prisma-encryption-key` (appends, reads, subscriptions, consumers, watches, seal, metadata, delete) and the watch capability derived from the key.
  - Code: `presentedKey` and `KEY_TEXT` (new), called by the `Stream` constructor, which keeps the trimmed key; `createStream` makes its handle first and sends the handle's key (`_kh()`), so the key is checked in one place.
  - Not changed: what is sent for a key that passes (`fetch` trimmed the same whitespace from the header value), the credential path (`presentedCredential`, #148), `generateEncryptionKey()`.
  - Not changed, and outside this record: the other caller-supplied header values on the same requests, the routing key (`prisma-routing-key`, `append`, `appendBytes`, `appendMany`, `Producer.append`, `Producer.appendMany`) and the producer id (`producer-id`, `Stream.producer(id)`), which this record left sent as given. One holding a line break, a carriage return or a NUL, another control character but a tab, or a character above U+00FF inside it failed inside `fetch` before anything was sent (the built SDK, Node 24.18, a counting `fetch` wrapper): a plain append rejected `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` after 1 call, `fetch`'s `TypeError` quoting the value as its `cause`; a producer append rejected `StreamsTransportError` (`retryable: true`) after 4 calls and 7 s. Whitespace at either end (a line break included) did not fail: `fetch` stripped it and the value went out as another; a Latin-1 character was sent and the server refused it. Since #167 (call 5) both are refused before any request, with the bearer token.
- **Condition:** A key that, with `[ \t\r\n]` trimmed from both ends, holds a character outside U+0021..U+007E, or a key that is not a string (a JavaScript caller's unset environment variable). An empty key is not refused.
- **Before:** The key was sent as given.
  - A line break, a carriage return or a NUL inside it: `fetch` threw `TypeError: Headers.append: "<the whole key>" is an invalid header value.` Any other control character: `TypeError: fetch failed` (cause `InvalidArgumentError: invalid prisma-encryption-key header`). A character above U+00FF: `TypeError: Cannot convert argument to a ByteString ...`. `req()` took each for a transport failure: `metadata()` (unfixed SDK, Node 24.18) made 4 requests after waits of 1, 2 and 4 s and rejected `StreamsTransportError` (`retryable: true`) whose `cause` quoted the key; `append()` made 1 and rejected `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` ("retry only if a second copy is acceptable") although nothing was sent, the key in its `cause`; `subscribe()` reconnected until aborted (48 attempts in 300 ms with its waits collapsed) and surfaced nothing, and the consumer iterator likewise.
  - A tab, a space or a Latin-1 character inside it reached the server: `400` `invalid_key` or `missing_key` on a keyed route, and nothing on a route that reads no key (`metadata()`).
  - A key that was not a string was sent as `fetch` converts it (`undefined`).
- **After:**
  - `stream()` throws, and `createStream()` rejects before any request, with a `StreamsError`: `status` 0, `code` `invalid_encryption_key_format`, `retryable: false`, no `cause`, and the message `the encryption key is not printable ASCII without spaces (a line break, a control character, a space or a character beyond ASCII is inside it, or it is not a string); copy it again from where you keep it`. Neither the message nor any field holds the key.
  - A key with whitespace around it is kept trimmed; the bytes sent are the ones `fetch` sent before.
- **Retry semantics:** The refusal is not retryable and no request is made, so nothing is replayed; before, the refusals `fetch` made were replayed as transport failures (`retryable: true`) on every request that replays one, and a subscription's or consumer loop's reconnection never ended.
- **Who is affected:** Callers whose key holds such a character (a wrapped paste, a key copied from a document): they get the refusal at the handle, without the key, instead of a transport error that quotes it, a false unknown outcome or a silent loop. Callers that made a handle with such a key, or with no key, only for a route that reads no key (`metadata()`, `delete()`, `watches()`): refused now; a handle made with an empty key, or any placeholder of printable ASCII without spaces, still passes, so a caller who lost the key can still delete the stream. Not the server, the raw surface, raw HTTP clients or keys made by `generateEncryptionKey()`.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting, and the SDK has no switch for it.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/encryption-key.test.mjs (new; the runtime's own `fetch` against a loopback server, so `fetch`'s header checks are the ones a key meets): for a key with a line break, a carriage return, a NUL, another control character, a DEL, a vertical tab at its end, a character above U+00FF, a zero-width space, a tab, a space and a Latin-1 character inside it (11 rows), `createStream()` rejects and `stream()` throws with that `StreamsError` (class, `status`, `code`, `retryable`, the exact message), its JSON with `message`, `stack` and `cause` holds no part of the key, and no request is made; a key that is not a string, the same for both; a generated key with whitespace around it, a 44-character padded standard key with whitespace around it and a generated key are sent trimmed and as given. Red on the unfixed SDK: the eight rows `fetch` refuses at `createStream` with `['StreamsTransportError', 0, 'transport_error', true]` for `['StreamsError', 0, 'invalid_encryption_key_format', false]`; the tab, space and Latin-1 rows at `createStream: got undefined` (the loopback server took them); the not-a-string row at `stream: got undefined`. The trim row is green before and after (it pins the bytes sent).
  - Controls (hand-applied, reverted, `cmp`-checked): refusing control characters only (`/^[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$/`, the spec's sentence) fails the Latin-1, U+2019, space and zero-width-space rows; keeping the key untrimmed fails the trim row; a `cause` that quotes the key fails eleven rows at `the error does not carry the key`.
  - Unchanged and green: every other SDK test (their keys are `"A".repeat(43)` or generated), sdk/scripts/credential-provider.test.mjs's credential format rows.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes; a key refused now never reached a keyed route intact (`fetch` refused it, or the server refused it), and the keys the SDK makes pass. The one path that worked and is refused now is a handle made with such a key, or none, for a route that reads no key. The README's "Encryption keys", the CHANGELOG (Breaking) and WIRE-MATRIX §4 say so. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the suite, CI's `sdk-package` smokes and the platform e2e. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled.
- **Owner decision:** call 4 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`): option (a), ratified as built, over narrowing it to control characters only (which leaves a key with a character above U+00FF replayed as a transport failure) and widening it to the server's full key format (a second copy of `StreamKey::from_b64`'s rule, and a handle a caller who lost the key can no longer make). The follow-up the lane review raised on this commit, a routing key and a producer id `fetch` cannot send, was put to the owner separately as call 5 of the same day (with the bearer token, the skeptic's addition) and is built as #167.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the review finding, the verifier's fix and the lane's spec, with the departure stated in Program item. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #167 8f7d95b6 — The SDK refuses, before any request, a routing key, a producer id or a bearer token that a header cannot carry byte for byte, with `StreamsError` `invalid_routing_key`, `invalid_producer` or `invalid_token_format`, without showing it

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), from the round-4 lane review's finding on #166: the header-value trap that record closed for the stream key stayed open for the routing key and the producer id. Put to the owner as that record's follow-up question, with the bearer token added by the `sdk-2` skeptic. Built in build round 5 (lane sdk, item call5-header-values) under the owner's call 5 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`, "accept all recommended"; research `round3/owner-calls-5-recs.json` `sdk-headers`: the analyst's option (c) with the skeptic's three amendments: `seal()`'s routing key is checked too, the `undefined` producer id is stated as it behaved, and the tests assert the SDK's own errors and the bytes the server received, never a runtime's message text, because CI's `sdk-package` runs Node 22). Ratified under OWNER-DECISIONS-6 call 5; numbered #167 at landing-4 (2026-10-17).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - Routing key: `Stream.append`, `appendBytes` and `appendMany` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}/records` and `/records:batch` without the producer triple, WIRE-MATRIX §2.7/§2.8), `Producer.append` and `Producer.appendMany` (with it), through `Stream.appendRaw`, `Stream.appendMany` and `Stream._producerAppend`, each sending `prisma-routing-key`; and `Stream.seal({ final, routingKey })` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}:seal`, §2.5), alone or through a producer, whose final record's routing key travels in the JSON body.
  - Producer id: `Stream.producer(id)` and the exported `Producer` constructor it calls (`producer-id` on every producer append and a producer-backed final seal).
  - Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`): the `StreamsClient` constructor's `token`; a `tokenProvider`'s answer (a string or `{ token, expiresAt }`) where a refresh caches it; `StreamsClient.connect`'s first exchange, which seeds the cache the same way.
  - Code: `HEADER_TEXT`, `MAX_ROUTING_KEY_LENGTH`, `headerText`, `presentedRoutingKey` and `presentedToken` (new). `cachedToken` checks the token, and `refreshToken` runs it before its settle handlers, so a refused token takes a failed refresh's path (the cache keeps nothing, and the next request asks the provider again).
  - Not changed: a read's `routingKey` (`read`, `subscribe`; the query value, left unchecked by the call: the skeptic's optional read check was not taken), the stream key (#166), the credential (#148), consumer names, every server-minted value, and what is sent for a value that passes.
- **Condition:** A routing key that is given (not absent, `null` or empty) and is not a string, or holds anything but printable ASCII (U+0020..U+007E) and tabs, or has whitespace (a space, a tab, a line break, a carriage return) at either end, or is longer than 1,024 characters. A producer id, or a token (a static one that is not absent or empty, or any answer of a provider), that is not a non-empty string of that text.
- **Before** (the unfixed SDK, Node 24.18, a loopback server reached through the runtime's own `fetch`, backoffs collapsed):
  - A line break, a carriage return or a NUL inside the value, another control character but a tab, or a character above U+00FF: `fetch` threw a `TypeError` before anything was sent (quoting the value for the first three), which `req()` took for a transport failure. A plain append made 1 call and rejected `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`outcome_unknown`, `retryable: false`, "retry only if a second copy is acceptable") although nothing was sent; a producer append, and any other request with such a token, made 4 calls over 7 s and rejected `StreamsTransportError` (`retryable: true`), the value in its `cause`. A token with a line break or a carriage return at its start sat inside `Bearer <token>` and met the same `TypeError`. One with a space or a tab at its start was sent inside the value (`"Bearer  t"`, `"Bearer \tt"`), which the server read as the token `" t"` (`"\tt"`) and refused `401` `unauthorized`: the SDK rejected `StreamsError` `401` `unauthorized`, with a `tokenProvider` after its one `401` refresh asked the provider again and sent the same token (two requests, two provider calls).
  - Whitespace at either end: `fetch` stripped it without a word, so the request carried another value. `append(v, { routingKey: "k " })` (or `"k\n"`) was written under `"k"`, and a whitespace-only key under the default lane. Producer `"p "` was sent as producer `"p"`, which the SDK keeps as a separate scope with its own sequence, so a value at a sequence below the server's last for `"p"` was answered `duplicate: true` unwritten (`decide_producer`, `src/shard/commit_plan.rs`, checks no body below the last sequence). A token `"t "` went out as `Bearer t`, a whitespace-only one as `Bearer` (the server's `401`).
  - A Latin-1 character (`fetch` sends U+0080..U+00FF), a routing key over 1,024 characters, or an empty producer id: sent, and refused by the server (`400` `invalid_routing_key`, `400` `invalid_producer`, `401` `unauthorized`).
  - A value that is not a string: sent as `fetch` converts it (`42`). An `undefined` producer id threw a `TypeError` at the first append from `MemoryProducerStateStore`'s key, before any request, and was sent as `"undefined"` with a caller's durable store.
  - A final seal's routing key was sent as given in the JSON body: the server refused what `parse_routing_key` refuses (`400` `invalid_routing_key`) and accepted whitespace at either end, so `seal({ final, routingKey: "k " })` made lane `"k "`, which no append could write.
  - A `tokenProvider` that returned no token (`undefined`, or anything but a string or an object): its refresh rejected with a raw `TypeError` and stayed cached as the refresh in flight, so every later request rejected with it and the provider was never asked again (the probe: two requests, one provider call).
- **After:**
  - Before any request, every append and `seal()` reject, `stream.producer(id)` throws, and the `StreamsClient` constructor throws, with a `StreamsError`: `status` 0, `retryable: false`, no `cause`, and the code and message:
    - `invalid_routing_key`: `the routing key is not text a header carries as it is (printable ASCII and tabs, no whitespace at either end, at most 1,024 characters); nothing was sent`
    - `invalid_producer`: `the producer id is not text a header carries as it is (printable ASCII and tabs, no whitespace at either end, not empty); nothing was sent`
    - `invalid_token_format`: `the bearer token (the client's token, or one a tokenProvider or the issuer returned) is not text a header carries as it is (printable ASCII and tabs, no whitespace at either end, not empty); nothing was sent`
  - Neither the message nor any field holds the value. The first two codes are the server's own for the same values (`parse_routing_key`; `AppendCode::InvalidProducer`); the server answers a bad bearer token `401` `unauthorized`, so the third is the SDK's, beside `invalid_encryption_key_format` and `invalid_credential_format`.
  - A request whose `tokenProvider` returned such a token, or no token, rejects with `invalid_token_format`, as do the requests waiting on that refresh; the cache keeps nothing, and the next request asks the provider again. While a valid cached token is in use, a refresh beside it that returns one is not surfaced and is tried again 30 s later, as any failed refresh is. `connect` rejects with it when the issuer's first token is one.
  - Nothing is trimmed: a value that passes is sent byte for byte, interior tabs and spaces included (the server accepts them). An empty or absent routing key is the default lane, and an empty static token sends no `Authorization`, as before.
- **Retry semantics:** The refusal is not retryable and no request is made, so nothing is replayed. Before, `fetch`'s refusals were replayed as transport failures (a producer append's and a token's for 7 s, `retryable: true`).
- **Who is affected:** Callers whose routing key, producer id or token holds such a value, most often a line break or a space at an end (a value read from a file or an environment variable) or a character copied from a document: they get the refusal, without the value, instead of a write under another key or producer, a false unknown outcome, 7 s of replays or the server's `400`/`401`. Callers that relied on `fetch`'s silent stripping now trim the value themselves. A `tokenProvider` that returns a bad token no longer wedges the client. Not the server, the raw surface, raw HTTP clients or reads; not the in-repo SDK callers (`sdk/smoke.mjs`, `scripts/platform-e2e.mjs`), whose routing keys and producer ids are of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` and whose tokens are issued JWTs.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting, and the SDK has no switch for it.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/header-values.test.mjs (new; the runtime's own `fetch` against a loopback server that records the routing-key, producer-id and authorization bytes it receives; every backoff collapsed; assertions on the SDK's errors and the received bytes only):
    - 18 routing-key rows (a line break, a carriage return, a NUL, another control character, a DEL, U+2019, an emoji or a Latin-1 character inside; a space, a tab or a line break at its start or end, CR LF at its end; only whitespace; 1,025 characters; a number): `append`, `appendBytes`, `appendMany`, `Producer.append`, `Producer.appendMany`, `seal` and a producer-backed `seal` each reject with that `StreamsError` (class, `status`, `code`, `retryable`, the exact message, no `cause`, no part of the value in its JSON with `message` and `stack`), and no request is made.
    - 19 producer-id rows (the first 16 of those, plus empty, `undefined` and a number): `stream.producer(id)` throws so; no request.
    - 17 bearer-token rows (the same 16 and a number), each for the static token and for a `tokenProvider` answering it as a string and as `{ token, expiresAt }`; a provider answering `undefined`, `""` or `{ token: "" }`; a provider refused once is asked again by the next request, which carries `Bearer t2`; `connect` whose issuer answers a token holding a line break rejects so before any request carries it.
    - Pins, green before and after: routing keys `a\tb`, `a b`, `a+b`, `a%20b`, `!~` and one of 1,024 characters are received byte for byte from `append`, `appendMany` and `Producer.append`, and an empty or absent one sends no header; producer ids `p`, `p q`, `p\tq` and `p+q` byte for byte; tokens `a.b-c_d`, `a b` and a provider's `x\ty` byte for byte, and an empty or absent static token sends none.
  - Red on the unfixed SDK (`npm run build`, then `node --test scripts/header-values.test.mjs`): 57 of the 60 tests fail and the three pins pass. The rows `fetch` refuses fail at `['AppendOutcomeUnknownError', 0, 'outcome_unknown', false]` (the routing key's first write, `append`) or `['StreamsTransportError', 0, 'transport_error', true]` (producer id, token, the provider asked again, `connect`); the stripping, Latin-1, length, empty and number rows at `append: got undefined`, `producer: got undefined` or `token: got undefined` (the request went out); the `undefined` producer id at `got TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`; the provider row at `got TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'expiresAt')`.
  - Controls (hand-applied to `src`, rebuilt, reverted, `cmp`-checked): whitespace allowed at the ends fails 15 rows; no 1,024 cap fails the 1,025 row; `seal()` unchecked fails the 18 routing-key rows at `seal`; the token checked inside the refresh's settle handler (where a refusal leaves the rejected refresh cached) fails the asked-again row; the `Producer` constructor unchecked fails the 19 producer rows; the static token unchecked fails the 17 token rows; the value kept in the error's `details` fails the 48 rows whose value holds the marker, at `the error does not carry the value`.
  - Unchanged and green: every other SDK test (`npm test`: 298 pass with this file, `AUTH_BEHAVIOR_OK`, `WATCH_CAPABILITY_VECTOR_OK`, on Node 24.18, 22.15 and 18.20), among them sdk/scripts/producer-ordering.test.mjs (mechanism `sdk-producer-order`), token-refresh.test.mjs and credential-provider.test.mjs.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes. The rule is exactly what `fetch` sends unchanged and the server accepts on the header path, so a value refused now never reached the server as given (`fetch` refused it, sent another value, or the server refused it), and a value that passes is sent as before. The one path that worked and is refused now is a value with whitespace at an end, which was written under the stripped value. The README's "Routing keys, producer ids and tokens", the CHANGELOG (Breaking) and WIRE-MATRIX §4 say so. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the suite, CI's `sdk-package` smokes and the platform e2e. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled.
- **Owner decision:** call 5 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`): refuse before any request what the header cannot carry byte for byte (tab and U+0020..U+007E, no whitespace at either end, a routing key of at most 1,024 characters, a non-empty producer id), at the append paths, the `Producer` constructor, `seal()`'s routing key and the bearer token; option (c), over the lane's printable-ASCII-without-spaces rule (stricter than the server, which accepts interior tabs and spaces) and leaving the values sent as given (which keeps the silent writes under another key or producer). It answers #166's follow-up question.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the owner's call and its research (`sdk-headers`: the analyst's `on_accept` and the skeptic's `better`; `sdk-2`'s skeptic for the token). Not checked by an independent pass.

### #168 b5ad8b10 — The SDK's `read()` and `subscribe()` send a space in a routing key as `%20`, so a key with a space reads the lane its appends were written to

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), found by the `sdk-headers` analyst while researching #166's follow-up question ("that holds whichever option is chosen"), and accepted as the sibling commit of #167 under the owner's call 5 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`, "accept all recommended": "read()/subscribe() send a space as %20"; research `round3/owner-calls-5-recs.json` `sdk-headers`). Built in build round 5 (lane sdk, item call5-header-values). Ratified under OWNER-DECISIONS-6 call 5; numbered #168 at landing-4 (2026-10-17).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - `Stream.read({ routingKey })` (`GET /v1/streams/{name}/records?routingKey=...`, WIRE-MATRIX §2.9) and `Stream.subscribe({ routingKey })` (its catch-up reads, §2.9, and its long polls, `GET .../records:long-poll?routingKey=...`, §2.10).
  - Code: `recordsQuery` (new) serializes those two queries and replaces every `+` with `%20`. `URLSearchParams` writes a space as `+` and a plus as `%2B`, so every `+` it wrote stands for a space and the replacement is exact.
  - Not changed: what any other query carries (`scan`, `listStreams`, `usage`, watch waits: server-minted cursors and fixed values), the append header (#167), and the read's routing key, which is not checked (call 5 leaves reads unchecked).
- **Condition:** A read or a subscription whose `routingKey` holds a space.
- **Before:** `URLSearchParams` sent the space as `+`, and the server's `parse_query` (`src/product.rs`: "'+' is NOT treated as a space") decodes only `%XX`, so `read({ routingKey: "a b" })` and `subscribe({ routingKey: "a b" })` asked for lane `"a+b"`: an empty lane, or another key's records when lane `"a+b"` held some, while `append(v, { routingKey: "a b" })` wrote to lane `"a b"` (its header carries the space). A tab (`%09`), a plus (`%2B`) and every other character were sent percent-encoded and read back.
- **After:** The space goes out as `%20`, so the server reads `"a b"`, the lane the appends were written to; every other byte of the query is unchanged.
- **Retry semantics:** Unchanged: the same requests, retried as before (#148; a subscription's reads reconnect).
- **Who is affected:** SDK callers reading or subscribing to a routing key with a space: they now read that key's records instead of an empty lane or the lane with a `+` in its place. Not the server, raw HTTP clients, appends, keys without a space, or the default lane.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/header-values.test.mjs (#167's file; its loopback cell now answers a records read up to date and a long poll also sealed, so a subscription reads once, polls once and ends), "read() and subscribe() ask for the lane a routing key's appends were written to": for the keys `a b`, `a  b c`, `a\tb`, `a+b`, `a%20b`, `a&b=c`, `!~` and a 1,024-character key holding spaces, the bytes of the append's `prisma-routing-key` header equal the `routingKey` the server's own query decoding (split on `&`, then `=`, only `%XX` decoded, as `parse_query` does) reads from `read()`, from `subscribe()`'s catch-up read and from its long poll.
  - Red on the SDK before this commit (`npm run build`, then `node --test scripts/header-values.test.mjs`): this row fails and the file's 60 others pass, at `"a b"`: `actual: [ 'a+b', 'a+b', 'a+b' ]`, `expected: [ 'a b', 'a b', 'a b' ]`.
  - Controls (hand-applied to `src`, rebuilt, reverted, `cmp`-checked): the fix in `read()` only fails the row at `"a b"`; the long poll left unfixed fails it at `"a b"`; replacing only the first `+` fails it at `"a  b c"`.
  - Unchanged and green: every other SDK test (`npm test`: 299 pass, `AUTH_BEHAVIOR_OK`, `WATCH_CAPABILITY_VECTOR_OK`), among them retry-classification.test.mjs (mechanism `sdk-retry-classification`: a subscription's reconnection).
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes, and the only query bytes that change are the `+` that stood for a space, which the server read as a plus. The README's "Routing keys, producer ids and tokens", the CHANGELOG (Fixed) and WIRE-MATRIX §4 say so. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the suite, CI's `sdk-package` smokes and the platform e2e. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled.
- **Owner decision:** call 5 of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`): `read()` and `subscribe()` send a space as `%20`, in a commit beside #167's refusal.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the owner's call and its research (`sdk-headers`). Not checked by an independent pass.

### #148 dc8b29f4, amended by 06f36423, ad332467, 80e8e697, 38b59eed, 1ff0c3ed, 2c8b2aeb, f5f98296, d4d46c48, d908b2e9 — The SDK replays a transport failure of a request the server answers idempotently, within the attempts the 429/503 replay already shares, and its consumer and watch loops reconnect instead of ending

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), built as the SDK triage's item B2 (S-2, drafted there as SDK-E4; Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12, `sdk.md` and its triage), decided under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-11 to Fable 5.1, with the triage's skeptic corrections K7 (one budget shared with the `429`/`503` replay, and an off switch) and K8 (no timers). Built without two of the triage's replays, producer appends and `settle`: each turns a test of a script pinned in `docs/refactor/review-mechanisms.json` red, and those scripts are not edited without the owner. Replaying them (a hand-applied control) fails `sdk/scripts/producer-ordering.test.mjs` "fetch failure propagates and does not poison subsequent producer operations" (mechanism `sdk-producer-order`, R20) with `Missing expected rejection.`, and `sdk/scripts/consumer-cleanup.test.mjs` "batch settlement is idempotent and failed decisions are never reported acked" (in the script `sdk-consumer-cleanup`, R21, pins) with `4 !== 1`, each because its fixture scripts one transport failure and asserts it reaches the caller after one request. This record is amended when they join. A subscription's own reads are not replayed by the request either: the triage leaves `subscribe()` unchanged, and its loop's reconnection from the durable cursor of an applied read is pinned (`sdk-retry-classification`, R22). Owner question X2 (sdk O2: ratify SDK-E0, SDK-E4 and SDK-E2 at landing) was decided by the owner on 2026-10-12 as recommended (`OWNER-DECISIONS-2-2026-10-12.md`, X2: the public-beta records are ratified at landing and numbered from #141 in landing order, none held), the default this record was built on; N1 (sdk O1) was decided (1a) the same day and changes nothing here (plain appends are not replayed under any option). The number is assigned at landing, from #141 in landing order. Ratified at landing (X2), except the refused-replay rule of the producer-append amendment (After), which the owner ratified as built on 2026-10-13 (README, "Owner decisions", row "Public-beta calls, round 3 (decided 2026-10-13)", call 7), with an SDK text-and-test commit for its three-branch recovery (fence, seal, anything else; a `421` through the new endpoint's client) before `publish-sdk`, built in round 4 (the recovery-text amendment, below).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - Replayed after a transport failure: `StreamsClient.createStream` (`PUT /v1/streams/{name}`, WIRE-MATRIX §2.2), `listStreams`, `Stream.metadata`, `read`, `scan`, `watches` (and the definitions and epoch `watch()` reads), `seal` with or without a final record or a producer (§2.5: an exact replay answers `200`), `Stream.consumer()` (`PUT .../consumers/{consumer}`), `Consumer.config`, `Consumer.delete` (§2.14: `204` for an incarnation already deleted), `Consumer.pull` and the consumer iterator's pulls, and `Watch.wait`; since the producer-append amendment (below), producer appends (`Producer.append`, `Producer.appendMany`; §2.7/§2.8 with the producer triple), with the same `producer-id`, `producer-epoch`, `producer-seq` and body; since the settle amendment (below), `PullBatch.settle()` and the iterator's settlement (`POST .../consumers/{consumer}:settle`), with the same decisions.
  - Not replayed: plain appends (`append`, `appendBytes`, `appendMany`, #147), `Stream.delete` (§2.4: a replay after a success answers `404`), and `Stream.subscribe()`'s reads and long polls (its loop reconnects, as before).
  - Loops: the consumer iterator (`for await (const message of consumer)`, `Consumer.messages()`) and `Watch.subscribe()`.
  - Option: `StreamsClientOptions.retry?: { transport?: boolean }`, default `true`.
- **Condition:**
  - A replayed request's `fetch` rejects: a refused or reset connection (a deploy, a restart, an edge restart), DNS, TLS, or a browser's CORS or mixed-content block.
  - For the loops: a pull or a watch wait that ends in a transport failure, or in a `429` or `503` marked or defaulted `retryable`, after its request's own attempts.
- **Before:**
  - Every request rejected at its first transport failure with `StreamsTransportError` (`status` 0, `code` `transport_error`, `retryable: true`, the thrown value in `cause`), sent once.
  - The consumer iterator ended (`next()` rejected, `closed` reported `failed`) at a pull's transport failure, or at a `429`/`503` still refused after the pull's four attempts. `watch.subscribe()` ended the same way at a wait's failure, and aborting its signal while a wait was parked rejected `next()` with the abort reason.
  - `Stream.subscribe()` reconnected after 1 s (unchanged).
- **After:**
  - A replayed request whose `fetch` rejects is sent again (same method, URL, headers and body; the credential from the provider's cache) after 1, 2 or 4 s, the wait chosen by the attempt that failed (attempt 0, 1, 2), abort-aware, within the four attempts the request's `429`/`503` replay counts too; attempts after a `401` count, but the `401`'s single token refresh is not bounded by them (as before), so a request makes at most five attempts, the fifth only after a `401` at the fourth. When they are spent the last failure rejects as before: `StreamsTransportError`, or the `429`/`503`'s `StreamsError`. Three transport failures delay the error by 7 s; three `Retry-After: 5` answers by 15 s, as before.
  - Since the producer-append amendment: a producer append whose replay meets an error answer after an attempt's transport failure (another writer fenced the producer id: `403 stale_producer_epoch`, which `decide_producer` checks before duplicates; a sealed or sealing collection: `409 sealed`, which the product handler checks before the core; a quota `429` still refused after the attempts; a cell that no longer serves the project: `421 wrong_cell`; any other refusal) rejects with `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`outcome_unknown`, `retryable: false`, the refusal's `status`, the refusal as `cause`), not with the refusal: the lost attempt may have been written. The producer keeps its epoch and sequence, and `autoClaim` claims no epoch for it (claiming would store the record a second time under the new epoch). A refusal with no lost answer before it, and a transport failure that outlasts the attempts, reject as before. Since the recovery-text amendment (below) the rejection's message ends with the recovery for its `cause`, where it said "read the stream before sending it again" for every refusal: after a fence (`ProducerFencedError`), read the stream and send the value again only if it is absent and only under an epoch above `currentEpoch`, which a producer with `autoClaim` claims when its resend is refused (`bumpEpoch()` adds one to the producer's own epoch, which can land on the fencing writer's, where `decide_producer` answers a sequence below that writer's `duplicate: true` with no hash check); without `autoClaim`, stop using the producer id; after a seal (`409 sealed`), read the stream, which is final (a resend is refused `409` again, before the duplicate check); after any other refusal (`429`, `503`, `401`, `421`, any other `4xx`), send the same value on the same routing key through the same producer scope before any other value on that key, which the server answers `duplicate: true` if it was written and writes once if not (its row keeps only the last sequence and request hash per routing key and producer id, so a different value sent first is refused `409 producer_sequence_reused` if the lost attempt was written and is written ahead of it if not, and appends already queued on the key meet the same answer); after a `421`, through a client for the project's new endpoint, which keeps the producer's state only when made by `connect` (a `new StreamsClient({ url })` keys the scope on its `url` and starts at epoch 0, sequence 0, which the server can answer `duplicate: true` without writing). The owner ratified this rule as built on 2026-10-13 (call 7, Program item above): it is the first of the two options the review of the producer-append amendment gave (the other narrows the replay's claims and accepts the second copy that a fence with `autoClaim` stores under a new epoch), and it was chosen after X2, which ratifies the rest of this record at landing.
  - `retry: { transport: false }` sends every request once on a transport failure, as before.
  - The consumer iterator and `watch.subscribe()` pull or wait again after such a failure, until their signal aborts or `return()` is called: after 1 s, doubling to at most 5 s, back to 1 s after a success; `retry: { transport: false }` does not change this. Every other error ends them as before (`421`/`wrong_cell`, `401` after the refresh, `403`, `404`, a `503` marked `retryable: false`), and a failed settlement still ends the consumer iterator. A watch reconnection mints a fresh capability, and so does each replay of a `Watch.wait` (a review fix: the replay used to resend the capability minted for the first attempt, which a wait parked on a silently dead connection outlives, since `fetch` gives up on the headers only after the runtime's timeout, 300 s in Node, against the capability's 240 s; the server refuses an expired capability `403` `watch_unauthorized`, which is permanent and ended `watch.subscribe()`).
  - Aborting a `watch.subscribe()` signal ends the iterator (`done: true`) instead of rejecting with the abort reason, as `Stream.subscribe()` already did.
- **Retry semantics:** The SDK replays a transport failure only for requests whose replay the server answers without a second effect: a create (idempotent `PUT`), reads, a seal (an exact replay answers `200`), a consumer's create, configuration read and delete, a pull (a lease a lost answer took expires after `visibilityMs` and is delivered again, as when the caller pulls again today), a watch wait, and a producer append (the server deduplicates on producer id, epoch and sequence: a replay of an append that landed that reaches the duplicate check is answered `200` with `duplicate: true`, `count: 0` and the original cursor, and stores nothing, while a replay refused before that check (a fence by another writer of the producer id, `sealed`, a quota) rejects with `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`, on which `autoClaim` claims no epoch and whose message names the recovery for the refusal (After, above); the producer saves its next sequence once, after the answer, and its per-routing-key queue holds the scope's later appends, epoch bumps and seals until the replay settles), and a settle (the committer checks each token's lease generation and counts a decision for a lease already settled, or no longer leased, as `stale`, never as an error: triage D2; its one second effect: a retry or an extend the lost attempt applied keeps its lease and generation, so its replay applies it again and moves that lease's deadline by up to the replay's wait). `retryable` is unchanged on every error. The budget is not enlarged: the transport replay and the `429`/`503` replay stop at the fourth attempt whatever the mix, and a `401` refreshes the token once whatever the attempt, as before, so a request makes at most five attempts (three transport failures and a `401`, then the refreshed token's attempt). A settle the SDK replays after a retryable `429`/`503` (as before) or, since the settle amendment, after a transport failure reports an ack its first attempt applied as `stale`, so no record is acknowledged twice, and a message a replayed retry dead-letters is copied once (`dlq_and_settle`'s producer names the message, `src/application/consumer/delivery.rs`); a retry or an extend its first attempt applied is applied again (counted `retried`/`extended`, its deadline set from the replay's time) unless a pull delivered the message again in between, which changes the lease's generation (then `stale`). The README says so (it said, before the review of the settle amendment, that a replay never applies a decision twice, which held for acks only). Every `PullBatch.settle()` call shares the batch's one settlement, replays included.
- **Who is affected:** Every SDK user: a transport failure surfaces up to about 7 s later, or not at all when a replay succeeds, which is the purpose (a server deploy or restart). A caller that relied on the consumer iterator or `watch.subscribe()` ending at a transport failure (to restart it itself) now finds it still running, and a caller that caught the abort reason from `watch.subscribe()` now sees it end. Callers whose `fetch` failures are configuration can set `retry: { transport: false }` for the single requests. A producer whose append meets a transport failure now holds its routing key's later operations for up to about 7 s while the append is replayed, and gets the append's answer (possibly `duplicate: true`) instead of a `StreamsTransportError` it would have retried with the same sequence itself; when the server refuses the replay (a fence by another writer, a seal, a quota) it gets `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` with the refusal as `cause`, where its own retry met that refusal itself (and, for a fence with `autoClaim`, stored the record again under a new epoch); since the recovery-text amendment the error's message says how to settle the outcome for that refusal, where it said "read the stream before sending it again" for every refusal, which after a quota, a `503`, a `401` or a `421` led a caller who found the record to send a new value and meet `409 producer_sequence_reused` at that and every later append on the key until `bumpEpoch()`. A consumer whose settlement meets a transport failure gets the replay's answer, in which an ack the lost attempt applied counts as `stale` rather than `acked` and a retry or an extend it applied is applied again (its redelivery or visibility deadline later than the first attempt set it, by the time between the two attempts), and on a dead network the iterator's cleanup (`return()`, a `break`) takes about 7 s longer before it rejects with the settlement failure (triage K3's trade: fewer batches lost to a deploy). Not the server, the raw surface, raw HTTP clients or plain appends.
- **Deployment comparison:** `retry: { transport: false }` per client restores the single requests' behaviour; the loops' reconnection has no switch (triage D5).
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/restart-resilience.test.mjs (new; mocked `fetch`, every backoff run at once with its requested delay recorded, or the first timer of a delay withheld): `metadata` replays one transport failure after 1000 ms; with `retry: { transport: false }` it is one request and `StreamsTransportError`; four transport failures are four requests with waits 1000, 2000, 4000 and the last failure as `StreamsTransportError`; a transport failure, a retryable `503` (`Retry-After: 0`), a transport failure and a `200` are four requests and a success with waits 1000, 0, 4000; the same with a final `503` is that `503`'s `StreamsError`; (added by a review fix, pins) three transport failures and a `401`, then a `200` or a transport failure, are five requests, the fifth with the refreshed token, waits 1000, 2000, 4000; twelve operations (`createStream`, `listStreams`, `metadata`, `read`, `scan`, `watches`, `seal`, `consumer()`, consumer `config` and `delete`, `pull`, watch `wait`) replay one transport failure as the identical request, and since the producer-append and settle amendments a thirteenth and a fourteenth, a producer append and `settle`, with the rows also comparing headers; six were sent once (`append`, `appendBytes`, `appendMany` as `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`; stream `delete`, a producer append and `settle` as `StreamsTransportError`), four since those amendments; an abort during a request's transport backoff ends it with the abort reason before the timer fires, with no further request; the consumer iterator yields after four pull transport failures and four retryable `503`s (nine pulls, waits 1000, 2000, 4000, 1000, 0, 0, 0, 2000); its loop's waits double to 5 s and reset after a pull (1000, 2000, 4000, 5000, 5000, 1000) under `retry: { transport: false }`; it ends after one pull at a `404`, a `503` marked `retryable: false` and a `421`; an abort during its backoff ends it at once; (added by the review fix) a `Watch.wait` whose first attempt hangs for 300 s and then fails replays with a capability minted for the replay (its expiry 240 s after the replay, where the first one's had passed; red before the fix at `+ 1791820048 - 1791820348`, the first attempt's expiry resent), and the replayed-request rows compare a watch wait's URLs without its capability; `watch.subscribe()` yields after a transport failure and a retryable `503` (waits 1000, 0), reconnects past the request's four attempts at the same cursor with a capability (waits 1000, 2000, 4000, 1000), ends at a `403` after one wait, ends (`done`) when aborted during a parked wait, and ends at once when aborted during its backoff.
  - Red on the unfixed SDK: 24 of the file's 35 tests fail; each replay row first at `Error [StreamsTransportError]: the request transport failed` (or `actual: 1, expected: 4` for the budget rows), the three abort-during-backoff rows at `+ 'settled' - 'backoff'` (no backoff to abort), the parked-wait abort at `+ error: DOMException [AbortError]: This operation was aborted`. The 11 others pass before and after: the switch row, the six sent-once rows, the four permanent-refusal rows of the two loops.
  - sdk/scripts/producer-ordering.test.mjs (mechanism `sdk-producer-order`, R20; since the review of the producer-append amendment): "a replay refused after a lost answer (...) is an unknown outcome, stored once", five rows over a server for one producer id that refuses in the product's order (a cell that no longer serves the project before the product handler, a sealed collection and a quota before the core, then a stale epoch before the duplicate check) and loses the first append's answer after committing it: a successor fences the producer at epoch 1 (with `autoClaim` and without), the collection is sealed, a quota answers every replay `429` (`Retry-After: 0`), or the cell no longer serves the project (a `421` without a body; a row a later review added). Each: the record is stored once, the append and its replays at `0/0` are the only requests (two, or four for the quota), the rejection is `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (`outcome_unknown`, `retryable: false`, the refusal's status 403, 409, 429 or 421, the exact message, since the recovery-text amendment with the recovery for its refusal) with the refusal as `cause` (a `ProducerFencedError` with `currentEpoch: 1` for the fence, a `WrongCellError` for the `421`), the producer state stays `{epoch: 0, nextSeq: 0}`, the waits are 1000 (1000, 0, 0 for the quota). Red on the amendment's commit before that fix: the `autoClaim` row at `stored once` (`2 !== 1`: the SDK claimed epoch 2 and stored the record again, resolving `duplicate: false`), the other three at `rejected as an unknown outcome, got ProducerFencedError` / `got StreamsError`, and the wrong-cell row at `got WrongCellError`; red on 520e3a15 (no producer-append replay): all five at `the append and its replays only`. Controls (hand-applied, reverted): mapping every refusal, not only one after a lost answer, fails "automatic reclaim completes within the queue before a later epoch bump" and append-outcome's "a producer append: a 408 stays the server's StreamsError"; `autoClaim` claiming on an unknown outcome whose cause is a fence fails the `autoClaim` row at `2 !== 1`; answering the wrong-cell refusal without the lost-answer flag (`classify(error, false)` at `req()`'s wrong-cell exit) fails the wrong-cell row alone, at `rejected as an unknown outcome, got WrongCellError`.
  - sdk/scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs (#147): its producer append, producer `appendMany` and `seal` rows set `retry: { transport: false }`, since `seal` now replays a transport failure; its plain-append transport rows, unchanged, pin that a plain append is not replayed.
  - unchanged and green: sdk/scripts/retry-classification.test.mjs ("applied subscription recovers from transport at its durable cursor" pins `subscribe()`'s exclusion), producer-ordering.test.mjs and consumer-cleanup.test.mjs (they pinned the producer-append and settle exclusions; each is rewritten and re-pinned by its amendment, below), token-refresh.test.mjs, credential-cancellation.test.mjs.
  - Controls (hand-applied, reverted): replaying stream `delete` fails its sent-once row; ignoring the switch fails the switch row, the `seal` row of append-outcome and the loop-backoff row; replaying `subscribe()`'s reads fails "applied subscription recovers from transport at its durable cursor"; not resetting the loop's backoff fails the loop-backoff row; rejecting on a watch abort fails the parked-wait row; a flat 1 s transport wait fails five rows; replaying producer appends or `settle` fails the two pinned tests named above and this file's sent-once row.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes and the replays repeat only requests the server answers without a second effect, within the attempt budget requests already had; the cost is a later error (at most about 7 s) and loops that keep running through a restart, which is the change's purpose. Plain appends and stream deletion are not sent again after a transport failure, as before; a producer append's replay is deduplicated by the server or, when the server refuses it before that check, rejected as an unknown outcome on which `autoClaim` claims nothing, so the replay never stores a record twice, and its producer's queue keeps the scope's order; a settle's replay acknowledges no record twice and dead-letters none twice, and applies a retry or an extend again only to move that lease's deadline by up to the replay's wait. The README's "Errors and retries" (titled "Request failures and endpoint recovery" until B5 rewrote the README) and "Consumer cleanup and cancellation" say so, and WIRE-MATRIX §4 names the policy. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled. ### #147 22bfd489, amended by 9dfa0d42, 950c215f, 8ebf37b2, 7ff142a7 — The SDK's plain appends reject an answer that leaves their outcome unknown (a transport failure, a 408, a 5xx other than 503) with AppendOutcomeUnknownError, retryable false, and the SDK never sends one again

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11: self-serve behind a Console feature flag, so the SDK is published to strangers), built as the SDK triage's item B1 (S-1, drafted there as SDK-E0; Fable 5.1, 2026-10-12, `sdk.md` and its triage), decided under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-11 to Fable 5.1, with the triage's skeptic correction K1 (S-1 is client-visible, so it carries this record and the README paragraph in the same commit). Owner question X2 (sdk O2: ratify SDK-E0, SDK-E4 and SDK-E2 at landing) was decided by the owner on 2026-10-12 as recommended (`OWNER-DECISIONS-2-2026-10-12.md`, X2: the public-beta records are ratified at landing and numbered from #141 in landing order, none held), the default this record was built on, so nothing in it changes. Owner question N1 (sdk O1, plain-append duplicates) was decided the same day: (1a) now, (1b) and F2 Option A after the beta. N1 changes nothing here (under every option the SDK does not replay these answers), but (1a) makes S-5 owed (SDK-E3, its own record): under (1a) the server answers a stranded plain append `503` `outcome_unknown` `retryable: false`, which this record's rule passes through as a plain `StreamsError` with code `outcome_unknown`, not an `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`, and a body-less edge `503` still defaults to retryable and is replayed. S-5 moves the plain append's `503` rows (and the triage's body-less `503`) into this classification, with its rows in sdk/scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs replacing the `503` pins below where they invert, and the README, CHANGELOG and WIRE-MATRIX sentence that names "a `5xx` other than `503`". The number is assigned at landing, from #141 in landing order. Ratified at landing (X2).
- **Surface:** product, client behaviour: the SDK `@prisma/streams` (`sdk/src/index.ts`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - `Stream.append` and `Stream.appendBytes` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}/records`, WIRE-MATRIX §2.7) and `Stream.appendMany` (`POST /v1/streams/{name}/records:batch`, §2.8), sent without producer headers.
  - Code: the exported class `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` and `plainAppendFailure`, which `req()` applies (its `classify` argument) to the failure that ends a plain append's request, its transport failure or the answer it gives up on, in `Stream.appendRaw` (when it carries no producer headers) and in `Stream.appendMany`. A token provider's rejection is not the append's answer and is never classified.
  - Not changed: producer appends (`Producer.append` and `Producer.appendMany`, through `Stream._producerAppend`), `seal` with or without a final record, every other request, and `req()`'s retry loop.
- **Condition:** A plain append's request ends in one of these:
  - a transport failure (`fetch` throws: a connection refused or reset, DNS, TLS, a browser's CORS or mixed-content block);
  - a `408` (the product's `AppendTimeout`, "append timed out; outcome unknown", 10 s after the enqueue, rendered `append_failed`);
  - a `500` (`append_failed`: a corrupt descriptor or a preparation mismatch, which wrote nothing, or `AppendErr::Internal` from the transaction, which may have written);
  - a `502`, a `504`, or any other `5xx` that is not `503` (an edge's or a proxy's answer, body-less or text);
  - (added by a review fix) a `2xx` whose body the SDK cannot read: not JSON (an edge's or a proxy's page), or a connection lost after the status line, mid-body.
- **Before:** Never sent again after one of these: `req()` never replayed a transport failure, a `408` or a non-`503` `5xx` (it replays a `401` once, after its token refresh, and a `429` or `503` marked or defaulted `retryable`). A transport failure rejected with `StreamsTransportError` (`status` 0, `code` `transport_error`, `retryable: true`, the thrown value in `cause`); the others with the `StreamsError` `errorFrom` built (the server's status, code, message and details; `retryable: false`; without a JSON body `http_error` and `HTTP <status>`). An unreadable `2xx` rejected with the runtime's raw `SyntaxError` or `TypeError` from `res.json()`: no `status`, `code` or `retryable`, so a catch-all retry wrote the record again.
- **After:**
  - Still never sent again after that answer, which ends the last attempt (an earlier attempt, if the SDK made one, was a `401` before its token refresh or a retryable `429` or `503`: refusals that write nothing). The rejection is `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` (exported, a `StreamsError` subclass): `status` the HTTP status, or 0 for a transport failure; `code` `outcome_unknown`; `retryable: false`; `cause` the `StreamsError` built from the answer (the server's code, message and details) or the value `fetch` threw.
  - Its message: `the append's last attempt ended in <answer>, so the SDK cannot tell whether it was written; it will not send it again; retry only if a second copy is acceptable, or append through a producer`, where `<answer>` is `a transport failure` or `HTTP <status> <code>` (for example `HTTP 408 append_failed`, `HTTP 502 http_error`).
  - An unreadable `2xx` rejects with a `StreamsError` that is not `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`: `status` the `2xx` status, `code` `unreadable_response`, `retryable: false`, the read failure as `cause`, and the message `the server accepted the append (HTTP <status>), so it was written, but its answer could not be read; do not send it again`. The server accepted the record; only its cursor is lost.
  - Unchanged for a plain append: a `429` or a `503` (replayed by `req()` while `retryable`, at most four attempts, then that `StreamsError`), a `401` (one credential refresh), `WrongCellError` (`421`, or a `503` naming `wrong_cell`), every other `4xx` `StreamsError`, an abort's reason, a token provider's rejection (the append was not sent with that token, or after a `401` the cell had refused it; whatever the provider rejected with, a `StreamsTransportError` or a `5xx` `StreamsError` included), and every success.
- **Retry semantics:** The SDK did not and does not replay any of these answers. The flag changes from `true` to `false` for a transport failure, so a generic retry loop that reads `retryable` stops retrying a plain append whose outcome is unknown; the `408` and `5xx` rows were already `retryable: false` and change class and code. A caller that retries such an append anyway may write the record twice; a producer's retry of the same sequence is deduplicated by the server (WIRE-MATRIX §2.7, the producer triple). Whether a plain append's `503` is replayed was owner question N1, decided (1a) on 2026-10-12; S-5 (SDK-E3) makes that change, not this record.
- **Who is affected:** Callers of plain appends that branch on the class (`instanceof StreamsTransportError` no longer matches a plain append's transport failure), on `code` (`transport_error`, `append_failed`, `http_error`) or on `retryable`. Not the server, the raw surface, raw HTTP clients, producers, seals, reads, consumers or watches.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting, and the SDK has no switch for it.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - sdk/scripts/append-outcome.test.mjs (new; mocked `fetch`): `append`, `appendBytes` and `appendMany`, each with a transport failure, a `408` `append_failed`, a `500` with the product body, a `502` with an empty body and a `504` with a text body (15 rows): exactly one request, the class, `status`, `code`, `retryable: false`, the exact message and the `cause`. Red on the unfixed SDK, each after exactly one request: `'StreamsTransportError' !== 'AppendOutcomeUnknownError'` for the three transport rows, `'StreamsError' !== 'AppendOutcomeUnknownError'` for the twelve status rows.
  - The same file, added by the review fix that keeps the token provider's rejection out of the classification (each red before it, at its reference-equality assertion, with `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` in place of the provider's error): for each of the three operations, a `tokenProvider` that rejects with a `StreamsTransportError`, a `StreamsError` `500` or a `StreamsError` `408` makes it reject with that very value after no request, and a `401` whose token refresh rejects with a `StreamsError` `502` makes it reject with that value after one request (12 rows).
  - The same file, added by the review fix of an unreadable `2xx`: for each of the three operations, a `200` whose body is HTML and a `200` whose body breaks off mid-stream are one request and that `StreamsError` (`status` 200, `unreadable_response`, `retryable: false`, the `SyntaxError` or `TypeError` as `cause`), 6 rows, each red before the fix at `assert.ok(error instanceof StreamsError)` (the raw `SyntaxError` or `TypeError`).
  - The same file, added by the review fix of the message (which said the append was sent once and not replayed): a retryable `503` `temporarily_unavailable` then a transport failure are two requests and `AppendOutcomeUnknownError` with `status` 0, the transport failure as `cause` and the last attempt's message. Its request count and class pin what the SDK always did; its message assertion, with the fifteen rows' message assertions, is red on the old message (`'the append was sent once and its outcome is unknown: ...' !== "the append's last attempt ended in a transport failure, ..."`).
  - The same file's pins, green before and after: a retryable `503` `temporarily_unavailable` then `200`, and a `429` then `200`, are two requests and a success for each of the three operations; four retryable `503`s are four requests and that retryable `StreamsError`; a `421` is `WrongCellError`; a `400` is the server's `StreamsError`; a producer `append`'s and `appendMany`'s and `seal`'s transport failure stays `StreamsTransportError`; a producer append's `408` stays the server's `StreamsError`.
  - Controls (hand-applied, reverted): classifying a `503` too fails the four-`503` pin; classifying producer appends fails the three producer pins; the `StreamsTransportError` wrapper as `cause` fails the three transport rows; classifying every refusal but `429` and `503` fails the `400` pin.
  - unchanged: sdk/scripts/retry-classification.test.mjs (its "ordinary 429/503 retries" use `metadata()`), sdk/scripts/producer-ordering.test.mjs.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer of the server changes and no request is sent more or fewer times; only the SDK's error class, code and, for a transport failure, `retryable` flag change, on answers that leave a plain append's outcome unknown, and `retryable: false` states what the SDK already did. A caller that caught `StreamsTransportError` around a plain append no longer catches it there (the `0.3.0-beta.1` CHANGELOG lists it as breaking, triage item B5). The README's "Errors and retries" (titled "Request failures and endpoint recovery" until B5 rewrote the README) says so, and WIRE-MATRIX §4 names the SDK's plain-append policy. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the suite, CI's `sdk-package` smokes (Node 18 and 22, Bun, Deno, through a real server) and the platform e2e; the new file passes under Node 18.20, 22.15 and 24.18, and `npm test` under Node 22. No Rust file changes, so no mutation leg is selected and no formal receipt is staled. Ratified at landing under the owner's X2 decision of 2026-10-12.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change, from the SDK triage's B1 spec. Not checked by an independent pass.

### #150 84985808 — The interim token issuer answers `GET /healthz` (200 while it can mint, else 503 with the reason) and, behind its metrics bearer, `GET /v1/admin/metrics` (its counters, its state copy's age, the bundle's version, the admission gate and the offboarding job's backlog), the routes the watch polls

- **Program item:** Public beta (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-11, answers (1) and (9)), built as the issuer triage's item B2.9 (Fable 5.1, 2026-10-11), under the owner's answers of 2026-10-12 (he accepted every recommended answer of the public-beta calls); the alerting triage's rows 21, 27 and 28 bind these key names (its D5: "the JSON key names of `/v1/admin/metrics` are not fixed yet ... bind the names when the issuer's B2 lands"). Ratified at landing by the owner's answer X2 of 2026-10-12 ("ratify all at landing; hold none"), and given its number then, in landing order from #141.
- **Surface:** operator-debug, on a new service: the interim issuer (`deploy/issuer`). No answer of the server changes.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /healthz` and `GET /v1/admin/metrics` at the issuer's origin. Code: `Ops` (`deploy/issuer/ops.ts`), routed by `Issuer.fetch` (`deploy/issuer/server.ts`); another method answers 405 `method_not_allowed` with `Allow: GET`.
- **Condition:** Every request to either route.
- **Before:** No such service.
- **After:**
  - `GET /healthz`, unauthenticated: 200 `{"status":"ok"}` while the issuer's copy of the cell's state was revalidated within 300 s and the cell's keys feed holds the issuer's signing key; else 503 `{"status":"unavailable","reason":"state_stale"}` or `{"status":"unavailable","reason":"key_not_in_state"}`, exactly when the exchange answers 503 `issuer_unavailable` (#149). It names no id.
  - `GET /v1/admin/metrics` with `Authorization: Bearer <STREAMS_ISSUER_METRICS_TOKEN>` (compared as sha256 digests in constant time): 200, flat JSON, `Cache-Control: no-store`: `cell_id`, `kid`, `uptime_secs`, `healthy`, `cache_age_secs` (whole seconds since the last revalidation that succeeded; the exchange refuses past 300), `cache_fresh`, `state_feed_version`, `published_feed_version` (the bundle's as the issuer last saw it, null before its first look), `gate_open` and `gate_n_max` (the state's admission gate), `profile_ok` (whether the profile compiled into the issuer is the one `cell-admin init` recorded; false makes every project create answer 409 `beta_at_capacity` while `/healthz` stays 200, so the watch reads it here), `exchanges` (since boot, by outcome: `issued`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_credential`, `credential_not_active`, `project_not_active`, `rate_limited`, `issuer_unavailable`), `rate_limit_refusals` (since boot, by bucket), `revalidation_failures`, `republishes`, `offboarding_projects` and `offboarding_max_attempts` (from the state: the projects being offboarded, which the offboarding job drains, #151, and the most failed attempts any of their drains has recorded; from 7 on the job retries that drain hourly, so a value that keeps rising is a drain that does not finish), `rehash_pending`, `live_credentials_by_pepper` (active credentials with a secret, by pepper version: when only the newest remains, the owner may drop the older peppers). Without the bearer, or with another: 401 `unauthorized` "send Authorization: Bearer <the metrics token>" with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="streams-issuer"`.
- **Retry semantics:** None: the watch polls (`/healthz` every 15 s, the metrics every 60 s, alerting triage); a 503 from `/healthz` is the condition it pages on (row 21: two minutes).
- **Who is affected:** The owner and the watch. No customer.
- **Pinning tests:** deploy/issuer/ops.test.ts: "is 200 while the issuer can mint, 503 with the reason while it cannot" (a state copy 301 s old; `keys add --retire-others`; `POST /healthz` 405 `Allow: GET`); "answers only the metrics bearer" (none, wrong, one character longer, without `Bearer `); "reports the counters, the copy's age, the bundle's version and the admission gate" (every key and value after two issued and one refused exchange, 42 s on; `gate_open` false after `cell-admin gate --close`); "counts the projects being offboarded and the most attempts any of their drains has failed" (against the fake cell: three projects offboarded by `cell-admin offboard`, one drained by the job, the other two failing one and two attempts).
