### #83 c5791119 — The fleet's desired count has no assumed-capacity dimension: SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY is not an option

- **Program item:** NEXT-WORK §13, package 5 of `config-simplification.md` (switches with one live path), its third row. Owner answer of 2026-09-29: "For other questions, please make your own judgement call." The answer contains no explicit approval of this package; the removal was made on that delegation. The audit of the setting (`evidence/config-audit-2026-09-29/detail.md`, `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY`) put two questions to the owner; both are answered here by the implementer and are listed under "For the owner" below.
- **Surface:** process
- **Endpoint:** No product, raw or fleet-internal route. Process startup: the command-line argument `--scale-rps-capacity`, the environment name `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY`, `--help`. In a fleet (`FLEET_PREFIX` set): the string `reason` of the fleet document `fleet/desired.json`, which the log line "fleet desired A -> B (reason)" repeats. Operator: `GET /operator/data.json` (bearer-gated) returns that document as it is stored, as `fleet.desired`, so its member `reason` carries the changed string; `GET /operator/runbook` serves the RUNBOOK.md that is compiled into the binary, whose §3.5 loses the row of the setting.
- **Condition:** A process passes the argument or holds the environment name; or a fleet instance publishes a desired count.
- **Before:** The option was parsed (default 0 = dimension off). With a value C above 0 the fleet controller computed `need_rps = ceil(total rps / max(1, target utilisation x C))` from the rates the live heartbeats report, and the desired count was at least that; the shrink target had the same floor, so the fleet did not shrink below it. With the default of 0 `need_rps` was 0 and took part in neither maximum. The reason string ended `rps=R (need_rps) live=L`, for example `rps=0 (0) live=2`.
- **After:**
  - The argument is not declared: a process that passes it does not start (clap `UnknownArgument`, exit status 2, before any side effect). `--help` loses the entry.
  - The environment name is not read. A process that holds it starts as a process that does not, whatever the value; nothing is logged.
  - The desired count is the maximum over utilisation, edge slots, the hot instance, ack latency and edge latency, clamped to `FLEET_MAX` and floored by `FLEET_MIN`, as it was for every process with the default. The measured rate is still summed: it gates the edge-latency dimension (at least 5 requests per second) and is printed.
  - The reason string ends `rps=R live=L`: the token `(need_rps)` between the two is gone. Every other token keeps its place and form.
  - Unchanged, and now a constant: the boot line "fleet coordination on (prefix=P, cap=0 rps)" still prints `cap=0 rps`. The startup summary never held the value (it excludes the clap-owned settings). `bootstrap::run` names the field in that line, and the function is frozen by its exception rows, so the field stays in `CliArgs` with `#[arg(skip)]`.
- **Retry semantics:** None.
- **Who is affected:** Operators of a fleet. Nothing in the repository sets the name: no profile, family, rig, test or deploy script (`git grep`; the mentions outside `src` were the RUNBOOK §3.5 row, which said to leave it off, COMPUTE-SPEC §4 and the dated experiment records). On Compute the supervisor passes only `--listen`, so no Compute deployment passes the argument. A Compute project keeps every name it was ever given: a project that still holds `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY=150` from pilot run 5 has the dimension today and loses it on its next deploy without a message; it then scales on the five measured dimensions only. That run is the incident that retired the dimension (it scaled out at about 5% utilisation on a constant that described a slower engine). Whether such a project exists is visible only in the platform export (NEXT-WORK §11), which has not been run. A reader of the reason string that splits it by position finds one token fewer at the end. In the repository `bench/fleet/observe-fleet.py` reads the string and copies it verbatim; the server itself relays the whole document, `reason` included, in `/operator/data.json` (`operator_snapshot`, `src/fleet/repository.rs`; `src/operator.rs`), and the compiled-in operator page reads only `fleet.desired.instances`.
- **Given up:** the ability to make the fleet scale on an assumed capacity in requests per second without a source change.
- **Deployment comparison:** the pin of HEAD's leaves in `scripts/effective-config` stays 140 and `rename-map.json` does not change: the leaf `cli.scale_rps_capacity` remains and is 0 in every family, as before. The tool itself was not run (it builds rc.4 and HEAD); its unit tests were.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/fleet_controller.rs::an_unreadable_router_report_defers_only_the_desired_publication (gains one call of the new helper `assert_reason_ends_with_rate_and_live`, which holds that the last two tokens of the published reason are named `live` and `rps`; red-first: `the reason ends with the measured rate and the live count: cores_used=0.03 util->1 inflight=300 slots->3 hot_cpu=0% (0) ack_p50=0ms (0) edge_p50=0ms (0) rps=0 (0) live=2`, left `(Some("live"), Some("(0)"))`, right `(Some("live"), Some("rps"))`)
  - src/config/retired_tests.rs::a_retired_flag_on_argv_is_refused (the table gains the argument; red-first: `("--scale-rps-capacity", Ok(()))` on the left)
  - src/config/retired_tests.rs::a_retired_name_in_the_environment_changes_nothing with its helper `retired_names_helper` (the child process holds `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY=150` and the compared values gain `cli.scale_rps_capacity`; red-first: 150 on the left, 0 on the right)
  - src/config/tests.rs::cli_surface_is_pinned (loses the row; red-first with the option still declared: `("scale-rps-capacity", "SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY", "0")` in left only)
  - src/config/tests.rs::cli_fixture_matches_scrubbed_parse
  - Not pinned: that no rate can raise the desired count or hold the shrink target. The field and the computation are deleted, so no configuration can express the dimension and no test can set it; the pin is the reason string, which can only name the needs that exist. The values of `rps=` and `live=` are not asserted, only the names of the two tokens.
- **Residue:** the field `CliArgs::scale_rps_capacity` (always 0) and `cap=0 rps` in the boot line, for the change in which the owner next updates the exception rows of `bootstrap::run` (with the residue of edge record #80, so that TLA-011 and the bootstrap mutation owner are paid once). Removed on 2026-09-30 on the owner's instruction ("Please do the cleanup"), together with the residue of #80: the field is gone, the boot line reads "fleet coordination on (prefix=P)", and the rows of `bootstrap::run` were updated (`scope_lines` 583 -> 573, `syntax_facts` 977 -> 968); `cli.scale_rps_capacity` is declared as removed in `rename-map.json`. The comment in `src/fleet/heartbeat.rs` that names `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY` is history and still true; it is not edited, which keeps the `fleet_heartbeat` mutation owner out of this change.
- **For the owner:**
  1. The audit asked whether one option is worth an update of the `bootstrap::run` rows, a TLA-011 re-record and a fleet mutation leg, or should ride with the next change to those files. It was taken here without the rows: `bootstrap.rs` is not edited, TLA-011 goes stale through `src/fleet.rs` (12.1 min to re-record), and CI selects the `fleet` mutation owner and Miri.
  2. The audit asked: remove outright, or accept and ignore with a notice. Removed outright, as edge records #74, #80 and #81 did.
  3. Whether a live Compute project still holds `SCALE_RPS_CAPACITY` above 0; the platform export answers it before the binary is deployed.
- **Risk reason:** low: no route, status, code, header or field of an answer changes; the value of one string in the operator payload, `fleet.desired.reason` of `/operator/data.json`, loses a token. The default was off, and no deployment in the repository set the name. The risks are a start that is refused for a process that still passes the argument, and a fleet that silently loses a scale-out floor it still holds; the only recorded use of that floor is the incident that retired it. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the library suite, the release profile, the rigs that start the binary (the platform e2e among them), the effective-configuration comparison, Miri and the mutation leg of the `fleet` owner (both selected by CI for this change), and the re-record of TLA-011. WIRE-MATRIX needs no edit: its entry for `/operator/data.json` names the member `desired`, not the layout of `reason`, and the fleet document keeps its fields and their types. RATIFIED by the owner on 2026-09-30.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change. An independent review of 2026-09-29 corrected this record in three places: "Endpoint" said "None on the wire" and now names `GET /operator/data.json`, which relays the fleet document; "Who is affected" called `bench/fleet/observe-fleet.py` the only reader of the string in the repository and now names the server's relay; "Risk reason" said that no answer on the wire and no body changes. ### #84 ad4953fa — The history compactor is always on: HISTORY_COMPACTOR is not read

- **Program item:** NEXT-WORK §13, package 5 of `config-simplification.md` (switches with one live path), its fourth row. Owner answer of 2026-09-29: "For other questions, please make your own judgement call." The answer contains no explicit approval of this package; the removal was made on that delegation. The audit of the setting (`evidence/config-audit-2026-09-29/detail.md`, `HISTORY_COMPACTOR`) put one question to the owner and named one thing it could not determine; both are listed under "For the owner" below.
- **Surface:** process
- **Endpoint:** None on the wire. Process startup: the environment name `HISTORY_COMPACTOR` (it never had a command-line argument, so clap's surface and `--help` do not change), and the key `history.compactor_off` of the startup summary (a log line).
- **Condition:** A process holds `HISTORY_COMPACTOR=off`. Any other value, and an absent name, meant "on" before and mean nothing now.
- **Before:**
  - Without `MEMPROFILE_CERT`: the process started without a message. Every history database (the per-stream layout and the shared partitions of layout 2) was opened with no embedded compactor (`compactor_options: None`) and with L0 caps of 1,000,000 (`l0_max_ssts`, `l0_max_ssts_per_key`), so its L0 files were never consolidated and a flush never waited for compaction.
  - With `MEMPROFILE_CERT=compute-1g`, which the 1 GiB profile sets for every Compute family: the process refused to start, with `MEMPROFILE_CERT: history_v1 settings disable the compactor` and the same line for `history_v2`.
  - The startup summary printed `history.compactor_off`, `false` in every deployment of the repository.
- **After:**
  - The environment name is not read. A process that holds it starts as a process that does not, whatever the value; nothing is logged.
  - Every history database is opened with the embedded compactor on the worker options the engine resolved (by default one compaction at a time, polled every 2.5 s, 32 MiB output SSTs) and with L0 caps of 64: what every process without the name already ran.
  - A process that holds `HISTORY_COMPACTOR=off` together with `MEMPROFILE_CERT=compute-1g` starts, where it was refused.
  - The startup summary has no key `history.compactor_off`.
  - Unchanged: the guard of the certificate (`settings disable the compactor`) stays, because `compactor_options` is still an `Option` in SlateDB's `Settings`; no configuration reaches it for the history families now.
- **Retry semantics:** None.
- **Who is affected:** Nobody in the repository: no profile, family, rig, bench, test, workflow or deploy script sets the name (`git grep`; outside `src` it appeared only in the review documents). The effective-configuration evidence of 2026-09-24 shows `history.compactor_off` false in all 12 families on both sides. A Compute project keeps every name it was ever given: a certified project that holds `HISTORY_COMPACTOR=off` cannot be running today (its start is refused) and would start on its next deploy; an uncertified process that holds it gets the compactor back without a message. Whether such a project exists is visible only in the platform export (NEXT-WORK §11), which has not been run. A reader of the startup summary that expects the key finds it absent; nothing in the repository reads it.
- **Given up:** the bench hook for discard-mode runs. `s3lite --discard-substr` drops the bodies of matching PUTs; the switch existed so that history SSTs whose bodies were dropped were never read again by a compactor. With this binary such a run compacts history L0 files and fails when it reads a discarded body (read from the code: the emulator answers a GET of a discarded body with 500; no such run was made). No script pairs the two; a discard-mode benchmark of the history path now needs a source change. The help of `s3lite --discard-substr` still offered the mode for "an unbounded history tier" after this commit; it now says that the mode is not for the server's history databases.
- **Deployment comparison:** `history.compactor_off` is declared as a removed leaf in `scripts/effective-config/rename-map.json`, with its proposal in `proposed.json`; the pin of HEAD's leaves goes from 140 to 139. The tool itself was not run (it builds rc.4 and HEAD); its unit tests were.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/config/retired_tests.rs::the_history_compactor_cannot_be_switched_off (new; with `HISTORY_COMPACTOR=off` loaded, `history_settings` and `history2_settings` both return L0 caps of 64 and compactor options of 2,500 ms, one compaction and 32 MiB output SSTs; red-first: left `((1000000, 1000000, None), (1000000, 1000000, None))`, right `((64, 64, Some((2500, 1, Some(33554432)))), (64, 64, Some((2500, 1, Some(33554432)))))`)
  - src/config/retired_tests.rs::retired_environment_names_change_nothing (the table gains `("HISTORY_COMPACTOR", "off")`; red-first: the two configurations differ in `compactor_off: true` on the left, `compactor_off: false` on the right)
  - src/config/tests.rs::default_values_are_pinned (loses the assertion on the removed field)
  - scripts/effective-config/test_effective_config.py::PinTest::test_new_leaf_pin_is_the_source_field_count (red-first after the field was removed and before the pin was lowered: `AssertionError: 139 != 140`)
  - Not pinned: the absence of the key from the startup summary. The field is deleted, so the summary cannot name it.
- **For the owner:**
  1. The audit asked for approval to delete a bench hook that discard-mode benchmarks may still want. It is deleted here; see "Given up".
  2. The audit asked for approval of the re-record of three receipts. `src/history.rs` feeds TLA-016, TLA-018 and TLA-019 (103.8 min serial). All three were stale on the branch before this change, through the removal of the gather pacing (edge record #81) and the changes under `src/shard`, so this change adds no receipt to the re-record that is already due.
  3. The audit could not determine whether a Compute project still holds the name; the platform export answers it before the binary is deployed.
- **Risk reason:** low: no answer on the wire changes, the compactor was on by default, no deployment in the repository turned it off, and a certified deployment could not. The risk is an uncertified process that relied on the switch and now compacts; nothing in the repository is one. Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the library suite, the release profile, the rigs that start the binary, the effective-configuration comparison, and the re-record of TLA-016, TLA-018 and TLA-019. CI selects neither a mutation leg nor Miri for the files of this change. WIRE-MATRIX has no entry (no route, status, code, header or body changes). RATIFIED by the owner on 2026-09-30.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change. An independent review of 2026-09-29 found no false statement in this record. It found that the commit left the help text of `s3lite --discard-substr` (`src/bin/s3lite.rs`) advertising the use that "Given up" says is gone; the help is corrected and "Given up" says so.

### #87 9f25cf96 — A billing close or retention flag that the tombstone walk or the closure-debt pass enqueues on a shard it opened is applied: the pass keeps the shard until its committer has applied it

- **Program item:** NEXT-WORK §2, the finding recorded there as unconfirmed ("a close enqueued on an engine the walk cold-opened may be dropped when `walk_settle` retires that engine before the committer applies it"). An independent investigation (three analysts, three skeptics, one judge) confirmed it at 88015cc5. Made on the owner's instruction of 2026-09-30 ("Do them all in that order! use your own judgement").
- **Surface:** both
- **Endpoint:** No request changes. What changes: the storage billed for a stream incarnation that ended while its billing row was acknowledged clean (expired or hard-deleted and closed by the tombstone walk, or replaced and closed by the closure-debt pass): `GET /v1/streams/{name}/usage[?month=][&streamId=]` (`storageByteSeconds`, `ownedStoredBytesNow`, `status`, `effective`, `correctionTotals`, `correctionList`) and `GET /v1/projects/{project}/usage[?month=]` (`effective`, `correctionTotals`); the `_usage` ledger's closing snapshot of that row and the rollup's monthly and correction objects built from it. For a soft-deleted source its forks still read, the `retained_by_forks` flag on its row and snapshots. Operator: a shard the walk or the debt pass enqueued an op on stays a scheduler-held resident until the next sweep (`sweep_custody_prefixes`, the sweep's resident budget); `WALK_CLOSE_SUBMITS` still counts enqueues, and each is now applied.
- **Condition:** The walk (`src/billing/walk.rs` `walk_segment`) or the debt pass (`src/billing/replaced.rs` `settle_segment`) cold-opens a shard for a segment, finds its incarnation's row with an open gauge (or, for the walk, a soft-deleted source's row without the retention flag), enqueues the close (or the flag), and the shard holds no durable debt: no dirty row, no month final, no maintenance backlog, no trim debt. These are the rows the two passes exist for: acknowledged clean, then ended with nothing observing it (an idle expiry, a recreation over an idle-expired incarnation, a close lost to a crash or a full queue). Whether the committer applied the op before the retirement depended on whether the probe's scans yielded to it, which depends on the SST layout at the top of the shard's keyspace; on a layout where they do not, the op was lost on every visit. In production a lone op waits in no gather (`pace_min_reqs` 32), so the loss was a race; the pinning tests make it certain with a committer that gathers for 2 s.
- **Before:** Right after the enqueue the pass settled the shard (`walk_settle`). The settle's debt probe reads only the durable dirty index, which a queued op has not written, so it retired the engine, and the retiring committer dropped the op without a reply, a log line or a counter (the drain arm of `committer_loop`, `reject_op`, or `CommitTransaction::run` on a closed engine). The row stayed byte for byte as it was: gauge open, accounted-through at the last observation, no new version, no dirty marker. The drain emitted nothing, and every month the rollup closed carried the dead incarnation's gauge onto that month's invoice: storage billed for a stream that no longer existed. A later visit re-submitted the close at the same persisted instant: the debt pass when its cursor came back to the debt (the next sweep while the debts fit one page), the walk only after its cursor went round the whole cell catalog (ceil(N/256) sweeps of 300 s), and on a layout where the probe never yields every visit lost it again. A close that finally landed closed at the persisted instant, and the late-close path (#66) corrected the months already invoiced: the final amount was exact, but the carried months needed corrections. A lost retention flag left a soft-deleted source's row unflagged until a later visit; its gauge kept billing, but the flag that carries the fork billing contract across restarts and ownership moves was missing from the row.
- **After:** A step that enqueued a close or a retention flag keeps the shard. It stays scheduler-held, its committer applies the op (a close zeroes the gauge at the persisted instant, takes one version and marks the row dirty for the drain), and the next sweep's phase 1 keeps it as an indebted resident while the drain acknowledges the row, or evicts it with the debt durable. A step that enqueued nothing (no row, another incarnation's row, a closed gauge, a failed read or submit) hands the shard back as before. A close bills what it would have billed whenever it landed: the persisted instant, not the time it ran. A walk that closes on many distinct cold shards keeps up to the sweep's resident budget (`sweep_maint_resident`, default 2) of them and defers the rest to the next sweep, the pace it already had whenever the applied close was visible to the probe.
- **Retry semantics:** None at the HTTP level. The passes still re-submit a close they find open, at the same persisted instant, and the committer still skips a close that would change nothing (#72).
- **Who is affected:** Customers whose streams expired, were hard-deleted or were replaced while their rows were clean: storage is no longer billed past the close instant for the months until a revisit, and no correction is needed for months already invoiced. Invoice consumers: fewer negative storage corrections from late closes (#66). Operators: a sweep may keep up to its resident budget of such shards one sweep longer. No status, code, header or body shape changes.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/billing_walk_custody.rs::a_close_the_walk_submits_on_a_shard_it_opened_is_applied_before_the_shard_is_handed_back (new, red-first in 5 of 5 runs: `the walk handed back the shard it opened before its committer applied the close it enqueued there`, left `(81, 1790772820470, 0, (2026, 9), 1)`, right `(0, 1790772820529, 4779, (2026, 9), 2)`)
  - src/dst/tests/billing_walk_custody.rs::a_close_the_debt_pass_submits_on_a_shard_it_opened_is_applied_before_the_shard_is_handed_back (new, red-first in 5 of 5 runs: `the debt pass handed back the shard it opened before its committer applied the close it enqueued there`, left `(81, 1790772812887, 0, (2026, 9), 1)`, right `(0, 1790772812950, 5103, (2026, 9), 2)`)
  - src/dst/tests/billing_walk_custody.rs::a_retention_flag_the_walk_submits_on_a_shard_it_opened_is_applied_before_the_shard_is_handed_back (new, red-first in 5 of 5 runs: `the walk handed back the shard it opened before its committer applied the retention flag it enqueued there`, left `(false, 1)`, right `(true, 2)`)
  - unchanged and green: ::a_shard_the_walk_opened_for_nothing_to_close_is_handed_back_before_the_next_segment (30 of 30 runs alone; its CI flake, gauge 81 still open with accounted-through 55 ms before the expiry, matches this race), and the `billing_closure_debts`, `billing_closure_owners`, `billing_controller` and `runtime_sweep` DSTs and the `billing::` unit tests.
- **Risk reason:** low: no status, code, header or body shape changes and no stored format changes; the only billed figures that change are storage past a close instant that a lost op left open, which the late-close corrections reversed once the close landed. WIRE-MATRIX has no entry: no wire surface changes. What remains: phase 1 still decides from the durable index, so an op still unapplied a whole sweep interval later would meet the same drop, and the exact fix (a reply on the committer op) is for the owner (NEXT-WORK §2). Not run for this record: `scripts/gate.sh`, the release profile, the mutation legs of the `billing_walk` and `billing_replaced` owners (selected by CI for this change) and the platform e2e rigs. Made on the owner's instruction of 2026-09-30 ("Do them all in that order! use your own judgement"); RATIFIED by the owner on 2026-10-01.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #163 1c04936b — The server listens with an accept queue of 1,024 connections, not 128, so a burst of up to 1,024 simultaneous connects is queued whole instead of having its SYNs past the 129th dropped

- **Program item:** Public beta, round 5 of the r4-rust lane: the Linux-only flake of `dst::dst_tests::shared_cell_hostile::a_capability_flood_never_starves_the_victims_watch`, whose 256 simultaneous connects met the 128-connection accept queue Tokio binds with (through mio, the standard library's value). Ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17. Numbered #163 at landing-4 (2026-10-17), in landing order from #160, the next free number at slate 5b639a55.
- **Surface:** both: every connection to the one listener, product, raw, operator and fleet-internal routes alike. No status, code, header or body changes.
- **Endpoint:**
  - The listener `bootstrap::run` binds (`tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(&config.cli.listen)`, unchanged) and hands to `serve_h1` (`src/http/serve.rs`).
  - Code: `serve_h1` passes it through `with_accept_backlog` before its first accept: the same socket, as an unconnected `std::net::TcpStream` into `tokio::net::TcpSocket::from_std_stream`, listens again with `ACCEPT_BACKLOG` = 1,024 and is registered with the runtime as a listener. listen(2) on a listening socket changes only its queue length: the address, `SO_REUSEADDR` and the connections already queued are kept. No unsafe code, no new dependency, and `bootstrap::run`, whose six exception-growth rows freeze it, is unchanged.
- **Condition:** more simultaneous connects than the accept queue holds before the accept loop takes them: a client fleet reconnecting at once after a deploy or a network blip, a burst of new connections under load, a hostile flood.
- **Before:** the queue held 129 connections (Linux: backlog + 1). A connect past them had its SYN dropped, so the client completed no sooner than its 1 s initial retransmit (then 3 s, 7 s while the burst lasted). In the pinning test, 383 of 512 simultaneous connects took 1.02 s or more.
- **After:** the queue holds up to 1,024 connections (Linux caps the request at `net.core.somaxconn`, 4,096 by default since 5.4 and on Ubuntu 24.04; a host set lower gets its own cap). All 512 of the test's connects complete inside a second and each is answered `200`. A burst past 1,024 meets the same SYN drops as before, past the new line. macOS caps every backlog at `kern.ipc.somaxconn` (128 by default), so development hosts see no change. Each queued connection costs the kernel its socket until the accept loop takes it; the accept loop, the drain floor and the admission bounds that follow are unchanged.
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged in form. Fewer connects wait out a TCP retransmit during a burst; nothing a client retries at the HTTP layer changes.
- **Who is affected:** clients connecting in bursts of more than 129 to one instance: they connect at once instead of 1 s or more later. No one else.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting; 1,024 is a constant. Prisma Compute's kernel cap (`net.core.somaxconn`) bounds it; at 4,096 it is not reached.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/http/serve.rs::tests::a_connect_burst_past_the_default_backlog_is_queued_whole (new, Linux only: one request served first, then 512 connects sent in one poll of a single-threaded runtime, so the accept loop takes none of them before the last SYN is sent; every connect completes inside 1 s and every request is answered `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`. Red on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.17, 4 CPUs, somaxconn 4096; release binary of the tree without the `with_accept_backlog` call): `383 of 512 connects took a second or more, the slowest Some(1.016583692s): the accept queue dropped their SYNs`. Green three runs of three. Ignored off Linux: macOS completes the loopback handshake after the connect returns, so the burst never fills the queue there and the test passes on both trees, measuring nothing. Since landing-5 it skips with a message under a soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` below 1,280, the descriptors the burst holds plus room, instead of failing on `connect: Too many open files`)
  - src/http/serve.rs::tests::listening_again_keeps_the_address_and_a_queued_connection (new, named `listening_with_the_deeper_queue_keeps_the_address_and_the_queue` until landing-5, which named it for what it checks: a connection queued before `with_accept_backlog` is the one the re-listened socket accepts next, at the same address; it does not check the queue's depth)
  - unchanged and green: `http::serve::` (16 on Linux, 15 and the ignored one on macOS) and `dst::dst_tests::shared_cell_hostile::a_capability_flood_never_starves_the_victims_watch` on Linux (the release binary above, alone).
- **Risk reason:** low: no response changes; connects that were delayed by a second or more now complete, and the kernel holds up to 1,024 queued connections per instance instead of 129. Not run for this record: the full Linux suite, the `http_serve` mutation leg, Miri and any field run; no formal receipt covers `src/http/serve.rs`.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change. The lane's earlier attempt deepened the queue with an `unsafe` `libc::listen`; it was replaced by the safe re-listen above and never committed.

### #164 4d374446 — A metrics point the ledger refuses is kept and sent again at the next drain round, so a shed while an instance drains no longer loses an `_ops_metrics` point

- **Program item:** Public beta, the owner's round-6 decisions of 2026-10-15 (`OWNER-DECISIONS-6-2026-10-15.md`), call 16 (Q0 A2): "no shed at idle" counts client requests only, the acceptance text reports the lost `_ops_metrics` points (0-2 per run), and retrying them is an engineering follow-up. This record is that follow-up. Q0's six runs refused 1-4 of the server's own appends each in the drain window after load end ("instance memory pressure"); `_usage` and `_audit_events` were retried from their outbox and requeue at the next 8 s round, but each refused `_ops_metrics` point was gone. Ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17. Numbered #164 at landing-4 (2026-10-17), in landing order from #160, the next free number at slate 5b639a55.
- **Surface:** operator-debug: the `_ops_metrics` ledger and what the ops rollup takes from it (its raw tier and minute tier). No status, code, header or body of any request changes, and no usage answer changes.
- **Endpoint:** no route. The drain loop (`spawn_telemetry`, `src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs`) emits through `MetricsEmission::round`, which takes the snapshot (`ops::collect_snapshot`), caches it for `/operator/data.json` as #159 states (landing-4 joined that cache to this commit's emission), lets `ops::evaluate_alerts` read it, and appends with `ops::append_metrics`. `ops::emit_metrics_once`, which the loop called before, is now the rigs' one-shot emission (`#[cfg(test)]`).
- **Condition:** an instance with `USAGE_STREAM_KEY` set whose `_ops_metrics` append fails: a shed write (instance memory pressure or the in-flight cap), a refused or failed relay to the ledger's owner, a store error.
- **Before:** the failed point was logged (`ops metrics emit: …`) and dropped; the next point was taken `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS` (15 s) later.
- **After:**
  - The newest refused point is kept and sent again at the next drain round (`TELEMETRY_DRAIN_SECS`, 8 s by default), alone or, when a new point is due in that round, with it in one append, oldest first. A refused batch keeps only its newest point, so a refusal loses a point only when it lasts past the next point's round (at the defaults, a refusal that lasts more than about 15 s). The log line says `the newest point is sent again next round`.
  - At most one point is ever kept, in memory: a restart drops it, as before.
  - Written appends stay one per point or fewer (a kept point and a new one share an append), inside §11.3's budget of 240 an instance-hour.
  - The alert rules read each snapshot once, when it is taken; a resend does not run them again.
  - An append whose outcome was unknown (a relay that timed out after the owner wrote it) is sent again too, so that point can be stored twice: the raw tier keys points by instance and time and keeps one, and the minute tier's counters (last wins) and gauge maxima are unchanged, but its `samples` counts the point twice.
- **Retry semantics:** Not applicable to clients. The server's own `_ops_metrics` append is now retried once a round until it lands or a newer point replaces it.
- **Who is affected:** operators and dashboards reading `_ops_metrics` or the ops rollup: points refused during a drain window (Q0: 0-2 a run) now arrive about 8 s late instead of never. Nothing a customer sees.
- **Deployment comparison:** Not applicable: no setting changes.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/billing_controller.rs::a_refused_metrics_point_is_sent_again_at_the_next_drain_round (new: with the in-flight cap saturated the drain loop's first point is shed and `_ops_metrics` holds nothing after 2 s; once the cap clears, the next round, 8 s after the first, stores exactly one point, the one taken while shed (its `ts_ms` before the clear), before the next point is due at 15 s. Red on the tree before the change: `the shed point is sent again before the next point is due: Elapsed(())`)
  - unchanged and green (dev profile): the `billing_controller` filter, whose cadence and graceful-stop tests wait for the first round's point, and `ops::`.
- **Risk reason:** low: no client-visible change; operator telemetry loses fewer points, and in the unknown-outcome case a minute's `samples` can count one point twice. No formal receipt covers `src/ops.rs` or `src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs`.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #172 627ae830 — A deploy wrapper whose binary download fails answers $PORT with the generic 500 `binary_exited` a dead binary gets, and logs the stage, object key and error only to the platform log

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, hygiene lane item 1: the Composer entry (`deploy/composer/streams/entry.ts` `refuse`) and the supervisor (`deploy/app-server/supervise.ts`) already answer the customer-reachable port with a generic body; the two wrappers' download-failure path was the one place that put deployment detail on it.
- **Surface:** process (the deploy wrapper's boot, `deploy/app-server/index.ts` and `deploy/app-gen/index.ts`); the port it answers is the service's public $PORT.
- **Endpoint:** Every request to $PORT on an instance whose wrapper could not download its binary (`downloadBinary`), its auth-feed bundle (`FEEDS_S3_KEY`, app-server) or its token map (`TOKENS_S3_KEY`, app-gen). The Composer cell entry is not affected: it never had this path.
- **Condition:** The download throws at boot (a wrong or missing key, a bucket the credential cannot read, an unreachable endpoint, a size, ELF or machine check that refuses the object).
- **Before:** `500` with `content-type: application/json` and a pretty-printed body `{"stage": "binary_download", "key": "<the S3 object key>", "error": "<the download's error text>"}`, to any caller, unauthenticated, with no `cache-control`. The same JSON went to the platform log.
- **After:** `500`, `content-type: application/json`, `cache-control: no-store`, body exactly `{"error":"binary_exited","message":"the service is not running; its exit is recorded in the platform log"}`, byte for byte what `supervise.ts` serves for a dead binary and the Composer entry for a refused boot. The log line is `binary download failed; serving the generic 500; details: {"stage":"binary_download","key":"...","error":"..."}`; the wrapper still holds the port and never exits, so the instance still reads as dead rather than as a cold start or an edge 404 (R25-G).
- **Retry semantics:** None: the instance stays unhealthy until it is redeployed, as before. Nothing retries on this body.
- **Who is affected:** Operators diagnosing a failed boot read the platform log instead of the port (no repository script, bench harness or runbook step reads the old body: `git grep binary_download`). Clients see one generic 500 shape for every boot failure; the object key and the S3 error text are no longer disclosed.
- **Pinning tests:** deploy/supervise.test.ts "a failed binary download serves the generic 500 and logs its stage, key and error" (new; runs each app's index.ts in a child Bun with `@prisma/compute` stubbed and its bucket on a closed port). Red on the unfixed tree: `expect(received).toBe(expected)`, received `{"stage": "binary_download", "key": "bin/LEAK-KEY-app-server", "error": "S3Error: an unexpected error has occurred"}`.
- **Risk reason:** low: the status is unchanged (500, as the Composer entry and the supervisor serve; not 503), only an unauthenticated failure body loses deployment detail, and it adds `cache-control: no-store` to that failure. WIRE-MATRIX lists no wrapper boot surface, so it has no entry. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (the hygiene lane's b9b8c9ef); numbered #172 at landing-5 (2026-10-18), the next free number at slate b673bb04.

### #174 7a59d754 — The SDK refuses an `issuerUrl` that is neither `https:` nor a loopback host before it sends the credential, with `CredentialExchangeError` `insecure_issuer`, unless `allowInsecureIssuer`

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, issuer triage item B8 (the internal adversarial pass over the interim issuer), finding M3 (medium): an attacker on the network path between a client and the edge (threat (d)) reads the durable credential from any exchange sent to an `http:` issuer. The SDK already refused an `http:` cell `endpoint` (`insecure_endpoint`) because every request carries the stream key; the exchange, which carries the credential itself, had no such check.
- **Surface:** SDK (`@prisma/streams`, `sdk/src/index.ts`: `issuerBase`, called by `prismaStreamsCredential` and so by `StreamsClient.connect`). No answer of the server or the issuer changes.
- **Endpoint:** `POST {issuerUrl}/v1/token/streams`, as the SDK sends it.
- **Condition:** `issuerUrl` is not a URL, or its scheme is not `https:` and it is not `http:` to `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and the caller did not pass `allowInsecureIssuer: true`.
- **Before:** the exchange was sent to whatever `issuerUrl` named, `Authorization: StreamsCredential prisma_streams_<id>.<secret>` in the clear over `http:`.
- **After:** `prismaStreamsCredential` throws, and `StreamsClient.connect` rejects with, `CredentialExchangeError` `status` 0, `code` `insecure_issuer`, `retryable` false, message "issuerUrl is neither https nor a loopback host, and the exchange would send the credential in the clear; use the issuer's https URL, or pass allowInsecureIssuer to accept it" (the URL is not echoed), before any request. `allowInsecureIssuer: true` (an option of both) sends it as before. A loopback `http:` issuer (the platform emulator, `prisma dev`) is unchanged.
- **Retry semantics:** not retryable: fix `issuerUrl` (the beta issuer is served over `https:` only).
- **Who is affected:** an app that configured an `http:` non-loopback issuer: none known (the issuer's page and `docs/AUTHENTICATING.md` give its `https:` origin; `scripts/platform-e2e.mjs` uses a loopback emulator). A development issuer on a private network (`http://issuer:8080` in Docker Compose) needs `allowInsecureIssuer: true`.
- **Pinning tests:** sdk/scripts/credential-provider.test.mjs "an issuerUrl that is neither https nor loopback is refused before the credential is sent, unless allowInsecureIssuer" (three refused URLs, no request made, from both entry points; four loopback forms exchanged; the opt-in exchanged). Red on the unfixed tree: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: the request resolved` (`connect` with `http://issuer.example` exchanged).
- **Risk reason:** low: a new refusal for a configuration that leaks the credential, with an explicit opt-in; WIRE-MATRIX §4's SDK paragraph names it. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #176 ad6a51d3, 6dc37315, 379a88c6 — Every response the server sends carries each of its `Prisma-<Name>` headers also as `Streams-<Name>` with the same values, and an expose list naming a `Prisma-<Name>` names its `Streams-<Name>`, because the Prisma Compute edge strips `Prisma-*` response headers too

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, field round 2 (FIELD-REPORT.md "Round 2"; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-19 01:00, the lead under the owner's delegation): on the scratch cell behind Composer a 200 records read carries no `Prisma-Next-Cursor`, `Prisma-Up-To-Date` or `Prisma-Sealed` (`curl -D`; round 1's "response headers pass" was wrong: the `prisma-request-id` seen then is the edge's own). SDK paging re-read page 1, `subscribe` never went live, the cell-watch canary's tail (row 19) stayed open, and the k2cost walk/tail/churn/audit and lifecycle audit were invalid. The same family as #173 (request side).
- **Surface:** both (every route of the server's router: product, raw, listing, usage, operator, health, fleet-internal and axum's own 404/405)
- **Endpoint:** every response, through the router's outermost response layer (`crate::header_alias::stamp`, called where `router` in `src/http.rs` stamped `nosniff` and the origin marker). Inventory of the `prisma-` response headers the server sets (`rg -i '"prisma-' src`): `Prisma-Next-Cursor`, `Prisma-Up-To-Date`, `Prisma-Sealed`, `Prisma-Durable-Cursor`, `Prisma-Pending-From` (product records read, long-poll, `src/product.rs`), `Prisma-Next-Scan-Cursor`, `Prisma-Scan-Complete` (`:scan`, `src/product/scan.rs`), `Prisma-Durable-Cursor` on a 409 `cursor_beyond_tail` (`src/product/read_cursor.rs`), `Prisma-Consumer-Version` (consumer create/get and the `consumer_deleting` conflict), `Prisma-Error-Code: wrong_cell` (`auth_failure_response`), and `Prisma-Streams-Origin` on every response. SSE carries its cursors in `event: control` frames (body), not headers; the raw surface's own headers are `Stream-*`. The rule is generic (`prisma-<rest>` → `streams-<rest>`, and `prisma-streams-<x>` → `streams-<x>`), so a `Prisma-` response header added later is mirrored without a table.
- **Condition:** a response carries a header whose name starts with `prisma-`, or an `access-control-expose-headers` list that names one.
- **Before:** only the `Prisma-` names were sent; the product's expose list named only them (`content-type, retry-after, prisma-next-cursor, …, prisma-consumer-version`). Behind the edge a client saw none of them.
- **After:**
  - Each `prisma-<rest>` response header is also sent as `streams-<rest>`, with the same values in the same order (a `streams-<rest>` a handler set is replaced by them); a `prisma-streams-<x>` header is sent as `streams-<x>`, the prefix once, not twice: `Streams-Next-Cursor`, `Streams-Up-To-Date`, `Streams-Sealed`, `Streams-Durable-Cursor`, `Streams-Pending-From`, `Streams-Next-Scan-Cursor`, `Streams-Scan-Complete`, `Streams-Consumer-Version`, `Streams-Error-Code`, and `Streams-Origin` for the origin marker `Prisma-Streams-Origin` (the cell-watch reads it to tell the cell's answer from the edge's).
  - An `access-control-expose-headers` list that names a `prisma-` header also names its `Streams-` name, appended once: the product's list ends `…, prisma-consumer-version, streams-next-cursor, streams-up-to-date, streams-sealed, streams-next-scan-cursor, streams-scan-complete, streams-routing-key, streams-durable-cursor, streams-pending-from, streams-consumer-version`. A list of `*` (the preflights) is unchanged.
  - Statuses, bodies and the `Prisma-` headers are unchanged.
  - Clients read the `Streams-` name first and fall back to `Prisma-`: the SDK (`@prisma/streams` 0.3.0-beta.1, and through it the lifecycle harness's probe and the platform e2e), the cell-watch canary and poll (cursor and origin marker), the k2cost walk, tail, churn and audit, and the field gate. cell-check reads no `Prisma-` response header. Local-only probes (chaos, fleet, soak, awsbench, consumer-saga-smoke) talk to servers without the edge and keep the `Prisma-` names.
- **Retry semantics:** none.
- **Who is affected:** every client behind the Composer edge, which could not page, long-poll, settle a consumer delete by version or tell a wrong cell by header; every response grows by the twin headers (about 30-60 bytes on a read, 30 + the marker on others). A client that reads only `Prisma-` names is unaffected where the edge is absent.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/header_alias.rs::product_answers_send_each_prisma_response_header_as_its_streams_name (new: create, append, read with exact records, the expose list, scan, consumer create, sealed read; every `prisma-` header has its `streams-` twin with the same value). Red on the unfixed tree: `assertion left == right failed: create: prisma-streams-origin's streams- form in {…} left: None right: Some("dst-instance")`.
  - src/dst/tests/header_alias.rs::every_surface_sends_its_prisma_response_headers_as_streams_names (new: listing, raw 404, product 404, unrouted 404). Red: `/v1/streams: prisma-streams-origin's streams- form … left: None right: Some("dst-instance")`.
  - src/header_alias/tests.rs: `every_prisma_response_header_is_sent_as_its_streams_name_with_every_value` (every value in order, a stale twin replaced, other headers untouched), `an_expose_list_naming_a_prisma_header_names_its_streams_form`, `every_response_is_stamped_with_nosniff_the_origin_and_its_streams_forms`.
  - sdk/scripts/response-header-names.test.mjs (new: a node:http fake cell that sends only `Streams-*` response headers, as the edge leaves them: paging, long-poll subscribe and its wake, a sealed subscribe ending, scan, the consumer version a delete sends, a header-only wrong cell; red on the unfixed SDK: 6 of 6 fail, e.g. `cursor: ''` where `'c2'`), and the edge-modelling fake cells of deploy/cell-watch and bench/k2cost (red: 24 of 210 fail).
- **Risk reason:** low: only headers are added, under a name space the product did not use on responses (`Streams-Replay-To` is the one `streams-` response header the server already sent, and it has no `Prisma-` form); no status, body or `Prisma-` header changes. Reversal: drop the mirror from `stamp` and the clients' `Streams-` reads. To raise with Platform: Composer strips customer `Prisma-*` response headers. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (the hdr2 lane: ad6a51d3 the server, 6dc37315 the SDK, 379a88c6 the canary, harnesses and field gate; hashes of the lane, before landing); #176 was the next free number at slate 9ba08a12.

### #182 e10ca199 — On a shared cell a records read or long-poll without `maxBytes` pages 1 MiB and reserves 1 MiB of read memory, not 8 MiB, so a burst of default reads no longer fills the instance's read memory and refuses its neighbours `503 read_memory_busy`

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, lane mem2 (the Layer B hostile phase). The owner's call "Shared cells Q1" (2026-10-08) named (B), "a 1 MiB default page on shared cells", the fallback, and his round-3 call 4 (2026-10-13) made it the fallback "if Layer B shows `read_memory_busy`" (NEXT-WORK, phase B lane, (1)). Layer B on rc.7 (layerb2-report.md) showed it for compliant tenants: `503 read_memory_busy` n0 9,910, n0-free 9,936, s1-free 4,565, victim 1,548, with the read memory at 92-124 MiB of 125 already in the compliant phase.
- **Surface:** product.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /v1/streams/{name}/records` and `GET /v1/streams/{name}/records:long-poll` without `maxBytes`, on a cell with `PROJECT_SHARE_K` > 1 (the shared-cell profile sets 8). Owner: `product::read_memory::paged_query`, called by the product entry (`product_entry_axum_inner`, `src/http.rs`), which serves such a read as if it named `maxBytes=1048576`, so the reservation (`page_bytes`) and `product_read` take it as they take a client's own `maxBytes`. Not affected: a read that gives `maxBytes` (clamped 4 KiB-8 MiB as before), `:scan` (4 MiB default), SSE, consumer pulls (4 MiB coverage), the catalog, the raw surface, and every dedicated cell (k = 1).
- **Condition:** a records read or long-poll on a shared cell gives no `maxBytes`.
- **Before:** the read reserved 8 MiB of the instance's read memory (125 MiB at the 500 MB shed line) and its project's line until its page rendered, and the page held up to 8 MiB. About 15 default reads in flight filled the read memory; under the hostile phase, with requests slowed, compliant consumer pulls and readers waited 2 s and were refused.
- **After:** the read reserves 1 MiB and its page stops adding records at 1 MiB; its first record is always returned whole, as any page's is, so a stream of records larger than 1 MiB (up to `MAX_RECORD_PAYLOAD_BYTES`) still renders one record a page, beyond the 1 MiB reserved until the page settles to its exact size, as an explicitly small `maxBytes` already did. Its cursor headers lead to the next page as any page's do. A woken long-poll takes at most 1 MiB again. About 125 default reads fit the read memory at once.
- **Retry semantics:** none new; a client that wants larger pages sends `maxBytes` (up to 8 MiB).
- **Who is affected:** clients of a shared cell that read a backlog of more than 1 MiB without `maxBytes` (every SDK read): they make up to 8 times more requests for it, each charged to the project's request bucket, so a large catch-up takes longer under a low `requests_per_sec` (the free tier's 10/s reads 10 MiB/s with default pages). Readers that keep up (pages under 1 MiB) see no difference.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/read_memory_wakes.rs::a_shared_cells_default_page_reserves_one_mib_and_renders_at_most_that (new: a k = 8 cell, a 3 MiB stream whose whole page a never-reading client holds (larger than the 1.7 MB a Linux loopback send buffer takes, so it stays held on Linux and macOS), a read memory with 1 MiB 4 KiB of room beside it; a default read answers 200 with 14-47 records, at most 1 MiB, and leaves the ledgers at the held page). Red on the unfixed tree: `assertion left == right failed ... left: (503, false) right: (200, true)`. Its first form held a ~1 MiB default page from a never-reading client, which Linux's loopback autotuning takes whole, so the hold ended and the leg failed on Linux only (the trap a680bc77 records for read_memory_wakes).
  - The dedicated-cell legs of src/dst/tests/read_memory.rs (k = 1, 8 MiB `PAGE_BUDGET`, the 3 MiB stream in one page) pass unchanged.
- **Risk reason:** low: no new refusal; pages are smaller and the cursor contract is unchanged. Request count for large catch-ups grows. Reversal: `paged_query` returns the query as sent. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (lane mem2, before landing); the number is assigned at landing.

### #183 ac81f269 — Over the RSS shed line a records append is refused 429 `rate_limited` before its body is buffered, its stream looked up or its volume charged: the body is read and dropped, so a shed no longer holds the body it refuses and the client reads the 429 on a connection that stays open

- **Program item:** public-beta week of 2026-10-17, lane mem2 (the Layer B hostile phase; the lead's ask "a shed should not buffer the body"). In Layer B on rc.7 the instance shed 2,748,790 appends over 40 minutes; each was buffered whole (up to `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES`, 8 MiB on a shared cell, under its project's memory line), its descriptor read, its body parsed and its project's append volume debited before the RSS gate refused it. Amended after the lane's review (M1): a first build answered without reading the body, so a client still uploading met a reset instead of the 429, which the SDK reports as `AppendOutcomeUnknownError`.
- **Surface:** product.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /v1/streams/{name}/records` and `POST /v1/streams/{name}/records:batch`. Owners: `product::read_memory::body` (the product entry's body step), `admission::body::discard_within` (the read-and-drop), `application::append::memory_gate` (the gate, shared with `AppendService::check_memory`). Not affected: `:seal` with a final record, creates, deletes, consumer routes, the raw surface (its own order) and every read.
- **Condition:** the sampled RSS plus the absorber's reserved bytes is over `ADMIT_RSS_SHED_MB` (500 on the beta profiles) when an authenticated append has passed project admission, its project's memory gate and the reserved-name guard, as its body is about to be buffered.
- **Before:** the body was read and buffered whole, the descriptor read, the body checked (400s, 413s), the volume quota debited, then the gate answered 429 `rate_limited` (`Retry-After: 2`, after a 25 ms tarpit). A missing stream answered 404 and a bad body 400 even over the line.
- **After:** the same 429 `rate_limited` (`Retry-After: 2`, 25 ms tarpit, the same body) is answered before any of that: the body is read and dropped a frame at a time (never buffered), up to `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` or 2 s, whichever comes first; no descriptor is read and nothing is charged. Over the line a missing stream, a bad body, an over-capacity body and a project over its volume quota get this 429 instead of their own answers. A body that ends inside both bounds leaves the connection open for the next request; a longer or slower one is given up and the connection closes after the answer. Below the line nothing changes; the append path's own gate still refuses an append whose RSS crosses the line while it runs.
- **Retry semantics:** unchanged: retryable after 2 s; the append was not written.
- **Who is affected:** appending clients while an instance is over its shed line (already refused): the answer can now take up to 2 s more while their body arrives. The volume quota is no longer spent on refused appends. A client whose body takes longer than 2 s to send may still see the connection close after the 429.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/shared_cell_hostile.rs::an_append_over_the_shed_line_is_refused_before_its_body_is_read (a shed line of 500 MiB and an RSS of 501: a head declaring 4 MiB with no body is answered `429`, `retry-after: 2`, `rate_limited`; a client uploading 1 MiB reads the same 429, finishes its upload and its next append on the same connection is served 200 under the line; a read is served over the line). Red on the unfixed tree: `Err(Elapsed(()))` (no answer: the server waited for the body); red on the first build (no read-and-drop): `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Os { code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe }` (the upload met a closed connection).
  - src/admission/body/tests.rs::a_discarded_body_ends_inside_its_bounds_or_is_given_up.
  - src/dst/tests/append_application.rs::a_raw_append_over_the_shed_line_is_refused_by_the_append_paths_gate (the append path keeps its own gate).
- **Risk reason:** low: the refusal and its retry are unchanged; only its precedence and its cost change. Reversal: drop the `appends` branch in `product::read_memory::body`. Status: ratified at landing by the lead under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-17.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change (lane mem2, before landing); the number is assigned at landing.

### #186 (this record's commit) — Native queues are served under `/v1/queues` for the default group, and every stream-surface request that names a queue's stream is refused 409 `queue_via_queue_routes`

- **Program item:** native queues, package Q2 (docs/QUEUES-PLAN.md §1; docs/QUEUES-DESIGN.md §4, §6, §7, §9.2, §11), on the `queues-dev` engine (091e8b93). The wire contract is the first release's HTTP contract the server, SDK and benchmark rig implement together (2026-10-23), with the coordinator's resolutions of the same day (a `max` above `maxBatch` is capped; `release` carries no `notStarted`; `bodyBase64` in standard or URL-safe base64, padded or not; republish requires the key; the wake-up secret is `HMAC-SHA256(root, "queue-wakeup/v1" ‖ storage hash ‖ version_be)`, returned base64url without padding).
- **Surface:** product and raw.
- **Endpoint:** new: `GET /v1/queues`; `PUT|GET|PATCH|DELETE /v1/queues/{name}`; `POST /v1/queues/{name}:cancel`, `:republish`; `POST /v1/queues/{name}/messages`, `messages:batch`; `GET /v1/queues/{name}/messages/{id}`; `POST /v1/queues/{name}/groups/default:claim`, `:settle`, `:pause`, `:resume`, `:redrive`, `:discard`; `GET /v1/queues/{name}/groups/default/failed`, `/pending`; `PUT|DELETE /v1/queues/{name}/groups/default/wakeup`. Changed: every `/v1/streams/{name}...` route and raw `/v1/stream/{name}` (GET, HEAD, PUT, POST, DELETE) whose stream is a live queue, and a raw fork (`Stream-Forked-From`) whose source is one. Owners: `application::queues` (workflows), `product::queues` (routes, `guard`), the committer's `NqOp` operations (`shard::transaction::native_queue`), `CreationService::create_product` (the queue's stream, of content type `application/vnd.prisma.queue+json`, the persisted queue kind).
- **Condition:** a queue exists from a `PUT /v1/queues/{name}` with the stream key. The queue routes authenticate, admit and resolve tenancy as `/v1/streams` (enforce: the customer token, its scopes and stream grant; off and shadow: the deployment bearer). Scopes: create `streams.create`; delete `streams.lifecycle.manage`; GET `streams.metadata.read`; list `streams.catalog.read`; send `streams.records.append`; claim, settle, pause, resume, redrive, discard, cancel, republish, PATCH, the failed and pending views, one message and the wake-up subscription `streams.records.read` and `streams.records.append`.
- **Before:** `/v1/queues` answered 404 from the router (no route). A queue stream did not exist.
- **After:** the routes answer as the contract specifies, errors in the product shape `{error: {code, message, retryable}}`: `400 invalid_config|invalid_message|invalid_settle|invalid_body|deliver_at_beyond_retention|immutable_field|invalid_cursor|invalid_wakeup_url|missing_key|invalid_key`, `403 wrong_key`, `404 queue_not_found|message_not_found|reclaimed|group_not_found|unknown_route`, `409 queue_config_conflict|queue_deleting`, `413 message_too_large|too_large`, `429 queue_full|dedup_full` (retryable), `503 queue_unavailable|claim_read_failed` (retryable) and `503 wakeup_unavailable` (not retryable; a deployment without `STREAMS_CURSOR_KEY`). A queue's stream answers 409 `queue_via_queue_routes` (not retryable) on every `/v1/streams/{name}` route except the self-authorizing watch wait after authentication and admission (before the body is read); the watch wait reads its descriptor only through the watch lookup budget (phase B step 15), so the guard leaves it to that read, and a queue feeds no watch journal and on the raw surface for the deployment credential; a raw fork of it answers the same code. A `PUT /v1/queues/{name}` over a stream of another kind answers 409 `queue_config_conflict`; `GET /v1/queues/{name}` of one answers 404 `queue_not_found`. The stream-surface guard is that request's first descriptor read (cached for the handler): a store failure on it answers #64's answer, 503 `temporarily_unavailable`, retryable, `Retry-After: 1` (a corrupt descriptor 500 `internal`, not retryable), on every `/v1/streams/{name}` route, including the routes whose handler answered a store failure otherwise (create: 500 `internal`, retryable; consumer routes: 500 `internal`, retryable). The raw guard lets a failed read through to the raw handler, which reads again and answers as before.
- **Retry semantics:** `queue_full`, `dedup_full`, `queue_unavailable`, `claim_read_failed` (every lease of that claim released with its attempt given back) and the shared admission and ownership answers are retryable; `queue_via_queue_routes`, `queue_deleting` and `queue_config_conflict` are permanent. A send is atomic (a batch is all or nothing); a duplicate `dedupKey` within the window answers 200 with the original id. A settle with a foreign or garbage token answers that op `stale`, never 400.
- **Who is affected:** queue clients (the SDK's queue API, the benchmark rig); a client that names a queue's stream on the stream surfaces. No existing stream changes: the queue kind is a content type no product create offers by default.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/queue_product.rs: `a_sent_message_is_claimed_decrypted_and_acked`, `bytes_come_back_as_padded_base64_and_the_list_names_the_queue`, `retry_and_an_expired_lease_redeliver_with_the_next_attempt`, `dedup_answers_the_original_and_refusals_are_exact`, `a_failed_message_is_listed_and_redriven`, `peek_cancel_republish_and_discard_act_on_the_named_messages`, `pause_holds_claims_and_a_parked_claim_takes_a_late_message`, `a_deleted_queue_is_fenced_then_gone_without_rows`, `queue_streams_are_refused_on_the_stream_surfaces` (red on the unfixed tree: every `PUT /v1/queues/...` answered 404 from the router, e.g. `left: (404, Null, Null) right: (201, String("jobs"), Number(5))`); src/dst/tests/product_descriptor_reads.rs (the #64 answer, now given by the guard's read); src/application/queues/admin.rs::tests (the wake-up secret's derivation, the URL rule).
- **Departures from the contract and design, for the owner:** `stats.scheduled`, `oldestDueAgeMs` and `nextAvailableAt` are null and `due` counts undone messages neither leased nor retrying (scheduled ones included), because the state row keeps no availability summary; settle `error` text is accepted (at most 1 KiB) and not stored; a deleting queue's cleanup runs as request maintenance (10 s per job) and resumes on the next GET or DELETE of the queue, not from the sweep; claims hold no read-memory reservation and queue routes meter no read bytes or operations yet; the queue kind is the descriptor's content type rather than a new descriptor field (a field grows `PersistedDescriptor`'s exception contract, an owner decision).
- **Risk reason:** low for existing clients: only requests naming a queue's stream change, and queues are new. Reversal: drop the `routes()` merge and the two guards.
- **Status:** awaiting the owner's ratification.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #187 (this record's commit) — An instance stores one `_ops_metrics` point a minute instead of one every 15 s, and the alert rules keep their 15 s cadence on a snapshot of their own that `/operator/data.json` serves

- **Program item:** the streams cost report of 2026-10-24 (Fable 5.1): section 6 lever 5 (E9-B1), section 7 item 3, section 8 decision 3, option (a) "60 s with alerts on their own 15 s tick", its recommendation. The spec (OBSERVABILITY-BILLING §11.2, §13.1, §17.1, §17.2) said 15 s; this commit changes it to 60 s. Numbered #187, the next free number at slate 2e0d1b86.
- **Surface:** operator-debug: the `_ops_metrics` ledger and what the ops rollup takes from it (its raw tier and minute tier), and `ops` on `GET /operator/data.json`. No customer route, status, header or body changes, and no usage answer changes.
- **Endpoint:** no route for the ledger; `GET /operator/data.json` (`operator::data`, the `ops` key of #159). The drain loop's emission `MetricsEmission` (`src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs`): `due` decides what a round takes a snapshot for (a point every `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS`, else the alert rules every `ALERT_EVALUATION_INTERVAL`, 15 s), `take` collects it and carries the peaks, `round` caches it, runs `ops::evaluate_alerts` and appends points with `ops::append_metrics`; `OpsSnapshot::carry_peaks` (`src/ops.rs`); the default of `BillingConfig::metrics_interval_secs` (`src/config/model.rs`).
- **Condition:** an instance with `USAGE_STREAM_KEY` set whose `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS` is unset (no profile or deploy script in the repository sets it).
- **Before:** a point every `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS` = 15 s, at the first 8 s drain round that reached it: every 16 s, 225 an instance-hour. On an idle cell each point is an append, so a WAL object, an L0 flush, a manifest write and compaction: about 1,300 Class A and 5,000 Class B requests an hour, $3.5 of a shared cell's $14.8 monthly floor (cost report §5.3). The alert rules ran on each point (every 16 s). `ops` was the last point, at most 16 s old.
- **After:**
  - A point every 60 s, at the first drain round that reaches it: every 64 s at the default 8 s cadence, 56.25 an instance-hour (OBSERVABILITY-BILLING §17.2's budget lowered from 240 to 60). The minute tier holds one sample a minute instead of three or four, and about one minute in 16 none (points 64 s apart); its gauge maxima still cover every peak (below).
  - The alert rules still run every 15 s, at the first round that reaches it (every 16 s at the defaults): on each point, and between points on a snapshot collected for them alone. That snapshot is cached for `/operator/data.json` exactly as a point is, so `ops` is still at most 16 s old (inside the cell watch's 60 s `r20_snapshot_stale` line), and it is not stored, so `ops` may be a snapshot `_ops_metrics` does not hold.
  - A collection drains the two peak-since-scrape gauges (`rss_peak_since_scrape_mb`, `history_flush_wait_ms_max`). Each later snapshot takes the larger of its own and the unstored one's, so every stored point carries every peak since the previous stored point, as before; between points `ops` carries the peaks since the last stored point.
  - A deployment that sets `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS` keeps that point cadence; the rules run on every point and at least every 15 s whatever it says. The resend of a refused point (#164) is unchanged: a resend runs no rules, and a kept point and a new one share an append. The boot log's effective configuration prints `"metrics_interval_secs":60`.
- **Retry semantics:** Not applicable to clients.
- **Who is affected:** operators and dashboards reading `_ops_metrics` or the ops rollup: a quarter of the points, at minute resolution. Alert latency and the operator surface's freshness are unchanged. Nothing a customer sees.
- **Deployment comparison:** `METRICS_INTERVAL_SECS=15` restores the old point cadence; nothing else changes with it.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - src/dst/tests/runtime_journals.rs::an_idle_server_stores_one_ops_metrics_point_a_minute (paused clock, the drain loop on the HTTP rig at the defaults, ten idle minutes: exactly 10 points; from 10 s to 600 s at most 30 WAL PUTs and 160 PUTs in all, measured 22 and 116, against 78 and 340 at 15 s). Red on the unfixed tree: `assertion left == right failed: ten idle minutes store one point a minute (0 s, 64 s, ... 576 s), not one every 16 s; left: 38, right: 10`.
  - src/dst/tests/runtime_journals.rs::alerts_run_every_16_s_between_minute_points (an ops event dropped at the queue cap after the 16 s round opens `ops_event_drops` at the 32 s round and not at 24 s; the cached snapshot carries the drop and both drained gauges; `_ops_metrics` holds only the first point until the 64 s point, which carries the drop). Red on the unfixed tree: `and not stored; left: [0, 0, 1], right: [0]`. Control: the default alone moved to 60 s fails it with `the drop opens its alert at the 32 s round`.
  - src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs::emission_tests::default_rounds_take_a_point_a_minute_and_run_the_alerts_every_16_s (ten minutes of 8 s rounds: points at 0, 64, ... 576 s; the rules every 16 s, 38 times) and ::the_next_point_carries_the_peaks_the_alert_snapshots_drained; src/dst/tests/runtime_journals.rs::carry_peaks_raises_only_the_drained_peak_gauges; src/config/tests.rs pins the default at 60.
  - unchanged and green (dev profile): the `billing_controller` filter (its refused-point, cadence and graceful-stop tests wait for the first round's point), `runtime_journals`, `ops::`.
- **Risk reason:** low: operator telemetry only; the metric resolution drops to a minute, alert latency and the operator surface's freshness are kept, and the peaks are not lost. No formal receipt digests `src/ops.rs`, `src/billing/telemetry_loop.rs` or `src/config/model.rs`.
- **Status:** awaiting the owner's decision (cost report decision 3) and ratification.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #200 (this record's commit) — One `POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait` long-poll waits on every tail, consumer-group pull and watch a client names, and answers whichever is ready with exactly what the per-stream routes would deliver

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 2 (DESIGN-6A §5, research-density §1, REVIEW-6A F15): multiplexed waits, the density lever for small tenants. A small (S) tenant holds 25 waits (20 tails, 5 group pulls), so a launch cell is connection-bound at about 48 S (the live pool of 1,200, the edge's ~1,300 usable sockets); one multiplexed wait per client makes it one. Long-poll, not SSE: SSE does not pass Compute ingress (PRO-218).
- **Surface:** product.
- **Endpoint:** new: `POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait` (+ `OPTIONS` preflight). Owner: `product::live_wait` (route, admission, the wait, the answer) with `tail`, `group`, `watch`, `wire`; `WatchService::observe` (the watch wait without its own admission, `application::watch`); `LineageWatch` (`application::consumer::pull_wait`). WIRE-MATRIX §2.24.
- **Condition:** a request with a JSON body `{waitMs?, maxBytes?, subs}` (1-256 subscriptions of kind `tail`, `group` or `watch`, each with the stream key), authenticated as every product route (enforce: the customer token; off/shadow: the deployment bearer), naming its own project in the path.
- **Before:** 404 (no route); a client waited with one long-poll per stream: `GET …/records:long-poll`, `POST …/consumers/{c}:pull` with `waitMs`, `GET …/watches/{w}/keys/{k}`.
- **After:** 200 `{"results": [...]}` as soon as any subscription is ready (records past a tail's cursor, a group walk that leases, a watch touched; at once for a cursor from `now`, which the entry pins), or at `waitMs` (≤ 25 s) with nothing (`[]`, plus each watch's current cursor). Entries in request order: tail `{id, records, cursor, upToDate, sealed}`, group `{id, backlog, messages}`, watch `{id, event}`, refusal `{id, status, error}` with exactly the status and `error` the per-stream route gives the same token (e.g. 403 `prefix_denied` for a stream outside its grant, 403 `missing_scope`, 403 `wrong_key`, 404 `not_found`, `consumer_not_found`), never failing the rest; 421 `not_owner` (retryable) for a stream this instance does not serve, 400 `deliver_unsupported` for `deliver: applied`, 400 `unsupported_format` for a tail on a non-JSON stream. Whole-request answers: 400 `invalid_body`; 401; 404 `unknown_project` (path names another project, journaled); 413 `too_large` (body over 256 KiB); 429 `live_subscription_limit` (> 256 subscriptions, not retryable; or #202's project share, retryable); 503 `subscription_capacity` (#202); and the page routes' admission answers (429 `project_concurrency_limit`, `project_memory_pressure`, `rate_limited`, the read-debt 429, 503 `read_memory_busy`). Tails share `maxBytes` (default 256 KiB, [4 KiB, 1 MiB]) evenly; a tail past its share answers `upToDate: false`. Group leases start when the answer is built; a lost answer's leases expire after their visibility window and are delivered again (at-least-once, as a lost pull answer). A group walk reserves read memory for the records past its consumer's cursor at their segments' mean payload (+64 B each, +4 KiB), at most one whole coverage (4 MiB); a drained group (its cursor at every segment's tail) is not walked at all.
- **Retry semantics:** the client keeps every cursor; a request lost in transport is sent again with the same cursors (no state on the server). Retryable: 429/503 admission answers, `not_owner`, `live_subscription_limit` from the share; permanent: 400s, 404 `unknown_project`, > 256 subscriptions, the per-subscription refusals the per-stream routes call permanent.
- **Who is affected:** clients that adopt the route (the SDK by default, #203; the K2 rig's `mux` mode). The per-stream routes are unchanged.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/live_wait.rs: `subscriptions_from_now_are_answered_at_once_with_pinned_cursors`, `an_append_wakes_exactly_its_tail_and_an_idle_wait_answers_empty_at_its_deadline` (red on 63139112 without the route: `left: 404 right: 200`), `ready_tails_are_answered_in_request_order_within_one_shared_budget`, `every_subscription_is_held_to_the_tokens_grants_and_answered_its_own_refusal`, `a_drained_group_waits_without_walking_and_an_append_wakes_it_leased`, `an_unsettled_lease_is_redelivered_through_the_wait_at_its_deadline`, `a_woken_group_reserves_what_was_appended_not_a_whole_coverage`, `a_watch_pins_its_cursor_and_a_matching_append_invalidates_it`, `a_retired_engine_answers_its_wait_retryably_and_the_replay_gets_the_next_record`, `a_tail_waiting_through_a_splits_seal_window_follows_it_to_the_first_record_after`, `a_wait_reserves_its_answer_and_is_refused_when_read_memory_is_held`, `a_woken_group_waits_for_room_for_what_was_appended`, `a_tail_polling_through_a_seal_window_releases_its_reservation_between_polls`, `a_wait_waiting_for_read_memory_on_its_first_walk_waits_parked`, `a_group_with_a_small_backlog_reserves_its_backlog_not_a_whole_coverage`; `product::live_wait::wire::tests`.
- **Risk reason:** medium: a new route sharing the per-stream operations (`execute_read`, `consumer::pull`, the touch journal), not new storage paths; nothing in `src/shard.rs` changes. The group drained probe skips a walk only when the segments' loaded queue state shows nothing past the cursor unsettled (a consumer the state does not hold reads as cursor 0). Reversal: drop the route merge.
- **Status:** awaiting the owner's ratification.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #201 (this record's commit) — A multiplexed wait's answer meters one read operation however many streams it answers, and an empty one meters one

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 2 (research-density §4 row 2).
- **Surface:** usage and billing: `readOperations` per stream (`/v1/streams/{name}/usage`, `/v1/projects/{p}/usage`).
- **Endpoint:** `POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait` (#200); `product::live_wait::Serve::render`.
- **Condition:** a multiplexed wait answers.
- **Before:** each per-stream long-poll answer, empty (204) or not, meters one read operation on its stream, and its records and payload bytes.
- **After:** one read operation per answer, on the stream of the first answered tail in request order (no tail answered: the first tail subscription's stream; no tail subscription: none); every answered tail meters its records and payload bytes on its own stream without an operation; each non-empty group batch meters one queue operation with its records and bytes (as `:pull`); watches meter nothing (as the watch wait). An empty answer meters one read operation (as today's 204). The body's length is debited from the project's read-byte bucket. A stream's `readOperations` is therefore an allocation of the project's, not a count of its own answers; the project total is exact.
- **Retry semantics:** not applicable.
- **Who is affected:** clients of #200: fewer read operations (an S tenant's ~2.2 tail answers a second become one operation per multiplexed answer); per-stream `readOperations` of multiplexed streams move to the first-named stream.
- **Owner option:** not metering the empty answer (one operation per 25 s per idle client) is the T profile's metering lever (PLAN (g) 8); this record keeps it.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/live_wait.rs::one_answer_meters_one_read_operation_and_each_streams_bytes (three tails, two answered: `[(0,0,0), (1,1,a), (0,2,b+c)]`; an empty answer: one operation on the first tail's stream).
- **Risk reason:** low: billing rows keep their shape; the per-op price is unchanged.
- **Status:** awaiting the owner's ratification.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #202 (this record's commit) — A multiplexed wait holds one live-pool place and one project live place however many streams it watches, and one subscription unit per stream from a budget sized under the RSS shed line

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 2 (research-density §1.3, §4 row 4; REVIEW-6A F15's memory line).
- **Surface:** quotas and admission: the live pool (`SSE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`), the project's live share (`max_live_subscriptions`), a new subscription-unit budget.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait` (#200); `admission::live_units`.
- **Condition:** a multiplexed wait waits (parks) / is admitted.
- **Before:** each waiting long-poll, pull or watch held one pool place and one project place.
- **After:** a multiplexed wait is parked from its start: one pool place and one project place for all its subscriptions (when the pool or share is full it waits as an active request, as every wait). Each subscription takes one unit for the request's lifetime from the instance's budget, `RSS_SHED_MB` MiB / 16 in 4 KiB units (8,000 at the 500 MB line: 31.25 MiB beside read memory's quarter, the F15 budget line; unbounded with no shed line), and from its project's share of it, the budget / `PROJECT_SHARE_K` (1,000 at k = 8; the whole budget at k = 1). Over the share: 429 `live_subscription_limit`, `retry-after: 1`; over the budget: 503 `subscription_capacity`, `retry-after: 5`. The route counts as data plane for the pre-auth survival bound and the idle release.
- **Retry semantics:** both refusals retryable; units free as requests end.
- **Who is affected:** multiplexed clients; the pool and shares now bind on connections, not streams.
- **Pinning tests:** src/dst/tests/live_wait.rs::a_wait_on_twenty_streams_parks_once_and_too_many_subscriptions_are_refused (20 streams, `parked() == 1`); src/admission/live_units.rs tests (`8,000` at 500 MB; share and budget refusals, release on drop); src/product/live_wait.rs::tests (the data-plane path).
- **Risk reason:** low-medium: the 4 KiB a unit is a budget against ~2 KiB measured per watched stream (E11 on Linux decides the density claim).
- **Status:** awaiting the owner's ratification.
- **Check against commit:** written with the change.

### #203 (this record's commit) — The SDK waits through one multiplexed long-poll per client for every `subscribe()` tail past its catch-up, consumer iterator and watch subscription, and per stream on a cell without it

- **Program item:** layout 6A package 2 (DESIGN-6A §5: one multiplexer per client and project token, used by default).
- **Surface:** SDK (`@prisma/streams`).
- **Endpoint:** `Stream.subscribe()` (durable tails, after the catch-up reads), `Consumer.messages()`, `Watch.subscribe()`; `sdk/src/live_mux.ts`; option `liveMux` on `StreamsClientOptions` and `ConnectOptions` (default `true`).
- **Condition:** a client with a `project` and a token (`connect()` always has both).
- **Before:** one long-poll (or pull) per subscription, each its own connection.
- **After:** the client's subscriptions wait through `POST /v1/projects/{project}/live:wait` (#200), one request at a time; a subscription takes part only while its iterator waits for its next answer.
